skills.name: git-advanced-workflows
skills.description: Git beyond add/commit: fixup/autosquash interactive rebase, stacked branches with update-refs, conflict prediction and resolution (zdiff3, rerere, merge-tree), worktrees for parallel tasks, cherry-pick backports, reflog recovery, pickaxe/line-log archaeology, safe force-push and history rewriting; load when rebasing, untangling history, resolving conflicts, running parallel worktrees or recovering lost work.
outline: Per-repo config baseline (never silently rewrite a user's global config): merge.conflictStyle=zdiff3, rerere.enabled=true, rebase.autoSquash=true, rebase.updateRefs=true, rebase.autoStash=true, push.autoSetupRemote=true, fetch.prune=true, diff.algorithm=histogram, blame.ignoreRevsFile=.git-blame-ignore-revs.

Clean-history procedure: git commit --fixup=<sha> (or --fixup=amend:/reword:), git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main, then git rebase -x '<fast test cmd>' origin/main so every commit builds and passes; compare before/after with git range-diff @{u}...HEAD and attach it to the PR.

Stacked branches: one rebase moves the whole stack via --update-refs; git rebase --onto <new-base> <old-base> <branch> to transplant; push with --force-with-lease --force-if-includes; decision table own branch / shared branch / protected branch for when force-push is allowed (never on shared).

Conflict playbook: predict with git merge-tree --write-tree main feature before merging; read the zdiff3 base hunk; git log --merge -p <path> to see both sides' commits; git checkout --ours/--theirs -- <path> for whole-file picks; lockfiles and generated files: take one side then regenerate (uv lock, pnpm install, go mod tidy), never hand-merge; rerun tests before rebase --continue.

Worktrees for parallel agent tasks: git worktree add -b task-x ../repo-task-x origin/main, one branch per worktree, separate venv/node_modules/build dirs, git worktree list|remove|prune; pitfalls: a branch cannot be checked out in two worktrees, untracked config (.env) is not copied, stash and refs are shared.

Archaeology: git log -S'symbol' -p (pickaxe on occurrence count), -G'regex', git log -L :func:path (function history), git blame -w -C -C -C with ignore-revs, git log --first-parent main for the merged-PR view, git show :/message; bisection stays in debugging-method (link, do not copy).

Recovery matrix: uncommitted change lost (git fsck --lost-found, editor history), bad last commit (git commit --amend / git reset --soft HEAD~1), pushed bad commit (git revert), bad merge (git revert -m 1), deleted branch or botched rebase (git reflog, then git branch rescue <sha>); always create a rescue branch before risky operations.

Backports: git cherry-pick -x <sha> (records origin), ranges A^..B, git cherry -v release main to list unported commits, resolve with the same conflict playbook, label backport PRs with the original SHA.

History rewriting and big repos: git filter-repo --invert-paths --path secrets.env or --replace-text (rotate the secret first; rewriting does not un-leak it; coordinate re-clones); split a commit with edit + git reset -p HEAD^; partial clone --filter=blob:none, sparse-checkout cone mode, git maintenance start.

Pitfalls: rebasing published history, plain --force, git add -A committing build output or secrets, git stash without -u losing untracked files, commits made on detached HEAD (recover via reflog), resolving lockfile conflicts by hand, mixing formatting and logic in one commit.

Worked example: 14-commit messy feature branch reduced to 4 reviewable commits with fixups+autosquash; conflict in pyproject.toml and uv.lock against main resolved by taking main's lock and running uv lock; every commit verified with rebase -x 'uv run pytest -q -x'; range-diff pasted into the PR.

skills.name: refactoring-playbook
skills.description: Behaviour-preserving refactoring procedure: safety net first (characterization, approval and differential tests), a smell-to-refactoring decision table with micro-step mechanics, legacy-code seams, parallel change, branch by abstraction, strangler fig and Mikado graphs for large changes, and commit discipline; load when restructuring code without changing behaviour or executing items from a code-quality refactor list.
outline: Split source: code-quality-metrics section 5 keeps measuring and ranking targets; this skill owns executing them (that section gets a one-line pointer). Entry gate: behaviour to preserve stated in one sentence, all callers found with rg, branch coverage of the target measured; below ~70% write characterization tests first.

Characterization and approval tests: record real inputs (production samples, fixtures, logs) and snapshot outputs with syrupy/inline-snapshot (Python), insta (Rust), Vitest/Jest snapshots, ApprovalTests (JVM/.NET); keep snapshots deterministic (sorted keys, fixed clock); this is the oracle for the whole refactor.

Smell -> refactoring decision table: long function -> Extract Function / Split Phase; flag params -> separate functions or enum; repeated type switches -> Replace Conditional with Polymorphism or table-driven dispatch; long parameter list -> Introduce Parameter Object; feature envy -> Move Function; data clumps -> Extract Class; LCOM4 >= 2 -> split class along components; duplication -> extract after the rule of three; primitive obsession -> value type/NewType/branded type; deep nesting -> guard clauses.

Mechanics as numbered micro-steps (compile and test after each) for the six most-used refactorings: Extract Function, Inline, Rename (LSP/IDE rename, never text replace), Change Signature with a deprecated shim, Move Function/Module (git mv in its own commit), Split Phase.

Legacy seams (Feathers): sprout method/class, wrap method, extract interface, parameterize constructor, subclass-and-override for tests; break hidden dependencies on globals, singletons, clock, randomness and I/O by injection before changing logic.

Large refactors: parallel change (expand/migrate/contract) for APIs, branch by abstraction to swap implementations behind an interface, strangler fig at route/module level, feature flag at cutover, Mikado method graph (attempt goal, record prerequisites, revert, solve leaves first).

Commit discipline: refactor commits separate from behaviour changes and from formatting (formatting SHA added to .git-blame-ignore-revs); every commit green (git rebase -x); PR states 'no behaviour change' and how it was proven; > ~30 mechanical sites -> hand off to codemod-automation.

Verification: same suite green before/after; differential run old vs new on the recorded inputs (byte-identical or every diff explained); mutation testing on touched code (testing-strategy); re-run the code-quality-metrics commands for the before/after table; benchmark when the hot path changed (dynamic dispatch, allocations).

Pitfalls: refactoring and bug-fixing in one commit; silently 'fixing' behaviour that tests pin (record it as an Open doubt instead); unintended public API changes in a library (semver major); speculative generality; splitting functions to game CCN while they share mutable state; losing blame history through copy-delete moves.

Worked example: billing compute_totals (CCN 47, cognitive 88, 42% branch coverage): golden master over 500 recorded invoices, Split Phase (parse -> compute -> round), table-driven tax rules replacing a type switch, Introduce Parameter Object for 7 params; 9 commits each green; max CCN 12, outputs identical on all 500 invoices.

skills.name: codemod-automation
skills.description: Large-scale automated code rewrites with syntax-aware tools (ast-grep, comby, semgrep autofix, OpenRewrite, jscodeshift/ts-morph, LibCST, gofmt -r/gopls/go fix, rust-analyzer SSR, Coccinelle, clang-tidy, ruff/eslint/clippy fixers): tool choice, rule writing and testing, dry runs, batched application, verification and reintroduction guards; load when the same change must be applied at dozens to thousands of sites (API migrations, deprecations, renames).
outline: When to automate: > ~30 sites or the same change across repos; below that use LSP rename or hand edits; never sed over source except for unique literal tokens (it hits strings/comments and misses multi-line forms).

Tool choice table by language and change shape: ast-grep (tree-sitter patterns with $VAR/$$$ARGS metavariables, YAML rules with inside/has/not constraints and fix), comby (structural, any delimiter-balanced language), semgrep --autofix, OpenRewrite recipes (Java/Kotlin/Gradle/Maven: Spring Boot, JUnit 4->5, JDK upgrades), jscodeshift or ts-morph (TS with type info), LibCST codemods (Python, formatting-preserving), gofmt -r / gopls rename / go fix modernizers, rust-analyzer SSR, Coccinelle (C), clang-tidy --fix, linter fixers (ruff --fix [--unsafe-fixes], eslint --fix, pyupgrade, cargo clippy --fix).

Procedure: (1) inventory with counts (rg -c, sg run -p ... --json | jq length) and categorize variants; (2) write the rule against 3-5 real samples; (3) test it with fixtures (sg test valid/invalid cases, OpenRewrite RewriteTest); (4) dry run -> diff + diffstat; (5) apply in batches per package; (6) format, compile/type-check and test per batch; (7) list residual non-matching sites for manual work.

ast-grep crib: sg run -p 'foo($A, $B)' -r 'bar($B, $A)' -l ts src/ (-i interactive, -U apply all), sg scan -r rules/x.yml, rule YAML skeleton (id, language, rule, constraints, fix), sg new rule, rules committed under tools/codemods/ for reuse by downstream consumers.

Import and symbol hygiene in the same transformation: LibCST AddImportsVisitor/RemoveImportsVisitor, ts-morph addImportDeclaration + organize imports, ast-grep rule followed by ruff --select I --fix or eslint import fixers; check shadowed names and keep annotations valid.

Scaling out: shard by package for parallel workers (one swarm-run brief per shard carrying the tested rule file), one mechanical commit per shard plus a separate manual-fix commit; keep generated, vendored and fixture files excluded.

Verification: compiler/type checker as primary oracle, then tests; diffstat sanity (expected file count), spot-review 10 random hunks, zero remaining old-pattern occurrences, and a CI guard (sg scan or semgrep rule, or a lint rule) that blocks reintroduction.
LLM-assisted edits only for the residual tail, each hunk reviewed; deterministic rules for the bulk so the diff is reproducible and re-runnable after rebases.

Pitfalls: formatting churn (run the project formatter after), macros/templates/reflection/dynamic dispatch invisible to syntax tools, edge variants (keyword args, spreads, optional chaining, aliased imports), partially migrated codebases mixing old and new API, rewriting generated code that will be regenerated.

Worked example: replace deprecated datetime.utcnow() with datetime.now(UTC) in a 900-file Python repo: ruff check --select DTZ003 --statistics finds 214 sites; ast-grep rule rewrites the call and adds 'from datetime import UTC' (UP017 style); sg test fixtures cover aliased imports; 6 batches each mypy + pytest green; ruff DTZ003 enabled in CI; 3 sites comparing naive datetimes fixed manually in a separate commit.

skills.name: api-contract-design
skills.description: Designing and evolving service contracts: HTTP method and status semantics, RFC 9457 problem errors, cursor pagination, idempotency keys, ETag concurrency, additive evolution and deprecation headers, OpenAPI 3.1/TypeSpec and protobuf/gRPC rules, breaking-change gates (oasdiff, buf) and client/server code generation from specs with drift checks; load when adding or changing an endpoint, RPC, event schema or SDK.
outline: Split source: code-review-checklist 'API design and compatibility' keeps review checks; this skill owns designing contracts (the checklist links here). Spec-first workflow: write OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON Schema 2020-12), TypeSpec or .proto first, lint (redocly lint, Spectral ruleset, buf lint), review the contract diff before code; code-first only with the exported spec committed and diffed in CI.

HTTP semantics table: method -> safe/idempotent -> codes (GET 200/304/404; POST 201+Location or 202+status URL; PUT/PATCH 200/204/409/412/422; DELETE 204/404); 400 vs 422, 401 vs 403, 409 vs 412, 429 + Retry-After; never 200 with an error body.

Error model: RFC 9457 application/problem+json (type URI, title, status, detail, instance) plus machine-readable errors[] with JSON pointers to fields and stable error codes clients can switch on; no stack traces or SQL.

Pagination and filtering: keyset/cursor pagination with an opaque base64 cursor encoding the sort key plus id tiebreaker, max limit, next link; offset only for small admin lists; one filter/sort grammar across endpoints; totals optional because they are expensive.

Idempotency and concurrency: Idempotency-Key on POST (store key + request hash + response ~24 h; same key with different body -> 422, in-flight duplicate -> 409); ETag + If-Match -> 412 to prevent lost updates; 428 when a precondition is required.

Evolution rules: additive-only within a version (new optional fields/endpoints), tolerant readers ignore unknown fields, enums treated as open by clients, never repurpose a field; deprecate with Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) headers plus changelog; URL major versions only for breaking redesigns.

Protobuf/gRPC rules: never renumber or reuse field numbers (reserved numbers and names on removal), enum zero value X_UNSPECIFIED, optional for presence, request/response wrapper messages, deadlines on every call, Google AIPs (AIP-158 pagination, AIP-180 compatibility, AIP-193 errors); Connect RPC for browser-friendly gRPC.

Breaking-change gates in CI: oasdiff breaking base.yaml head.yaml --fail-on ERR, buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main', schema-registry compatibility modes (BACKWARD/FULL) for event schemas (Avro, Protobuf, JSON Schema).

Code generation from specs: TS openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch or orval, Go oapi-codegen, multi-language openapi-generator or Kiota, buf generate (connect-go, connect-es, protoc-gen-go), Python datamodel-code-generator (pydantic), sqlc for SQL -> typed code; decide committed vs build-time output and add a drift check (regenerate && git diff --exit-code).

Contract testing: Schemathesis property-based tests generated from the OpenAPI document against the running provider; Pact for consumer-driven contracts between teams (testing-strategy covers levels).

Pitfalls: leaking DB schema into the API, booleans that later need a third state, timestamps without offset (use RFC 3339 UTC), int64 IDs as JSON numbers for JS clients (use strings), unbounded list endpoints, chatty N+1 APIs (offer batch or expand), credentials in query strings.

Worked example: add POST /v1/payments with Idempotency-Key, problem+json errors and cursor-paginated GET /v1/payments; spec reviewed first, oasdiff gate green, TS client generated with openapi-typescript, Schemathesis finds a 500 on an empty currency string that becomes a 422 before merge.

skills.name: sql-query-tuning
skills.description: Finding and fixing slow SQL: pg_stat_statements and slow-log triage, reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans in PostgreSQL 17/18 and MySQL 8.x, estimate-vs-actual diagnosis, composite/covering/partial/expression/GIN/BRIN index design, sargable rewrites, keyset pagination, ORM N+1 fixes, extended statistics and runtime timeouts; load when a query or endpoint is slow, a new query needs an index, or reviewing SQL performance.
outline: Split source: performance-optimization 'Databases', code-review-checklist SQL pitfalls and the cs-foundations planner notes keep one-line pointers here; MVCC and isolation live in database-transactions-isolation. Triage by total time, not mean: pg_stat_statements ORDER BY total_exec_time; MySQL performance_schema digest tables or the slow log; auto_explain (log_min_duration, log_analyze) to capture production plans with real parameter values.

Plan reading procedure: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, SETTINGS) on production-sized data (PostgreSQL 18 includes BUFFERS by default with ANALYZE); read bottom-up; per node compare estimated vs actual rows x loops (>= 10x off means statistics/correlation problem), Rows Removed by Filter, Heap Fetches on index-only scans, Sort/Hash 'Disk:' spills (work_mem), shared read vs hit; MySQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE / FORMAT=TREE; SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN; visualize with pev2/explain.dalibo.com.

Node -> meaning -> usual fix table: Seq Scan with selective filter -> index; Nested Loop with huge outer row counts -> fix estimates or index the inner join key; Sort on large input -> index matching ORDER BY; Index Scan with many heap fetches -> covering index or VACUUM for the visibility map; lossy Bitmap Heap Scan -> work_mem.

Planner model: cost units, cardinality estimation and the independence-assumption failure, join algorithms (index nested loop, hash, merge) and when each wins, System R join ordering and GEQO above geqo_threshold = 12, generic vs custom plans for prepared statements (plan_cache_mode).

Index design rules: composite order equality -> sort -> range (or ESR), leftmost-prefix (PG18 B-tree skip scan helps low-cardinality leading columns but do not design around it), INCLUDE for covering, partial indexes (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL), expression indexes (lower(email)), GIN for jsonb/arrays and pg_trgm for ILIKE '%x%', BRIN for append-only time columns; index every FK referencing column; weigh write amplification; find unused (pg_stat_user_indexes.idx_scan = 0) and duplicate indexes; trial with HypoPG; build CONCURRENTLY (zero-downtime-migrations).

Sargable rewrites: no functions/casts on indexed columns (created_at >= $1 AND created_at < $2 instead of date(created_at) = $1), parameter types matching column types, OR across columns -> UNION ALL, NOT IN (subquery) -> NOT EXISTS, DISTINCT hiding join fan-out, CTEs inlined since PG12 unless MATERIALIZED, exact COUNT(*) on huge tables -> estimates or maintained counters.

Keyset pagination: WHERE (created_at, id) < ($1, $2) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 50 with a matching composite index; OFFSET cost grows linearly with page depth and gives unstable pages without a unique tiebreaker.

ORM N+1 and chatty access: detect by query counting in tests (Django assertNumQueries, SQLAlchemy event listener, Prisma query log) and SQL logging; fix with select_related/prefetch_related, selectinload/joinedload, Prisma include, WHERE id = ANY($1) batching, DataLoader for GraphQL; bulk writes with COPY or multi-row inserts.

Statistics, maintenance and runtime guards: ANALYZE after bulk loads, ALTER COLUMN ... SET STATISTICS 500-1000 for skewed columns, CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies, ndistinct, mcv) for correlated columns, autovacuum tuning on hot tables; statement_timeout, lock_timeout, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout per role; PgBouncer transaction-mode and prepared-statement caveats.

Verification: before/after plan plus timing over >= 10 runs with cache state stated (performance-optimization statistics), identical parameters, write-path cost of the new index measured, and a regression test asserting query count or plan shape where cheap.

Pitfalls: tuning on a 1k-row dev database (seq scan is correct there), hints as a first resort, SELECT * defeating index-only scans, collation/locale differences between environments, parameter-dependent plans tested with one value only.

Worked example: /orders endpoint at 2.3 s: plan shows Seq Scan + Sort spilling 180 MB, estimate 120 rows vs actual 410k; fix with index (tenant_id, status, created_at DESC, id) INCLUDE (total) plus keyset pagination; result Index Only Scan, heap fetches 0 after VACUUM, p50 4 ms.

skills.name: zero-downtime-migrations
skills.description: Schema design defaults and zero-downtime schema changes on live databases: PostgreSQL/MySQL DDL lock levels, lock_timeout with retries, expand-migrate-contract with deploy ordering, NOT VALID constraints, concurrent indexes, batched resumable backfills, migration-tool specifics (Alembic, Django, Prisma, Flyway, Atlas, golang-migrate) and linters (squawk, Atlas lint, strong_migrations); load when writing, reviewing or sequencing a database migration.
outline: Split source: code-review-checklist 'Database migrations' checklist and the expand/contract line keep pointers here. New-table defaults: bigint identity or UUIDv7 keys (uuidv7() built in from PG18), timestamptz, numeric(p,s) for money, text + CHECK over varchar(n), NOT NULL by default, FKs with an index on the referencing column, UNIQUE constraints for business invariants (never app-only checks), created_at/updated_at, soft delete only with partial unique indexes, enum type vs lookup table trade-off.

PostgreSQL DDL risk table: ADD COLUMN nullable or with a constant default = metadata only (PG11+); volatile default and most ALTER TYPE = full rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; CREATE INDEX blocks writes -> CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (outside a transaction; a failed build leaves an INVALID index to drop); FK/CHECK -> ADD ... NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT; SET NOT NULL -> valid CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) first (PG12+ skips the scan) or PG18 NOT NULL ... NOT VALID; RENAME instant but breaks running code; DROP COLUMN instant but only after code stops reading it.

Lock-queue hazard: even instant DDL waits behind long transactions and then blocks every query queued after it -> SET lock_timeout = '2s' plus statement_timeout and retry with backoff; check pg_stat_activity for long transactions first; MySQL metadata locks behave the same way.

Expand-migrate-contract with deploy ordering, e.g. rename a column: (1) add new column, (2) deploy dual-write, (3) backfill, (4) deploy reads from new, (5) stop writing old, (6) drop old in a later release; app versions N and N+1 must both work against every intermediate schema; reversible until step 6, which is the named point of no return.

Backfills: batch by primary-key ranges (1k-10k rows), commit per batch, throttle on replication lag and load, idempotent UPDATE ... WHERE new_col IS NULL, resumable checkpoint, run as a job outside the migration transaction, watch dead tuples/autovacuum; verify with row counts and checksums.

MySQL specifics: ALGORITHM=INSTANT (add column, 8.0+), ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE checks, gh-ost or pt-online-schema-change for table copies; table rewrites and reclaiming space in PostgreSQL via pg_repack (or PG19 REPACK CONCURRENTLY where available).

Tool specifics: Alembic (review autogenerate output; concurrent index inside op.get_context().autocommit_block()), Django (sqlmigrate to read SQL, AddIndexConcurrently with atomic = False, SeparateDatabaseAndState), Prisma Migrate (--create-only then edit SQL), Flyway/Liquibase, Atlas (atlas migrate lint), golang-migrate/sqlx/Diesel; one concern per migration file.

Lint and test in CI: squawk on SQL migrations, Atlas lint, strong_migrations (Rails), django-migration-linter; apply on a production-sized snapshot and time it; run the previous app version's tests against the new schema; document down-migration or forward-fix only.
Safety net: PITR/backup checkpoint before irreversible steps, feature flag for the read switch, post-backfill verification queries, rollback plan written before running.

Pitfalls: migration frameworks wrapping CONCURRENTLY in a transaction, ORMs selecting * and breaking on dropped columns (ignore the column in the model first), enum ADD VALUE inside transactions on old versions, triggers/views/materialized views depending on altered columns, single giant UPDATE backfills bloating the table and the WAL.

Worked example: make orders.customer_id NOT NULL with an FK on a 400M-row table: CHECK (customer_id IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID -> batched backfill of orphans -> VALIDATE -> SET NOT NULL -> drop CHECK -> FK NOT VALID -> VALIDATE; each step under lock_timeout 2s with retries; total exclusive-lock time under 50 ms.

skills.name: regex-engineering
skills.description: Writing correct, fast and portable regular expressions: when to use a parser instead, flavor differences (PCRE2, Python re, JavaScript u/v flags, RE2/Go, Rust regex, Java, .NET, POSIX grep/sed/awk), test-table-driven construction, anchoring and full-match validation, Unicode traps, catastrophic backtracking diagnosis and fixes, and safe multi-file search-and-replace; load when writing, debugging or reviewing a regex or an rg/sed/perl rewrite.
outline: Split source: cs-foundations section 6 keeps automata theory and security-review keeps the ReDoS threat entry; both point here for practice. Decision table: regex fits tokens, lines and flat formats; use parsers for HTML/XML (lxml, selectolax), JSON (jq), CSV (csv module), URLs (urllib.parse, URL), dates (date parsers), nested or balanced constructs; email validation = loose sanity check plus a verification message.

Flavor matrix: lookbehind, backreferences, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, named-group syntax ((?P<n>) vs (?<n>)), \A/\z, \p{L}, inline flags, linear-time guarantee across PCRE2 (grep -P, rg -P), Python re (atomic/possessive since 3.11) and the regex module, JavaScript (u and v flags, d indices, RegExp.escape in ES2025), Go/RE2 and Rust regex (no lookaround/backrefs, linear time; fancy-regex adds them), Java, .NET (NonBacktracking, match timeouts), POSIX BRE/ERE with GNU vs BSD differences.

Construction procedure: write positive and negative examples as a test table first, anchor, build incrementally, prefer negated classes ([^"]*) over lazy dot, name groups, use verbose mode (re.X, (?x)) with comments for anything over ~40 chars, compile once as a module constant.

Validation vs search: use re.fullmatch or anchors with the right end anchor; Python $ matches before a trailing newline (use \Z or fullmatch); JavaScript has no \A/\z; multiline changes ^/$; dotall for . across newlines.

Unicode traps: Python 3 \d and \w match non-ASCII digits/letters (use [0-9] or re.ASCII), case-insensitive matching with Turkish i and German sharp s, grapheme clusters (\X in PCRE2/regex module), normalize (NFC/NFKC) before matching, JS needs u or v for astral code points, \b is ASCII-centric in several flavors.

Catastrophic backtracking: dangerous shapes (nested quantifiers (a+)+, overlapping alternation (a|ab)*, adjacent .* sharing characters, repeated optional groups); fixes: mutually exclusive alternatives, unroll-the-loop ("[^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)*"), atomic groups or possessive quantifiers, a linear engine, input length caps; detect with recheck, regexploit, eslint-plugin-regexp, safe-regex plus a timing test (50 KB adversarial input under 100 ms); never run raw user-supplied patterns on a backtracking engine.

Multi-file search and replace: preview with rg -n (or rg -P), apply with rg -l pat | xargs perl -pi -e 's/.../.../g' or sd; GNU sed -i vs BSD sed -i ''; -E for ERE; replacement syntax \1 vs $1 vs ${name}; escape literal input (re.escape, RegExp.escape, regexp.QuoteMeta); syntax-aware changes go to codemod-automation.

Testing regexes: table-driven unit tests asserting both match/no-match and captured groups; property or fuzz test that the regex agrees with a reference parser and stays within the time budget on generated inputs (testing-strategy).

Readability in review: comment intent, compose complex patterns from named fragments (f-strings, String.raw), keep numeric range logic out of regex (parse then compare), flag any regex on a hot path without a compiled constant.

Regex set operations (from cs-foundations section 6): overlap, intersection and equivalence of patterns with interegular or greenery (routes or rules that shadow each other), DFA size inspection with regex-automata, blow-up from counted repetition like a{1000} and n-th-from-the-end families.

Pitfalls: greedy .* overmatching across delimiters, unescaped dots in hostnames/IPs, [A-z] including punctuation, forgetting the global/multiline flag, locale-dependent \w, regex-based HTML scraping that breaks on attribute order.

Worked example: log-line parser for 'ts level [req=..] msg' built from a 12-row example table as a verbose Python regex with named groups, ReDoS check clean on a 50 KB input, then ported to Go RE2 by restructuring a lookahead into an optional group; both versions pass the same table.

skills.name: resilience-patterns
skills.description: Making calls between components robust under failure and load: timeout and deadline budgets, retry classification with exponential backoff and full jitter, retry budgets, idempotency keys and dedup, bounded concurrency and backpressure sized by Little's law, rate limiting (token bucket, GCRA), circuit breakers, bulkheads, hedged requests and graceful shutdown, with library choices per language; load when writing or reviewing code that calls networks, queues, databases or third-party APIs, or fans out concurrent work.
outline: Timeouts first: every network call has connect and overall timeouts; propagate one deadline (gRPC deadlines, Go context, AbortSignal.timeout/AbortSignal.any, asyncio.timeout); per-hop timeout = remaining budget minus margin; start from the dependency's p99.9 x 1.5; worked budget table for a 3-hop chain.

Retry decision table: retry connection errors, 502/503/504, 429 (honour Retry-After), gRPC UNAVAILABLE; never 400/401/403/404/409/422 or non-idempotent writes without an idempotency key; 3-4 attempts max.

Backoff formula: full jitter sleep = random(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt)) with base ~100 ms and cap 10-20 s; decorrelated jitter as alternative; why un-jittered backoff synchronizes clients into thundering herds.

Retry amplification and budgets: retry at one layer only (3 layers x 3 attempts = 27x load), retry budget of ~10-20% extra requests (token-bucket style as in gRPC retry throttling), no retries while the circuit is open.

Idempotency: client-generated keys, server dedup table (key, request hash, stored response, expiry) behind a unique constraint, at-least-once consumers made safe by processed-message tables or idempotent upserts; transactional outbox for 'write then publish' (architect owns the design choice).

Bounded concurrency and backpressure: semaphores or worker pools sized by Little's law (concurrency = rate x latency x 1.2-1.5), bounded queues with an explicit overflow policy (block, reject with 429/503, drop oldest), never unbounded gather/Promise.all/goroutine-per-item over user-sized input, priority-based load shedding.

Rate limiting math: token bucket (rate r, burst b, refill time b/r), GCRA for Redis-backed distributed limits, client-side limiters that respect provider quotas, sliding-window counters for public APIs.

Circuit breakers and bulkheads: failure-rate threshold (e.g. 50%) over a sliding window with a minimum call count (e.g. 20), open duration (e.g. 30 s), limited half-open probes; separate pools per dependency so one slow dependency cannot exhaust all threads or connections.

Tail latency and shutdown: hedged requests after the p95 delay (~5% extra load) for idempotent reads only, cancelling the loser; graceful shutdown on SIGTERM (fail readiness, stop accepting, drain in-flight within terminationGracePeriodSeconds, close pools; preStop sleep for endpoint propagation).

Library map: Python tenacity or stamina, aiolimiter, asyncio.Semaphore; TS p-retry, p-limit, cockatiel; Go errgroup SetLimit, x/time/rate, failsafe-go; JVM resilience4j or Failsafe, Kotlin withTimeout; Rust tower (timeout/retry/concurrency-limit layers), backon; .NET Polly.
Testing: fault injection with toxiproxy or fake transports, fake clocks for backoff schedules, assertions on attempt counts and absence of duplicate side effects, chaos runs under load before launch.

Worked example: payment-provider client: 2 s overall deadline, 3 attempts with full jitter on 503/timeouts only, Idempotency-Key per charge, breaker at 50% failures over 20 calls, pool of 16 sized from 200 rps x 60 ms x 1.3; toxiproxy test shows zero duplicate charges and bounded p99 during a 30 s provider outage.

OpenTelemetry setup: SDK + OTLP exporter configured by env (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG); zero-code instrumentation first (opentelemetry-bootstrap -a install + opentelemetry-instrument, Node --require @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node/register, Java agent), then manual spans for business operations.

Metric design: RED per endpoint (rate, errors, duration histogram) and USE per resource (utilization, saturation, errors); histograms not averages (buckets around SLO thresholds or exponential/native histograms); monotonic counters with _total and base units (_seconds, _bytes); cardinality budget = product of label value counts, so no user_id/request_id/raw-path labels (use the route template).

SLOs and alerts: SLI = good events / valid events, error budget = (1 - SLO) x window; multiwindow burn-rate alerts for 99.9%/30 d (page at 14.4x over 1 h AND 5 min, page at 6x over 6 h AND 30 min, ticket at 1x over 3 d AND 6 h); alert on user-visible symptoms and link runbooks.

skills.description: React 19.x with TypeScript for maintainable UIs: effect discipline ('you might not need an effect', useEffectEvent), state placement and server-state libraries, Actions with useActionState/useOptimistic, typed props and generic components, forms with schema validation, keys and identity, performance with the React Compiler and Profiler evidence, accessibility and behaviour-focused component tests; load when writing, reviewing or debugging React components or hooks.

State placement: local useState/useReducer -> lift to the nearest common parent -> context for low-frequency globals (theme, auth) -> external store (Zustand, Redux Toolkit, Jotai) for high-frequency shared client state; server state in TanStack Query; URL as state for filters and pagination; never copy props into state.

Typing components: type Props with discriminated unions for variant props, children: React.ReactNode, ComponentProps<'button'> to extend native props, generic components (<T,>(props: ListProps<T>)), typed event handlers (React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>), context created with undefined default plus a guarded useX hook instead of any.
Forms: react-hook-form + zod resolver or native form Actions; controlled vs uncontrolled decision; errors linked with aria-describedby; pending state prevents double submit.
Lists and identity: stable keys from data IDs (never array index for reorderable lists), change key to reset state intentionally, never define components inside components.

Performance: measure with the React DevTools Profiler; with the React Compiler enabled (build-time Babel/SWC plugin) drop manual useMemo/useCallback noise; without it memoize only on Profiler evidence; virtualize long lists (TanStack Virtual); code-split with lazy + Suspense; keep context values stable.

Accessibility: semantic elements first (button, not clickable div), labels for every input, dialog focus management (native <dialog> or React Aria/Radix primitives), keyboard support and visible focus, aria-live for async status; eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y plus axe in tests.
Testing: Vitest + Testing Library role queries + user-event (typescript-testing-vitest), MSW for network, Playwright for critical journeys; assert behaviour, not internal state or CSS classes.

Pitfalls: setState during render loops, objects/arrays recreated in dependency arrays, hydration mismatches from Date.now/Math.random/locale formatting during render, over-broad context causing re-render storms, effect chains cascading state updates, leaked subscriptions.

Worked example: OrdersPage with 6 effects and duplicated state refactored: filters derived from the URL, TanStack Query with keyset pagination, useOptimistic for status toggles, discriminated Row props, compiler-enabled build; renders per keystroke 14 -> 2, one fetch race and two a11y violations removed, tests use role queries only.

Closures: Fn/FnMut/FnOnce inference, move closures, disjoint field capture (2021+), async closures `async || {}` with AsyncFn traits (1.85)

Value classes: mangled function names, exposing boxed variants (newer @JvmExposeBoxed support; check your Kotlin version), boxing at generic boundaries

skills.name: kotlin-coroutines-flow
skills.description: Kotlin coroutines and Flow under structured concurrency: scope ownership, exception propagation and SupervisorJob, cancellation hygiene, dispatchers, Mutex/Semaphore, callback bridging, cold flow vs StateFlow/SharedFlow/Channel, operator semantics, stateIn/shareIn and lifecycle-aware collection. Load when writing or debugging suspend code, flows, leaked jobs or swallowed cancellation.
outline: Scope ownership: lifecycle scopes, an application scope with SupervisorJob cancelled on shutdown, no GlobalScope, coroutineScope vs supervisorScope.
Exception propagation table: launch vs async, CoroutineExceptionHandler only on root coroutines, supervisor semantics, exceptions surfacing at await().
Cancellation hygiene: ensureActive/yield, rethrow CancellationException from catch(Exception) and runCatching, withTimeout vs withTimeoutOrNull, cleanup in finally with withContext(NonCancellable).

Dispatchers and shared state: Default/IO/Main and main-safety, limitedParallelism, dispatchers injected through constructors; Mutex.withLock, Semaphore, atomics, confinement to one coroutine via a Channel.

Bridging and fan-out: suspendCancellableCoroutine with invokeOnCancellation, CompletableFuture.await, runBlocking only in main and tests; async/awaitAll bounded by a Semaphore or flatMapMerge(concurrency).
Flow type choice: cold flow {}, StateFlow, SharedFlow (replay, extraBufferCapacity, onBufferOverflow), Channel.receiveAsFlow for exactly-once events; events vs state modelling.
Operator semantics: flowOn and catch affect only upstream, onCompletion, retryWhen, buffer/conflate/collectLatest, debounce/sample, combine vs zip vs merge, flatMapLatest/Merge/Concat.

Sharing: stateIn/shareIn with WhileSubscribed(5_000) vs Eagerly/Lazily, StateFlow equality conflation and update { it.copy(...) }, tryEmit failing without a buffer; callbackFlow + trySend + awaitClose and channelFlow for callback APIs; never withContext around emit.
Android collection and debugging: repeatOnLifecycle, collectAsStateWithLifecycle; DebugProbes.dumpCoroutines, CoroutineName, -Dkotlinx.coroutines.debug, the IDE coroutine debugger.

Pitfalls: leaked jobs, swallowed cancellation, silent withTimeout in launch, blocking calls on Default, runBlocking on Main, 'Flow invariant is violated', missed StateFlow events, several collectors re-running a cold flow, catch placed below the failing operator.

Worked example: a ViewModel that leaks a polling job and swallows cancellation, fixed; a search-box pipeline (debounce, distinctUntilChanged, flatMapLatest, stateIn) verified with Turbine in virtual time (test mechanics in kotlin-testing).

skills.name: logo-design-process
skills.description: Logo design from brief to vector master kit (discovery, mark-type choice, exploration funnel, construction geometry, optical corrections, wordmark from a licensed font, small-size and monochrome tests, lockups, export kit). Load when creating, refining or auditing a logo, monogram or wordmark.
outline: Discovery worksheet: 3 brand attributes, name meaning, usage contexts (16 px favicon, app icon, signage, embroidery, engraving). Competitor audit: collect 8-12 marks and plot them on two axes (geometric to organic, literal to abstract) to find unclaimed visual territory.
Mark-type decision table: wordmark, lettermark or monogram, pictorial, abstract, emblem, combination, mascot. Choose by name length, recognition budget, scalability and legal distinctiveness.

Exploration funnel: 20-40 thumbnails (described, or black-only vector_generate sketches in test mode), narrowed to 3-5 directions and then 1-2 refinements. Includes a vector_generate prompt skeleton for one-colour marks. Raster-generated logos are never deliverables.

Construction rules: integer coordinates on a 96- or 1000-unit grid, a limited angle set (0/45/90), one stroke and corner-radius vocabulary, node economy, closed paths and flattened booleans. Golden-ratio circle grids are presentation only and not a requirement.

Optical corrections: 1-3% overshoot on round and pointed forms, horizontals about 5-10% thinner than verticals, ink traps and opened counters for small sizes, visual centre of mass rather than geometric centre, optical kerning of the wordmark.

Wordmark from a real typeface: check that the licence allows logo use (OFL allows it, some commercial EULAs restrict it), outline the type, set custom kerning pairs and adjust letterforms. Never ship generated lettering.

Test ladder: render at 16/24/32/64/256 px plus 10 mm print, design in black first and add colour later, reversed and one-colour versions, over a photo, blur/squint test, favicon and app-icon crops, minimum line weight for embroidery (~1 mm) and laser engraving (~0.3 mm).

Distinctiveness sanity check: reverse image search (Google Lens, TinEye) plus a look at the trademark databases (USPTO Trademark Search, EUIPO eSearch, WIPO Global Brand Database). Report the result as an Open doubt and never as legal clearance.

Lockups and rules: horizontal, stacked and mark-only lockups, a clear-space unit derived from the mark (x-height or mark width fraction), minimum sizes in px and mm, and full-colour, 1-colour, reversed and grayscale versions.

Export kit: SVG checked with svgcheck --budget logo, vector PDF, transparent PNG at @1x/2x/3x, favicon.svg plus favicon.ico (16/32), 180 px apple-touch-icon, 512 px PWA maskable icon with content inside the 80% safe circle, and CMYK/spot versions handed to print-prepress. Files follow a naming convention.
Worked example: a geometric monogram on a 96-unit grid, 2 directions. The 16 px test closes a counter, so an ink-trap fix is applied before delivering the kit and usage table.
Pitfalls: hairlines that vanish small, a gradient as a requirement, trend-chasing, colour as the only differentiator, unlicensed fonts, detail below 1/32 of the mark height.

skills.name: type-scale-systems
skills.description: Typography systems: modular scale choice, role table, measure/leading/tracking rules, pairing tests, fluid clamp() type, variable and web-font loading without layout shift, OpenType features and print type settings. Load when defining, implementing or auditing a type system for screen or print.
outline: Modular scale size_k = base x r^k, with a ratio table from 1.125 to 1.618 by medium and number of levels, rounded to 0.5 px. Two-ratio approach: 1.2 on mobile, 1.25-1.333 on desktop.
Role table (display, H1-H3, body, small, caps label, code) giving size, weight, line-height and tracking defaults. Line-heights snap to a 4 px multiple so baselines align.

Rules: measure 45-75 ch (66 ideal; 30-40 for mobile and narrow columns), body leading 1.4-1.6 and headings 1.05-1.25, display tracking -1% to -3%, caps and small labels +5% to +12%, web body at least 16 px, UI labels at least 12 px.

Fluid type: slope/intercept derivation for clamp() (worked example 32 px at 360 to 56 px at 1440 gives clamp(2rem, 1.5rem + 2.222vw, 3.5rem)), always keeping a rem term to satisfy WCAG 1.4.4. Includes a small Python generator that emits a Utopia-style step scale as CSS custom properties.

Pairing: catalogue of OFL families (Inter, Source Serif 4, IBM Plex, Source Sans 3, Fraunces, Literata, Noto). Measure x-height match with fontTools (OS/2 sxHeight / unitsPerEm), contrast the classifications, and never pair two similar grotesques.

Web-font loading: WOFF2 only, subset with pyftsubset (--flavor=woff2 --unicodes per script, keep layout features), variable wght/opsz axes with font-optical-sizing:auto, preload only the 1-2 critical files, font-display: swap.

Layout-shift prevention: compute size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override for a metric-matched system fallback, using fontTools or Capsize/fontaine. Verify CLS with a Lighthouse run.

OpenType and CSS details: tabular-nums and lining-nums for data, oldstyle figures in prose, case-sensitive forms, ss01 via font-feature-settings, text-wrap: balance for headings and pretty for paragraphs, hyphens: auto (needs a correct lang attribute), typographic quotes and dashes.

Print settings: body 9-11 pt with leading +2-4 pt, a baseline grid equal to the leading, justification ranges (word spacing 80/100/133%), hyphenation limits, reversed text at least 8 pt medium weight, lines at least 0.25 pt, true small caps.
Multilingual: CJK line-height 1.7-1.8 with no italics, Arabic about 10-20% larger, RTL mirroring rules, and containers sized for +40% translation expansion.
Licensing check per medium (desktop, web, app embedding, broadcast, logo) and the 10-item typography critique checklist.
Worked example: a docs-site scale (1.2 mobile to 1.25 desktop from 16 px) emitted as tokens with a subset variable Inter and a metric-matched fallback, CLS 0.00 before and after.

skills.name: oklch-palette-ramps
skills.description: Colour palette construction in OKLCH: brand hex to gamut-safe 11-step ramps, tinted neutrals, semantic and state colours, dark-theme palettes, harmony schemes and categorical sets, with every step annotated by measured WCAG contrast. Load when building, extending or fixing a palette.
outline: Why OKLCH rather than HSL: perceptual lightness. CSS support: oklch(), color-mix(in oklch, ...) and relative colour syntax oklch(from var(--brand) calc(l - 0.1) c h) are Baseline in evergreen browsers.

Stdlib Python converter (hex to OKLab/OKLCH, WCAG luminance and contrast, lightness sweep at fixed hue/chroma), carried over from the colour reference. Gamut mapping with coloraide fit('srgb') following the CSS Color 4 method, because channel clipping shifts hue.

Ramp procedure: steps 50-950 with a target-L table from ~0.97 to ~0.25, chroma peaking at the mid steps and tapered toward both ends, fixed hue or a small deliberate hue shift for yellows and oranges in shades. Each step is gamut-mapped to sRGB, with an optional Display P3 variant behind @media (color-gamut: p3).

Contrast annotation per step against white, black and the darkest and lightest surfaces. Each step is marked text-safe (4.5:1), UI-safe (3:1) or decorative. Every intended pair is measured, never inferred from step distance.

Tinted neutrals: chroma 0.005-0.02 pushed toward the brand hue. Semantic colours: success ~145, warning ~75, danger ~25, info ~250 (OKLCH hue) with lightness equalised per role. Warning uses dark text on an amber fill.
Harmony schemes table (monochromatic, analogous, complementary, split-complementary, triadic) as starting points, plus the 60-30-10 proportion guide.

A brand colour that cannot serve two roles becomes two semantic tokens from one hue. Worked case: #E94560 becomes accent-on-dark #EC4862 (4.59:1 on #1A1A2E) and accent-fill #D63151 (4.76:1 under white).
Dark theme as its own mapping, not an inversion: surfaces in the #121212-#1E1E1E range, elevation shown by lighter surfaces, brand chroma reduced, body text ~#E6E6E6. Every pair is re-measured.

Categorical sets: Okabe-Ito (#E69F00 #56B4E9 #009E73 #F0E442 #0072B2 #D55E00 #CC79A7) with an OKLCH L spread of at least 0.10-0.15 between neighbours. Sequential and diverging scales are handed to chart-design-encoding.
Deliverable: a palette table (token, hex, oklch(), contrast vs white/black/surface, allowed roles) plus CSS custom properties and DTCG colour tokens for design-tokens-dtcg.

Pitfalls: HSL ramps with uneven perceived steps, pure yellow text on white, red/green pairs at equal L, saturated RGB brand colours with no CMYK or print fallback noted, chroma that is out of gamut at the extreme steps.

skills.name: icon-system-design
skills.description: Icon system design: canvas, live area and keyline shapes, stroke/cap/corner rules, pixel snapping at 16/20/24, metaphor choice, outline vs filled sets, naming and metadata, sprite and component export, and a measured consistency audit. Load when designing, extending or auditing an icon set.
outline: Spec sheet: 24 px canvas, 2 px padding (20 px live area), stroke 1.5 or 2 px, round or square caps and joins chosen once, one outer corner radius (e.g. 2 px), and keylines (circle ~20, square ~18, portrait and landscape rectangles 16x20 and 20x16).
Size variants: when to redraw rather than scale (16 px drops interior detail, uses a 1 px padding and a 14 px live area). Stroke widths per size and a matching rule for 20 and 32 px.

Pixel snapping math: odd stroke widths centred on .5 coordinates, even widths on integers. A 1.5 px stroke blurs at 1x, so pick it only for 2x-first products. Verify by rendering at 1x with resvg or rsvg-convert and Reading the result.

Construction rules: angles limited to 0/45/90 (30/60 for isometric sets), consistent terminals, front-on perspective, open versus closed shapes chosen once. Visual mass is equalised by measuring ink coverage per icon with Pillow and keeping it within about ±10% of the set median.

Metaphor table of conventions (magnifier for search, gear for settings, trash for delete, and so on). Avoid culture-specific gestures and text glyphs. 5-second recognition test with labels hidden, and an icon plus label for ambiguous actions.
Outline, filled and duotone are separate sets with one state mapping (outline default, filled active/selected) that is never mixed within a view.

Production pipeline: approve one anchor icon, then reuse its style sentence verbatim. Fan out per icon to vector-artist for sets of more than 8, hand-write simple glyphs, then svgcheck fit --size 24 --pad 2, currentcolor and check --budget icon.
Naming and metadata: kebab-case name-variant-size, plus a tags/synonyms JSON for search and semver for the set.

Delivery: individual SVGs, a symbol sprite used via <use href='#id'>, React components via npx @svgr/cli --icon --typescript, optional Iconify JSON. Icon fonts are discouraged (accessibility, hinting, CLS).

Accessibility: decorative icons get aria-hidden, meaningful icons need a title or an aria-label on the control, 3:1 non-text contrast, and the hit target at least 24x24 CSS px even when the glyph is 16.

Consistency audit: contact sheet of every icon at 24 and 16 px with a checklist (stroke weight, caps, radii, mass, perspective, optical size, alignment to keylines). Worked example: extending an open 24/2 px round-stroke set with three new icons that pass the audit.

skills.name: brand-guidelines-system
skills.description: Brand guidelines as a working system: logo usage rules, colour and type specs across HEX/OKLCH/CMYK/spot, imagery and generated-image direction, voice, do/don't sheets, accessibility pairings, an asset manifest and a brand-audit procedure. Load when writing, auditing or applying brand guidelines.
outline: Required sections in order: logo suite, colour, typography, grid and spacing, imagery, iconography and data-viz palette, motion if relevant, voice and tone, accessibility statement, asset manifest and changelog.
Logo usage: clear-space unit, minimum sizes in px and mm, allowed backgrounds, and a misuse grid (stretch, recolour, effects, rotation, crowding, low contrast) rendered as a do/don't sheet.

Colour spec per brand colour: HEX, RGB, OKLCH, CMYK per named profile (PSO Coated v3, GRACoL 2013) and Pantone Coated/Uncoated. Note that conversions are approximations confirmed by printer proofs, plus a usage-proportion bar.
Typography spec: families, weights, fallbacks, scale tokens, role table and per-medium licence status, linking to type-scale-systems.

Imagery direction: photography rules (light, palette, subject distance, crop, representation), illustration style sheet, and a generated-image policy (allowed routed models, mandatory review, disclosure, no real-person likeness, 2-3 canonical style references plus a verbatim style sentence for image models).
Voice and tone: 3-4 attributes in 'we are X, not Y' form, with example headlines, CTAs and error messages.
Accessibility statement: the approved foreground/background pairs table with measured ratios and permitted sizes, generated from tokens.

Brand audit procedure: capture live touchpoints (browser-operator screenshots), sample pixels and measure OKLab distance to the nearest token to flag drift, check logo clear space and type, then score and report fixes.
Application checklist for a new piece, plus the hide-the-logo consistency test.

Delivery layout: a brand/ folder (logo/, color/*.tokens.json, fonts/ with licences, templates/, imagery/refs/). Guidelines ship as an HTML page or doc, not PDF only, and are versioned with a changelog.

Pitfalls: CMYK values copied from automatic conversion, rules with no rationale, missing misuse examples, guidelines that ignore dark mode or small sizes, and a system that only works when the logo is present.

skills.name: design-tokens-dtcg
skills.description: Design tokens in the W3C DTCG 2025.10 format: primitive/semantic/component tiers, aliases, types, modes and themes, naming grammar, validation, and builds to CSS variables, Tailwind v4 @theme and native platforms with Style Dictionary or Terrazzo. Load when creating, migrating or validating a token set.
outline: Three tiers with a naming grammar {category}.{property}.{variant}.{state}: primitive color.blue.600 maps to semantic color.action.primary.bg, which maps to component button.primary.bg. Components reference semantics only, never primitives.

DTCG 2025.10 essentials: $value, $type, $description, $deprecated, $extensions, groups and {group.token} aliases. Colour values are objects {colorSpace: 'oklch', components: [...], alpha, hex fallback} and dimensions are {value, unit}. Composite types: shadow, border, typography, transition, gradient, strokeStyle. Check details against designtokens.org before using newer features ($extends, $ref, the resolver module).
An annotated .tokens.json example covering colour, dimension, fontFamily, typography composite and duration/cubicBezier.

Modes and themes: light, dark, high-contrast and density are swapped at the semantic tier only, with primitives shared. Organise them as one file per mode or as resolver sets, and emit them as [data-theme] selectors or media queries in CSS.

Build pipelines: Style Dictionary 4/5 (DTCG-aware; platforms css, js, ios-swift, android/compose) or Terrazzo (npx terrazzo build with css and tailwind plugins). Outputs are CSS custom properties, a Tailwind v4 @theme block, and Swift/Kotlin constants.

Stdlib Python validator: every alias resolves, no cycles, $type consistent along alias chains, tier rules respected, units present, no duplicate names after kebab-casing. Every semantic text/bg pair passes the target contrast (shared code with visual-accessibility-audit).
Naming rules: name by role, not by value (no blue-text), avoid component-token explosion, deprecate rather than delete, and keep a stable public set versus an internal set.
Migration recipes: Tailwind v3 tailwind.config.js theme to v4 CSS-first @theme, SCSS/LESS variables to tokens, and design-tool variables (Figma Variables via plugin or REST export) to DTCG.
Release discipline: a semver token package, a changelog generated from a token diff, and a visual regression pass (Playwright screenshot diff of key screens) after any semantic change.

Worked example: brand pink split into accent-on-dark and accent-fill semantics with dark-mode overrides, built to CSS variables and a Tailwind v4 @theme, with the validator and contrast check passing.
Pitfalls: hex strings where the format expects colour objects, aliases that cross tiers backwards, px values with units stripped, the dark theme forked at the primitive tier, tokens nobody consumes.

skills.name: ui-mockup-hifi
skills.description: UI/UX mockups from flow to high fidelity: screen inventory, wireframes with real content, component state matrix, platform conventions, token-driven HTML/CSS mockups rendered at breakpoints with Playwright, redline annotations and heuristic review. Load when designing, presenting or reviewing app or web screens.
outline: Inputs: user goals (jobs to be done), user flow as a numbered list or mermaid diagram, screen inventory, and content model. Missing flows or copy become an Open doubt.
Fidelity ladder: grayscale wireframe with real copy lengths, then mid-fi with grid and type scale, then hi-fi with tokens. Each step lists the decisions it freezes.

Mockups are built as single-file HTML/CSS that consumes the token CSS variables, because they render deterministically and double as hand-off. Render via Playwright (mcp__playwright__browser_take_screenshot, or npx playwright screenshot --viewport-size=390,844) at 390x844, 768x1024 and 1440x900, then Read each screenshot.
Component state matrix: default, hover, focus-visible, active, selected, disabled, loading/skeleton, error, empty and success. Every interactive component shows every applicable state.

Pattern defaults: mobile bottom tab bar with at most 5 items and side nav on desktop; forms single-column with labels above fields, 44-48 px fields and inline validation on blur; tables with right-aligned tabular numerals, sticky headers and row actions; modals and sheets, toasts, empty states with a next action.
Content realism: long names and strings, +40% localisation, zero/one/many and overflow data, real error messages. No lorem ipsum in hi-fi.
Targets and platforms: WCAG 2.5.8 minimum 24x24 CSS px, Apple HIG 44x44 pt, Material 3 48x48 dp, iOS Dynamic Type and Android font scaling at 200%, safe-area insets (env(safe-area-inset-*)).
Light and dark renders of every hi-fi screen, plus a forced-colors check on web.

Redlines: an overlay script or CSS outline mode that labels spacing values and token names on the screenshot. The spec lists components, tokens used and interaction notes (transitions, durations, reduced-motion behaviour).
Heuristic review: Nielsen's 10 heuristics scored 0-3, plus quick accessibility checks (focus order, labels, contrast) and the design critique rubric from the hub. Top fixes listed by impact.

Worked example: a settings screen taken from mobile wireframe to desktop hi-fi, with the state matrix, a three-breakpoint screenshot sheet, and review fixes (hover-only affordance replaced, placeholder-as-label removed).

skills.name: chart-design-encoding
skills.description: Data-visualisation design: chart form chosen by question, perceptual encoding ranking, categorical/sequential/diverging colour, axis/label/annotation rules, uncertainty, small multiples, dashboards and publication figures, styled in matplotlib, Vega-Lite or Observable Plot. Load before designing or critiquing any chart, figure or dashboard.
outline: Question-to-form table: comparison uses sorted bars or dot plots; trend uses lines; distribution uses histogram, box, violin or ECDF; relationship uses scatter with a trend line; part-to-whole uses stacked bars or a treemap (pie only for 2-4 parts); ranking uses lollipops; geography uses a choropleth of rates, not counts.

Cleveland-McGill encoding ranking (aligned position, unaligned position, length, angle/slope, area, colour saturation). Consequences: bars start at zero, lines may not, no 3D, no dual axes without clear justification.

Colour: categorical sets of at most 7 (Okabe-Ito, Tableau 10), sequential scales perceptually uniform (viridis, cividis or a single-hue OKLCH ramp), diverging only around a meaningful midpoint. Never use rainbow or jet. Highlight one series and gray the rest, then run a CVD check.
Axes and labels: direct labels instead of legends, units in titles, 5-7 ticks, thousands separators and SI prefixes, labelled log scales, and aspect ratio banked toward 45 degrees for line slopes.
Annotation layer: a title that states the finding, a subtitle for scope and units, event annotations, and a source/notes line.
Uncertainty: say which of SD, SE or CI the error bars show, use bands for series, show n, and avoid bar-plus-error-bar for distributions.
Overlays versus small multiples: more than 4 series moves to small multiples with shared scales. Includes rules for sorting facets.
Dashboards: a KPI tile row with delta and period, 2-3 key charts above the fold, consistent time windows and colours across tiles, filters top-left, stated refresh time.

Styling snippets: matplotlib rcParams (spines off, light grid, sizes, pdf.fonttype 42 for editable text), a Vega-Lite config block, and Observable Plot defaults. Export SVG or PDF for vectors and PNG at 2x for raster.
Publication figures: single column ~85-90 mm and double column ~170-180 mm, 7-9 pt text at final size, line widths of at least 0.5 pt, vector PDF with embedded fonts, panel labels (a), (b).
Accessibility: marks at 3:1 against the background (1.4.11), redundant shape or pattern encoding, and alt text giving the takeaway plus a link to a data table.
Worked example: a 9-slice 3D pie redesigned as a sorted horizontal bar with one highlighted category and a finding title, with before and after critique scores.

skills.name: print-prepress-pdfx
skills.description: Print preparation: printer-spec intake, bleed and safe zones, effective-ppi checks, ICC CMYK conversion (PSO Coated v3/FOGRA51, GRACoL 2013), rich black and total-ink limits, overprint and spot colours, font embedding, PDF/X-4 export, and command-line preflight with poppler, qpdf and Ghostscript. Load before sending any file to a printer.
outline: Printer spec intake: trim size, bleed (3 mm, or 0.125 in in the US), safe zone (3-5 mm), ICC profile, TAC limit, required PDF standard (X-4 or X-1a), spot colours, stock, proof type. Unknown values become an Open doubt and are never assumed.
Document math: final pixels = (trim + 2 x bleed) / 25.4 x ppi. Worked: A4 at 300 ppi with bleed is 216x303 mm, or 2551x3579 px. Backgrounds and images extend fully into the bleed.
Effective resolution: pdfimages -list (x-ppi/y-ppi) flags anything under 300 ppi, or under 150 ppi for large formats viewed from far away. Upscaling is a last resort and is labelled.

Colour conversion: a profile table (PSO Coated v3 / FOGRA51, PSO Uncoated v3 / FOGRA52, GRACoL2013 / CRPC6, SWOP2013 / CRPC5, Japan Color 2011). Rendering intent is relative colorimetric with BPC for vectors and brand colours and perceptual for out-of-gamut photos. Commands: magick -profile sRGB.icc -profile <CMYK>.icc, or Pillow ImageCms. Downloading ECI profiles needs permission.

Black and ink: rich black C60 M40 Y40 K100 for large areas, 100K only for small text and hairlines, never registration colour. Total ink 300-330% coated, 260-300% uncoated, ~240% newsprint. gs -o - -sDEVICE=inkcov gives page averages; use the tiffsep device or Acrobat Output Preview for maximum TAC.

Overprint and knockout: black text overprints, while white and light objects must never overprint. Simulate with Ghostscript -dOverprint=/simulate. Spot colours stay as Separation; dielines and varnish go on named spot layers set to overprint.
Fonts and fine detail: pdffonts must show emb=yes for all fonts, reversed text at least 8 pt, lines at least 0.25 pt, no RGB rich-black body text.
Boxes and marks: pdfinfo -box confirms TrimBox and BleedBox. Crop marks are offset at least the bleed outside the trim.

PDF/X export: X-4 preferred (live transparency, output intent), X-1a only when demanded (CMYK, flattened). Routes: design-tool export presets, Ghostscript with PDFX_def.ps (X-3 is reliable; confirm X-4 support in the installed version), HTML via WeasyPrint or Paged.js then conversion. qpdf --check for structure.

Preflight report table: size and boxes, ppi, colour spaces, fonts, TAC, overprint, spot list, with pass/fail. Final certification (callas pdfToolbox or Acrobat Preflight) is flagged as the printer's or the user's step.
Proofing: soft proof with a gamut warning, hard proof on the actual stock for brand-critical work, and expectations for dot gain on uncoated stock.

Worked example: an A5 flyer from HTML with bleed, CMYK conversion to PSO Coated v3, the full command checklist and the delivered PDF plus report. Pitfalls: missing bleed, web-resolution images, 4-colour small text, hairlines, Pantone values from auto-conversion.

skills.name: visual-accessibility-audit
skills.description: Accessibility in visual design: WCAG 2.2 contrast matrix for every text and UI pair, non-text and focus-indicator contrast, text over images with solved scrims, colour-vision-deficiency simulation, use of colour, target size, motion, forced colours and alt text, with APCA only as a second opinion. Load when designing or auditing visuals that must meet AA or AAA.
outline: WCAG 2.x luminance and contrast formula with the stdlib Python script, plus measured reference pairs (#767676 on white 4.54 passes, #777777 4.48 fails, #9CA3AF 2.54 fails) and the large-text threshold (24 px regular, 18.66 px bold).

Criteria table: 1.1.1, 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.6, 1.4.10, 1.4.11, 1.4.12, 2.3.1 (no more than three flashes per second), 2.4.7, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA), 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA), 2.5.8 Target Size 24x24 (AA).

Contrast matrix procedure: enumerate the pairs actually used (from tokens or by sampling screenshots), compute each, and record size, weight, target and pass/fail. Every failure gets a fix that moves OKLCH L at fixed hue and chroma.
Text over images: measure the worst point under the text box, not the average. Solve the scrim alpha from blended = a x scrim + (1 - a) x bg so that the worst pixel passes.

Non-text contrast: input borders, meaningful icons, chart marks and focus rings at 3:1 against adjacent colours. Focus indicator design: 2 px outline plus offset, contrasting with both the component and the page.

CVD simulation: Machado 2009 matrices (protan, deutan, tritan at severity 1.0) applied with NumPy on linear RGB, plus a grayscale pass. Categories must differ by at least 0.10-0.15 OKLCH L or carry labels or patterns.
Use of colour: redundant cues (icons for status, underlined links in body text, patterns in charts, text for errors).
Motion and forced colours: prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks, no parallax without opt-out, @media (forced-colors: active) using system colours, visible focus in Windows High Contrast.
Alt text: describe purpose, not appearance. Charts state the takeaway and link to data, decorative images use alt='', and complex images get a long description.
Automated checks for web: @axe-core/playwright or Lighthouse accessibility runs over rendered pages, with manual review for what automation misses (text over images, focus order).
APCA as an advisory second opinion only (roughly Lc 75 body, 60 large, 45 headlines and non-text). Never claim WCAG 3 conformance, because its contrast method is undecided.
Report template (pair, usage, size and weight, ratio, target, pass, fix). Worked example: a #E94560 CTA at 3.83:1 fixed to #D63151 (4.76:1), plus a CVD check of status chips.

skills.name: svg-hand-authoring
skills.description: Hand-written SVG craft for icons and illustrations: viewBox and coordinate maths, path grammar including arcs, primitives versus paths, generated geometry, stroke versus outlined fill, fill rules, symbols and sprites, gradients and clip paths with prefixed ids, CSS theming, lightweight animation, and accessible, safe embedding. Load when writing or editing SVG source directly instead of generating or tracing it.
outline: Coordinate system: viewBox maths, preserveAspectRatio, omitting width and height for responsive scaling, user units, and the effect of transforms on stroke width (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke).
Path grammar: M L H V C S Q T A Z in absolute and relative forms. Arc flags (large-arc, sweep) worked through, a circle as two arcs, rounded-rect and pill paths, and precision to 2 decimals.
Primitives versus paths: keep circle, rect and line where they read clearly, and convert to path only for booleans or when a toolchain needs it.
Generated geometry with stdlib Python: regular polygons and stars, points on arcs at given angles, rounded corners via arcs, grid snapping (.5 for odd strokes), and emitting d strings.

Strokes: linecap, linejoin and miterlimit rules, centred-only stroke alignment, and outlining strokes to fills when needed (picosvg, or inkscape --actions='select-all;object-stroke-to-path;export-filename:out.svg;export-do').
Fill rules: nonzero versus evenodd, and path direction for holes (counters in letters and rings).
Reuse: defs, symbol sprites with <use href='#id'> (SVG 2 href, with xlink:href only for legacy tools), and id prefixing to avoid collisions when inlined.
Paint: linear and radial gradients (objectBoundingBox versus userSpaceOnUse), patterns, clipPath versus mask, and filters used sparingly because of render cost and print issues.
Theming: currentColor, CSS custom properties inside inline SVG, and a prefers-color-scheme media query inside an SVG favicon.
Animation: CSS transforms with transform-box: fill-box and transform-origin, stroke-dasharray/dashoffset line drawing, limited SMIL, and a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.

Embedding and safety: inline versus img versus CSS background versus sprite trade-offs, role='img' with title and aria-labelledby or aria-hidden, and sanitising untrusted SVG with svgcheck sanitize. Validate with svgcheck check and render at two sizes (resvg, rsvg-convert or qlmanage).
Worked example: a 24-grid 'cloud-upload' icon hand-written with arcs, plus a small layered spot illustration using symbols and one gradient, both passing check --budget and the 32 px render test.

skills.name: layout-grids-posters-editorial
skills.description: Layout grids and composition for pages, screens, posters, editorial spreads and slides: column, modular and baseline grid math, spacing scales, responsive grids, hierarchy and squint tests, formats by viewing distance, editorial furniture, academic posters, 16:9 slides and HTML/Typst-to-PDF render-check loops. Load when composing or critiquing any layout.
outline: Column formula column = (W - 2M - (n-1)G)/n with worked cases (1440/12/G24/M72 = 86 px; 1080 social, 6 columns, G24, M60 = 140 px); snap margins for whole columns; grid-type decision table (manuscript, column, modular, baseline, hierarchical).
Modular and baseline grids: row height = k x leading with one leading between rows, fitting n rows in the text area, margins with inner smaller than outer for spreads (Van de Graaf as reference).
Spacing scale on a 4 or 8 base; space within a group at most half the space between groups; off-scale values are defects found by a regex audit script over CSS or exported specs.
Responsive: content-first breakpoints, 4/8/12 columns with 16-24/32/64-80 margins, CSS grid repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr)), subgrid for cross-card alignment, container queries vs media queries.

Hierarchy and composition: ranked levers (size, value contrast, position, isolation, weight, hue, motion), one focal point, Pillow blur squint test, Gestalt grouping before boxes, Z and F reading patterns, optical centre and 1-3% overshoot.
Grid-overlay verification: draw columns and baselines over a render (Pillow, or a CSS overlay in a Playwright screenshot) and Read it to confirm every edge lands on a line.

Posters: cap height ~ viewing distance/250-300, A-series and US sizes, 3-second test, headline of about 7 words, one dominant image, QR at least 2 cm with a 4-module quiet zone scan-tested at distance.

Editorial furniture and images: kicker, deck, byline, drop cap, pull quote, captions, folios, running heads, jump lines, 35-70 character measure; crop to the focal point, bleed vs boxed, captions adjacent, 300 ppi at final size.
Academic posters (3-4 column flow, body >= 24 pt at A0, title band) and slides (1920x1080 on 12 columns, 5% title-safe margin, body >= 24 pt, one idea and about 6 lines per slide).

Production and render-check loop: HTML/CSS @page via Paged.js or WeasyPrint, Typst #set page, hand-off notes for InDesign/Affinity, fonts embedded; export PDF, pdftoppm -r 100 -png, Read, score with the hub rubric, fix, repeat.

Pitfalls: everything centred or big, equal spacing everywhere, elements aligned to nothing, copy over busy image areas, crops cutting the focal point, QR too small, inconsistent caption styles, headline widows.
Worked examples: 1080x1350 webinar post on a 6-column grid (headline columns 1-5, bleeding image 3-6, CTA at the Z terminal); A2 event poster on a 6x8 modular grid with 14 pt baseline and a 25 mm QR.

skills.name: social-asset-kit
skills.description: Social and marketing asset sets with the image routers: a campaign matrix of placements and sizes, one master per idea derived by crop or outpaint, platform safe zones, typeset text and logo composited over generated art, contrast measured over pixels, batch naming and a manifest, and a kit QA sheet. Load when producing a multi-format campaign, ad set or launch kit.
outline: Kit matrix: rows are messages or variants, columns are placements. Placements: feed 4:5 1080x1350, square 1080, story/reel 9:16 1080x1920, profile-grid 3:4 crop, OG/link 1200x630, YouTube thumbnail 1280x720, IAB display 300x250, 728x90, 160x600, 320x50. Verify current platform specs with quick-researcher before launch.

Safe zones: stories lose ~14% at the top and ~20% at the bottom, feed posts must survive the 3:4 and 1:1 grid crops, and display ads need logo and CTA inside the frame. The union of all safe zones is computed in code to define the master's copy-safe box.

Master-first rule: generate one master at the widest aspect and highest resolution, then derive placements by Pillow crop or by image-editor outpaint (pad, flux-fill, composite). Never regenerate per format.

Generation: brief through image-brief-writing, route by need (nano-banana-2.1 for extreme ratios, flux-3 for photoreal), keep the seed fixed, and pass the accepted hero as a reference for every variant.

Text and logo are never baked into generation. An SVG or HTML template with slots {headline, sub, cta, logo} and brand fonts is rendered with resvg/rsvg-convert or a Playwright screenshot and composited over the art.

Contrast over pixels: sample the luminance under each text bounding box with Pillow, take the worst point, compute the WCAG ratio, and add a gradient scrim with alpha solved in code until the ratio reaches 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

Batch production: file names <campaign>_<message>_<placement>_<WxH>_v<n>.png, and a manifest CSV/JSON (file, size, copy, alt text, model, seed, references). Fan out per placement when there are more than 8 assets.
A/B variants change one variable at a time (headline, image or CTA colour), and the manifest records the variable.
Export: sRGB PNG or JPEG at quality 85-90, WebP/AVIF for web, ad file-size caps (IAB initial load about 150 KB), metadata stripped except provenance, and C2PA or platform AI labels where required.
QA contact sheet (imgcheck sheet of every asset) with a checklist: logo size and clear space, text legible at phone size, focal point crop-safe, palette consistent, no generation artefacts.
Worked example: a launch kit of 1 message x 6 placements from one 16:9 master, including two outpaints, one scrim fix (3.9 to 4.8:1), and the manifest and sheet delivered.

skills.name: photo-retouch-composite
skills.description: Photographic retouching and compositing with the image-edit router plus deterministic Pillow/NumPy steps: non-destructive step order, global tone and white balance, cleanup passes, colour and grain matching between plates, light, perspective and depth-of-field consistency, contact and cast shadows, product and portrait retouch limits, verified by diffs. Load when an edit or composite must look photographically real.
outline: Step order: assess, global tone and white balance, cleanup (dust, distractions), local dodge and burn, composite, final grade, output sharpen, then upscale last. Every step is numbered and logged in steps.jsonl per image-editing ground rules.

Deterministic global corrections in NumPy/Pillow, preferred over model edits so nothing drifts: percentile levels (0.5/99.5 clip), white balance from a picked neutral or gray-world, gamma and curves via a LUT, unsharp mask sized to the output (radius ~0.5-1 px at screen size).
Cleanup with the router: tight masks grown by max(8, 0.015 s), flux-fill with fill-content instructions, then composite back and check containment with masktool diff (outside MAE ≤ 0.5, inside ≥ 2).

Plate-matching checklist: light direction and hardness, colour temperature, black and white points, horizon line and camera height (perspective), scale against known objects, depth of field (Gaussian blur matched to the background plane), noise and grain.
Colour transfer: Reinhard mean/std matching in OKLab or Lab restricted to masked regions (NumPy snippet), then a local tweak. Histograms are compared before and after.
Grain matching: measure the high-pass standard deviation in flat areas of each plate and add matched Gaussian or luminance grain to the cleaner plate, so pasted elements do not look pasted on.

Shadows and reflections: a contact shadow from the subject alpha (squashed, blurred, multiplied at 30-60%), a cast shadow along the scene's light direction, and a flipped, faded reflection for glossy surfaces. Optional router harmonise pass followed by a containment check on the subject alpha.
Cutout quality: BiRefNet Matting via provider_run for hair and fur, then defringe (split-alpha, grow -1, feather 0.8, merge) and inspect on black and white backgrounds.

Product retouch: straighten labels, remove dust and seams, make backgrounds exactly white for marketplaces (255,255,255 verified by pixel scan, product filling ~85% of the frame), keep colour accuracy against a reference swatch.

Portrait limits and disclosure: keep skin texture (no plastic smoothing), no identity, body or age changes without stated consent, and note jurisdictional labelling rules (for example France's 'photographie retouchée' rule for altered body images in ads).

Worked example: a product cutout placed into a generated lifestyle scene. Colour transfer, contact shadow, grain match and a harmonise pass, then diff and sheet verification, with steps.jsonl delivered.

Failure table: halos (defringe), floating objects (contact shadow), mismatched sharpness (blur or sharpen per plate), plastic skin (reduce strength, restore texture), repeated cleanup textures (two smaller passes).

skills.name: image-brief-writing
skills.description: Art-direction briefs for image models: structured YAML brief fields, compiling to a ranked prose prompt, capability-based routing, reference roles, copy-safe zones, placement presets, genre templates, edit briefs, a 12-point review sheet and provenance. Load when directing image-generator, image-editor or vector-artist, or when writing image prompts yourself.
outline: Structured YAML brief fields: id, purpose, placement, subject, composition, style, light, palette, text_in_image, exclusions, technical, references and acceptance, with the webinar-hero example.

Compile rules: order (subject, setting, composition, style, light, palette, mood, exclusions), numeric positions and empty areas, hex palette with roles and background value, exclusions phrased positively plus one short 'no ...', exact quoted text of at most ~5 words, reference roles by position, no living artists or trademarks, under ~120 words.

Capability, not model: state the needed capability (exact text, RGBA, N references, extreme ratio) and let config/image-models.json routing pick. Run an image_providers preflight before promising a model.
Placement presets table (aspect, pixels, safe-area notes) for feed, story, square, OG, slide, web hero, A-series print and banners. Generate at native resolution, edit, then upscale last.
