Genre templates: product on seamless, editorial portrait (fictional person), isometric illustration, flat spot illustration or icon (vector route), logo exploration (vector-only directions), abstract background for text, seamless pattern (2x2 tile test with a half-offset seam fix), transparent cutout.

Photography and lighting vocabulary that moves results: shot sizes, lens mm and aperture look, lighting setups (Rembrandt, butterfly, rim, softbox key with fill card), time of day, colour-grade terms.
Edit briefs: a defect-to-operation table (masked local fix, recolour, outpaint, background swap, upscale, vectorise). Every instruction says what changes and what must stay identical.
Review sheet: 6 checks scored 0-2, accept at 9/12 or above with no 0 on subject or artefacts, plus a common failure-to-fix table (busy copy area, colour drift, style inconsistency, misspelled text).
Variant strategy: explore with n=4 without a seed, fix the seed of the best, change one factor per round, stop after 3 rounds without gain and name the capability gap.

Provenance and rights: sidecar fields (brief id, compiled prompt, alias and target, seed, references with roles, licence, reviewer score), disclosure, and no real-person likeness or generated real logos.
Worked example: the webinar hero taken from YAML brief to compiled prompt to image_generate JSON call (aspect 4:5, n 4, seed), review scores and the edit brief for the one defect.

skills.name: inequality-proving
skills.description: Proves, sharpens and machine-checks inequalities: catalogue of classical inequalities with hypotheses and equality cases, choosing a technique from the equality case, SOS and Schur/Muirhead, uvw/pqr, tangent-line trick, smoothing, Lagrange multipliers with boundary checks, and rigorous interval/SOS certificates. Load for any bound, estimate or inequality proof.
outline: Workflow: check homogeneity, normalise, find equality cases numerically (multistart minimisation of LHS - RHS), then choose a technique from where equality sits (symmetric interior point vs boundary)

Full catalogue moved from references/inequalities.md: means and convexity (power mean, weighted AM-GM, Young, Jensen, Karamata, Hermite-Hadamard, Schur) and sums (Cauchy-Schwarz, Engel/Titu, Holder, Minkowski, Chebyshev, rearrangement, Abel summation), each with hypotheses and equality case
Elementary-function and combinatorial estimates (e^x >= 1 + x, log bounds, Jordan, Stirling, binomial and entropy bounds, harmonic numbers, integral comparison), with domains stated

SOS method: write the difference as sum S_ij (x_i - x_j)^2, SOS-Schur criteria; machine search for SOS certificates via an SDP (CVXPY or SumOfSquares.jl), then round the certificate to exact rationals
Symmetric-polynomial tools: Muirhead (majorisation of exponent vectors), Schur of degree t, uvw/pqr for three variables (fix p and q, extremise over r, so two variables are equal or one is zero)
Tangent-line trick and SOS-tangent for sum f(x_i) with fixed sum x_i; smoothing/mixing variables, and when smoothing keeps the constraint
Calculus route: Lagrange multipliers with every boundary piece and non-smooth point checked; second-order condition; convexity in one variable at a time
Matrix and functional inequalities moved with their hypotheses: Rayleigh, Weyl, Hadamard, norm equivalences, Poincare, Wirtinger, Gronwall

Rigorous verification: interval branch-and-bound over boxes (mpmath.iv, python-flint arb) with box counts reported; exact rational spot checks at the equality case; short formal checks with Lean nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a - b), ...], positivity and gcongr

Pitfalls: multiplying by a quantity of unknown sign, treating cyclic inequalities as symmetric for a WLOG ordering, AM-GM missing equality that only happens on the boundary, using non-homogeneous constraints after scaling
Worked example: Nesbitt a/(b+c) + b/(c+a) + c/(a+b) >= 3/2 via the Engel form of Cauchy-Schwarz and a^2+b^2+c^2 >= ab+bc+ca; equality at a = b = c; checked by an SOS certificate and interval sampling

skills.name: matrix-decompositions-conditioning
skills.description: Numerical linear algebra in practice: choosing LU, Cholesky, QR, SVD, eigh or Schur for a task, with the SciPy/NumPy/Julia call; conditioning and digit loss, residual checks for backward stability, least squares and rank decisions, perturbation bounds, iterative sparse solvers and preconditioning. Load when solving, factorising or trusting a matrix computation.
outline: Decision table from task to factorisation to call: SPD solve -> Cholesky (scipy.linalg.cho_factor/cho_solve); general square -> LU with partial pivoting (lu_factor); least squares -> QR or SVD (lstsq, lapack_driver='gelsd'); symmetric eigenproblem -> eigh; general -> eig/schur; rank and null space -> SVD with a tolerance; matrix functions -> expm/logm/sqrtm
Rules: never form A^-1 to solve a system; never form A^T A when kappa is large (kappa(A^T A) = kappa^2); use slogdet instead of det; reuse one factorisation across right-hand sides

Conditioning: kappa_2 = sigma_max/sigma_min costs about log10(kappa) digits; numpy.linalg.cond and cheap 1-norm estimates (LAPACK gecon, onenormest); Hilbert H12 worked example (kappa ~ 1.7e16): tiny residual, wrong answer
Backward error and stability: relative residual ||b - A x|| / (||A|| ||x||) compared with unit roundoff; forward error <= kappa x backward error; iterative refinement in mixed precision
Rank-deficient and ill-posed problems: numerical rank with tol = sigma_max * max(m,n) * eps (the numpy default), truncated SVD, pivoted QR, Tikhonov/ridge with the L-curve or cross-validation

Trusting eigenvalues: symmetric eigenvalues are well conditioned (Weyl), non-normal ones are not (Bauer-Fike, pseudospectra); eigenvectors need a spectral gap (Davis-Kahan sin theta; Wedin for singular vectors), each with hypotheses

Structural facts and identities moved from references/linear-algebra-analysis.md: rank facts; existence of spectral, Schur, Jordan, polar and SVD forms; Courant-Fischer; interlacing; Gershgorin; Perron-Frobenius; definiteness tests (Sylvester's leading minors for PD only, all principal minors for PSD); Schur complement; Woodbury; Sherman-Morrison; determinant lemma; matrix calculus

Sparse and iterative solvers: CG (SPD; iterations grow like sqrt(kappa)), MINRES (symmetric indefinite), restarted GMRES and BiCGSTAB (general); preconditioners ILU (spilu), AMG (pyamg), Jacobi; eigsh with shift-invert; LOBPCG; stop on relative residual
Large and low-rank matrices: randomized SVD (sklearn randomized_svd with oversampling about 10 and power iterations), Nystrom, Eckart-Young bound on truncation error
Exact and high-precision routes: SymPy or python-flint fmpq_mat for exact rank and determinants; mpmath matrices for reference solutions
Performance: BLAS/LAPACK threading (threadpoolctl), float32 vs float64 trade-off, GPU via torch.linalg or CuPy, batched solves, Julia factorize(A) dispatch
Worked example: degree-15 least-squares polynomial fit with a monomial Vandermonde matrix (kappa explodes) vs a Chebyshev basis with QR; digit loss predicted, then measured

skills.name: probability-distributions-limits
skills.description: Probability calculations and limit theorems: distribution facts and relationships, expectation via indicators and conditioning, transformations, modes of convergence, LLN/CLT/delta method with their conditions, choosing a concentration or tail bound, martingales and optional stopping, Markov chains, plus seeded Monte Carlo checks. Load for any probability derivation or bound.
outline: Distribution reference table: Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, geometric, negative binomial, hypergeometric, uniform, normal, exponential, gamma, beta, chi-square, Student t, Cauchy, lognormal, Pareto, multivariate normal, each with mean, variance, MGF/characteristic function and parametrisation traps (scale vs rate; scipy.stats loc/scale conventions)
Relationships: a sum of independent exponentials is gamma; Poisson limit of the binomial; normal approximations and when they fail (np < 10); beta-binomial; ratios giving t and F; memorylessness
Expectation toolkit: linearity with indicators (no independence needed), laws of total expectation and total variance, the tower property, symmetry arguments, the tail-sum formula E X = sum P(X >= k)
Transformations: change of variables with the Jacobian, order statistics, convolution, sums of a random number of terms (Wald), uniqueness of the moment generating function

Modes of convergence (almost sure, in probability, L^p, in distribution) with the implication diagram and counterexamples; Slutsky and the continuous mapping theorem; delta method for the variance of a function of an estimator
LLN and CLT with conditions (finite mean or variance, i.i.d. or Lindeberg), Berry-Esseen rate, failure under heavy tails (Cauchy, Pareto alpha <= 2), Borel-Cantelli in both directions

Tail-bound selection table moved from the inequalities reference: Markov, Chebyshev, Cantelli, multiplicative Chernoff, Hoeffding, Bernstein, Azuma, McDiarmid, Paley-Zygmund, and when each is tightest

Martingales: how to construct one, conditions for the optional stopping theorem (bounded stopping time, or bounded increments with E tau < infinity), gambler's ruin probabilities and durations as worked derivations
Markov chains: stationary distribution from pi P = pi, reversibility and detailed balance, hitting times and absorption probabilities as linear systems (numpy), mixing time and coupling bounds
Paradoxes and pitfalls: uncorrelated is not independent, Simpson's paradox, the inspection (waiting-time) paradox, Bertrand's ambiguity, conditioning on measure-zero events, base-rate neglect
Simulation check protocol: numpy.random.default_rng(seed), N chosen from the target CI width, report estimate +- 1.96 s/sqrt(N), exact enumeration for small discrete cases
Worked example: coupon collector, E T = n H_n, Var T <= pi^2 n^2 / 6, P(T > n ln n + c n) <= e^(-c) by the union bound; checked by simulation for n = 50

skills.name: statistical-inference-bayesian
skills.description: Applied statistical inference for engineering and research data: estimators and confidence intervals (Wilson, bootstrap), choosing a test, power and sample size, multiple comparisons, A/B tests and benchmark comparisons, regression with robust errors, and the Bayesian workflow with PyMC/NumPyro/Stan and ArviZ diagnostics. Load when data must support a claim or an experiment must be designed.
outline: Start from the estimand and the design: unit of randomisation, independence assumptions, paired vs unpaired, fixed horizon vs sequential; decision table from question to method to the scipy.stats or statsmodels call
Estimators: bias, variance, MSE, consistency, MLE asymptotics with Fisher information, the Cramer-Rao bound; standard errors via the delta method or the bootstrap

Intervals: Wilson or Clopper-Pearson for proportions (statsmodels proportion_confint), never Wald at small n or extreme p; t-intervals; scipy.stats.bootstrap (BCa), and where the bootstrap fails (heavy tails, extremes, dependent data, which needs a block bootstrap)

Choosing a test: Welch's t-test by default rather than Student's, Mann-Whitney or Brunner-Munzel, chi-square vs Fisher exact, permutation_test for any statistic, paired tests; assumptions to check and effect sizes to report alongside p-values
Power and sample size: statsmodels.stats.power, Lehr's rule n ~ 16 sigma^2 / delta^2 per arm (80% power, alpha = 0.05), minimum detectable effect, simulation-based power for complex designs
Multiple comparisons: Bonferroni and Holm (family-wise error), Benjamini-Hochberg (scipy.stats.false_discovery_control), pre-registering the primary metric, the garden-of-forking-paths warning

A/B testing pitfalls: peeking without a sequential correction (use always-valid/mSPRT or group-sequential boundaries), sample-ratio-mismatch chi-square check, CUPED variance reduction, novelty effects, ratio metrics needing the delta method

Comparing performance benchmarks: many runs, warm-up, median with a bootstrap CI, Mann-Whitney or Hodges-Lehmann shift, noise floor from A/A runs; complements performance-optimization without repeating it
Regression: OLS assumptions, the statsmodels formula API, heteroskedasticity-robust (HC3) and clustered standard errors, multicollinearity (VIF), residual diagnostics, confounding vs causation

Bayesian workflow: conjugate updates (Beta-Binomial, Gamma-Poisson, Normal-Normal) for quick answers; PyMC 5, NumPyro or CmdStanPy otherwise; prior predictive check, NUTS fit, then R-hat <= 1.01, bulk/tail ESS >= 400 and zero divergences (ArviZ az.summary), posterior predictive check, prior sensitivity; simulation-based calibration for new models
Reporting: effect size with an interval, the exact test and its assumptions, the number of comparisons; Bayes factors only with a prior-sensitivity analysis; never conclude 'p > 0.05, so no effect'

Worked example: conversions 120/2400 vs 150/2400; Wilson intervals; two-proportion z ~ 1.88 (p ~ 0.06); Beta(1,1) posteriors give P(B > A) ~ 0.97; why both are reported and which decision rule applies

skills.name: combinatorics-generating-functions
skills.description: Counting and enumeration: the twelvefold way, bijections, inclusion-exclusion, ordinary and exponential generating functions with the symbolic method, recurrences to closed forms, Lagrange inversion, transfer matrices, Burnside/Polya, and coefficient asymptotics via singularity analysis, cross-checked by brute force and OEIS. Load for any count, recurrence or enumeration identity.
outline: Twelvefold-way table (balls labelled or not, boxes labelled or not; any, injective or surjective maps) with formulas in binomials, Stirling numbers of the second kind and partitions
Bijective and double-counting proofs of identities (Vandermonde, hockey stick, Catalan via the ballot problem and reflection), with an explicit check of the inverse map
Inclusion-exclusion and Mobius inversion on posets: derangements, surjections, Euler phi, deletion-contraction for the chromatic polynomial
Generating-function dictionary: OGF vs EGF (unlabelled vs labelled), operations (shift, derivative, convolution, binomial convolution), extracting coefficients with SymPy series
Symbolic method (Flajolet-Sedgewick): SEQ, SET, MSET and CYC constructions translated to OGF/EGF equations; worked examples on trees and compositions

Linear recurrences: characteristic polynomial, repeated roots, rational GF via partial fractions (sympy.apart, rsolve); guessing a recurrence from data (sympy find_linear_recurrence, guess_generating_function_rational), then proving it
Lagrange inversion for implicitly defined GFs: Catalan numbers, labelled trees n^(n-2), plane trees
Transfer-matrix method for words avoiding patterns and for tilings; the dominant eigenvalue gives the growth rate
Counting under symmetry: Burnside's lemma and the Polya cycle index for colourings of necklaces and cubes, with the group written out explicitly

Coefficient asymptotics: dominant singularity, [z^n](1 - z/rho)^(-alpha) ~ rho^(-n) n^(alpha-1) / Gamma(alpha), saddle point for entire GFs, Stirling and Hardy-Ramanujan partition asymptotics; ratio checks against exact terms
Verification: brute-force enumeration (itertools) for small n, OEIS lookup of the first 10-20 terms with the A-number cited, SageMath when available
Worked example: binary strings of length n with no '11'; transfer matrix, OGF (1 + z)/(1 - z - z^2), count F_(n+2), growth phi^n, brute-force check for n <= 20, OEIS A000045

skills.name: number-theory-modular
skills.description: Elementary and computational number theory: divisibility and Bezout, modular arithmetic, CRT, Euler/Fermat/Carmichael, orders and primitive roots, quadratic residues and square roots mod n, p-adic valuations and LTE, Diophantine techniques, multiplicative functions, primality and factoring tools, and pitfalls when implementing them. Load for congruences, integer equations or modular-arithmetic code.
outline: Core facts with hypotheses: Bezout and the extended Euclidean algorithm, CRT (pairwise coprime moduli; a consistency condition otherwise), Fermat, Euler phi, Carmichael lambda, Wilson, ord_n(a) divides phi(n), primitive roots exist exactly for 1, 2, 4, p^k and 2p^k
Quadratic residues: Euler's criterion, Legendre and Jacobi symbols, quadratic reciprocity with its supplements, Tonelli-Shanks and Cipolla for square roots mod p, Hensel lifting to p^k
Valuations: Legendre's formula for v_p(n!), Kummer's theorem, Lucas' theorem for binomials mod p, the lifting-the-exponent lemma with its exact conditions (p = 2 handled separately)
Diophantine techniques: modular obstructions, factoring over Z[i] or Z[sqrt d], infinite descent, Vieta jumping, Pell equations via continued fractions, bounding followed by finite search

Multiplicative functions: Dirichlet convolution, Mobius inversion, identities for sigma, tau and phi, summatory estimates; analytic facts to cite with precise statements (PNT, Mertens, Dirichlet's theorem)

Python and library calls: pow(a, -1, m), math.gcd/lcm/isqrt, sympy.ntheory (factorint, isprime, primitive_root, n_order, discrete_log, sqrt_mod, crt, jacobi_symbol, totient), gmpy2 for speed, PARI/GP and SageMath for heavy work, LMFDB for lookups

Primality and factoring: trial-division bounds, Miller-Rabin with deterministic base sets for n < 2^64, BPSW, Carmichael numbers that fool Fermat tests, the scale where Pollard rho and ECM work, when to stop and use a CAS

Implementation pitfalls: sign of % on negative numbers in C/C++/Java/Go/Rust vs Python, overflow in a*b mod m (use 128-bit or Montgomery multiplication), modulo bias when reducing random numbers, non-constant-time modular exponentiation in crypto code
Discrete log and order finding as computational problems (baby-step giant-step, Pohlig-Hellman), and their link to Shor's algorithm for quantum-computing questions
Verification: exhaustive checks over residues for small moduli, random large tests with gmpy2, exact integer arithmetic only
Worked example: LTE gives v_3(2^(3^k) + 1) = k + 1 (p = 3 divides 2 - (-1), p divides neither base, n = 3^k is odd); conditions checked, then verified for k <= 30 with exact integers

skills.name: real-complex-analysis
skills.description: Rigorous real and complex analysis: epsilon-delta templates, convergence tests, uniform convergence and limit-interchange theorems with their hypotheses, measure-theoretic convergence theorems, a counterexample catalogue, asymptotic expansions (Laplace, Euler-Maclaurin, Watson, saddle point), and contour integration with residues and branch cuts. Load for limits, series, integrals or analytic estimates.
outline: Epsilon-delta and epsilon-N templates with an explicit choice of delta and stated dependencies of constants; negating uniform vs pointwise statements; standard estimates (splitting with the triangle inequality, the epsilon/3 argument)

Decision table for series convergence: comparison, limit comparison, ratio, root, integral test, alternating/Leibniz, Dirichlet and Abel tests, Cauchy condensation; absolute vs conditional convergence and Riemann rearrangement
Uniform convergence: Weierstrass M-test, Dini, Arzela-Ascoli, conditions for term-by-term differentiation and integration; facts table moved from references/linear-algebra-analysis.md section 2

Interchange theorems with hypotheses: monotone and dominated convergence, Fatou, Fubini/Tonelli, the Leibniz rule (differentiating under the integral), change of variables; how to find a dominating function

Counterexample catalogue, moved and extended: n * 1_(0,1/n), Fubini failure for (x^2 - y^2)/(x^2 + y^2)^2, x^2 sin(1/x), the Cantor function, the Weierstrass function, rearrangements of conditionally convergent series
Taylor's theorem with Lagrange and integral remainders; bounding the remainder to get a rigorous numerical error; analytic vs C-infinity (e^(-1/x^2))

Asymptotic methods: algebra of O, o and ~; Euler-Maclaurin for sums (H_n, log n!); Laplace's method and Watson's lemma for integrals; stationary phase; saddle point; divergent asymptotic series and optimal truncation

Complex-analysis facts with hypotheses (moved from section 4): Cauchy's theorem and integral formula, the residue theorem, Liouville, maximum modulus, the identity theorem, the argument principle, Rouche for counting zeros

Contour integration recipe: choose the contour (semicircle, rectangle, keyhole, indented); justify vanishing arcs (Jordan's lemma, ML-inequality); residue formulas (g/h' at a simple pole, order-m formula); branch cuts and principal branches consistent with numpy/SymPy conventions
Check every evaluated integral or sum numerically with mpmath.quad or nsum at two precisions
Worked example: integral over the real line of cos x/(1 + x^2) = pi/e via e^(iz)/(1 + z^2) on the upper semicircle, Jordan's lemma justified, checked with mpmath to 30 digits

skills.name: ode-pde-analytic-methods
skills.description: Closed-form and qualitative methods for ODEs and PDEs: first-order techniques, linear constant-coefficient and Cauchy-Euler equations, series/Frobenius, Laplace transforms, linear systems via matrix exponentials, existence/uniqueness and stability (phase plane, Lyapunov), Sturm-Liouville and Green's functions, separation of variables, Fourier methods, characteristics and similarity solutions, verified with SymPy and numerical solves. Load when an ODE or PDE needs an analytic solution or a qualitative guarantee.
outline: Table from equation form to method: separable, first-order linear (integrating factor), exact or made exact by an integrating factor, Bernoulli, homogeneous, Riccati with a known solution, autonomous (quadrature)

Linear constant-coefficient and Cauchy-Euler equations: characteristic roots including repeated and complex ones, undetermined coefficients with the resonance rule, variation of parameters via the Wronskian
Power series and Frobenius at regular singular points (indicial equation, roots differing by an integer); recognising Bessel, Legendre, Airy and hypergeometric forms and citing DLMF
Laplace transform for IVPs with discontinuous or impulsive forcing (Heaviside, Dirac), transfer functions, partial fractions with sympy.apart and inverse_laplace_transform
Linear systems x' = Ax + f: eigendecomposition, Jordan blocks, expm, Duhamel's formula, fundamental matrices
Existence and uniqueness: Picard-Lindelof (Lipschitz) vs Peano; non-uniqueness for y' = sqrt(y); finite-time blow-up for y' = y^2; Gronwall for continuous dependence

Qualitative analysis: equilibria, linearisation and Hartman-Grobman (hyperbolic points only), trace-determinant classification, Lyapunov functions, LaSalle, limit cycles (Poincare-Bendixson), basic bifurcations (saddle-node, pitchfork, Hopf)
Boundary value problems: Sturm-Liouville eigenvalues and orthogonality, eigenfunction expansions, Green's functions with jump conditions, the Fredholm alternative

PDEs: classification (elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic) and well-posedness; separation of variables, where the boundary conditions decide the eigenfunctions; Fourier-series convergence and Gibbs; Fourier/Laplace transforms on unbounded domains; d'Alembert
First-order PDEs by characteristics, shock formation and Rankine-Hugoniot; similarity solutions (heat kernel); maximum principle and energy methods for uniqueness

Verification: sympy dsolve with hints and checkodesol; pdsolve for first-order linear PDEs; substitute back into the equation and boundary conditions; compare with scipy solve_ivp or a fine-grid numerical solution (integrator choice stays in physics-toolkit)
Worked example: heat equation u_t = k u_xx on [0, L] with u = 0 at both ends and u(x,0) = x(L - x); coefficients 8L^2/(n^3 pi^3) for odd n, decay rates, a truncation error bound and a numerical check

skills.name: numerical-error-analysis
skills.description: Error analysis for floating-point arithmetic and numerical methods: unit roundoff and error models, conditioning vs stability, cancellation and stable rewrites, accurate summation, root finding, quadrature, interpolation and step choice for differentiation, convergence studies, and tolerance-aware tests for numerical code. Load when a computed number must be trusted or a numerical bug is suspected.
outline: Floating-point model: fl(a op b) = (a op b)(1 + delta) with |delta| <= u; u = 2^-53 (binary64), 2^-24 (binary32), 2^-8 (bfloat16), 2^-11 (fp16); subnormals, signed zeros, NaN propagation, FMA and platform differences, -ffast-math hazards
Conditioning vs stability: relative condition number kappa_f(x) = |x f'(x)/f(x)|; forward error is at most about kappa x backward error; working out which of the two is the problem

Cancellation catalogue and stable rewrites: log1p, expm1, hypot, the quadratic formula with the sign trick, 1 - cos x = 2 sin^2(x/2), logsumexp and shifted softmax, Welford or two-pass variance, rationalising sqrt(x+1) - sqrt(x); Herbie for automated rewriting
Summation and reductions: pairwise (numpy), Kahan/Neumaier compensated summation, math.fsum with exact rounding, order dependence in parallel reductions and GPU atomics

Root finding: bisection, Newton (quadratic convergence; only linear at multiple roots), secant, Brent (scipy.optimize.brentq/root_scalar); bracketing, stopping criteria on both |f| and step size, conditioning of a root

Quadrature: scipy.integrate.quad with points/weight for singularities and oscillation, Gauss-Legendre vs Clenshaw-Curtis, tanh-sinh (mpmath.quad) for endpoint singularities, infinite ranges by substitution; reported error estimates are not bounds
Interpolation and approximation: Runge's phenomenon, Chebyshev nodes and barycentric interpolation, Chebyshev coefficient decay as an accuracy diagnostic, splines, minimax vs least squares

Numerical differentiation: forward-difference step ~ sqrt(eps) |x|, central ~ eps^(1/3) |x|, complex-step derivative Im f(x + ih)/h accurate to roundoff, automatic differentiation (JAX) as the default when available

Convergence studies: run at h, h/2 and h/4, compute the observed order p, apply Richardson extrapolation for an error estimate; keep discretisation, statistical and roundoff errors separate (ODE/PDE integrator details stay in physics-toolkit)
Reference values: mpmath at 50+ digits, interval/ball arithmetic (python-flint arb) for rigorous enclosures, comparison at two precisions

Testing numerical code: numpy.testing.assert_allclose with a justified rtol/atol, ULP distance via np.spacing, never ==, property tests over input ranges including tiny, huge, negative and subnormal values, determinism across BLAS thread counts
Worked example: sample variance of [1e9+4, 1e9+7, 1e9+13, 1e9+16] via E[x^2] - E[x]^2 vs Welford; the error model explains the catastrophic cancellation and the correct value 30 is recovered

skills.name: optimization-convex-nonconvex
skills.description: Formulating and solving optimisation problems: classifying the problem and choosing a solver (LP/QP/SOCP/SDP/MILP/NLP/black-box), convexity checks and DCP modelling in CVXPY or JuMP, KKT with constraint qualifications, duality certificates, first-order rates, local NLP solvers and gradient checks, global and combinatorial methods, and verifying solutions. Load when anything is minimised, fitted or scheduled.
outline: Classification table from problem form to class to solvers: LP/MILP (HiGHS, OR-Tools, Gurobi), QP (OSQP, Clarabel), SOCP/SDP (Clarabel, SCS, MOSEK), smooth NLP (IPOPT, scipy trust-constr/SLSQP), bound-constrained (L-BFGS-B), combinatorial (CP-SAT), expensive black-box (Optuna, BoTorch)

Recognising convexity: Hessian PSD tests, composition rules, perspective and Schur-complement tricks, common reformulations (abs, max, norms, ratios, log-sum-exp, geometric programs); CVXPY DCP/DGP/DPP errors and how to fix them

CVXPY practice: Parameters for repeated solves, prob.status (optimal vs optimal_inaccurate vs infeasible/unbounded), constraint dual_value, data scaling, solver tolerances; JuMP equivalents (is_solved_and_feasible, dual)

Optimality conditions: KKT (stationarity, primal and dual feasibility, complementary slackness), when they are necessary (Slater, LICQ, MFCQ) and when sufficient (convexity); second-order conditions for nonconvex local minima
Duality: Lagrangian dual, weak and strong duality, the duality gap as an optimality certificate, Farkas certificates of infeasibility, LP sensitivity from the duals

First-order methods and rates: gradient descent with step 1/L at O(1/k), Nesterov at O(1/k^2), linear rate under strong convexity (condition number L/mu), SGD at O(1/sqrt(k)), proximal gradient, ADMM; diagnosing divergence from the step size

Nonconvex local optimisation: choosing a scipy.optimize.minimize method, supplying exact gradients (JAX/autograd), checking gradients with scipy.optimize.check_grad or finite differences, scaling variables, multiple starts

Global and discrete: multistart, differential_evolution, dual_annealing, shgo, basin hopping; big-M pitfalls in MILP and tight formulations; branch-and-bound gaps as certificates; SOS/SDP relaxations for polynomial problems
Verifying any returned optimum: feasibility residuals, KKT residuals, duality gap, comparison with a perturbed restart, objective vs a known bound or relaxation

Pitfalls: a nonconvex problem fed to a convex solver, unscaled data, equality constraints with redundant rows, integer variables silently relaxed, optimal_inaccurate treated as optimal, a local minimum reported as global

Worked example: long-only minimum-variance portfolio as a CVXPY QP; duals read off; KKT residuals and duality gap below 1e-8; compared with the closed form when the nonnegativity constraints are inactive

skills.name: sympy-symbolic-verification
skills.description: SymPy for derivations and verification: assumptions, simplification strategies, solveset/nonlinsolve/rsolve/dsolve, calculus and series, exact linear algebra, lambdify and code generation, a rigorous protocol for checking identities, plus mpmath high precision and PSLQ, interval/ball arithmetic, and Z3 for finite or real-arithmetic checks. Load when deriving, simplifying or machine-checking a formula.
outline: Isolated environment (uv venv with sympy, mpmath, python-flint, z3-solver) and pinned versions; SymPy >= 1.13 behaviour to know about
Assumptions: symbols(positive=True, integer=True, real=True), refine and Q/ask, why sqrt(x**2) does not simplify to x without them; matching the CAS assumptions to the problem's domain

Simplification toolbox and when each applies: expand, factor, cancel, apart, together, trigsimp, powsimp/logcombine (force=True is unsound off the positive reals), radsimp, and nsimplify as a guess only
Solving: solveset vs solve (complete solution sets, ConditionSet), linsolve, nonlinsolve, Groebner bases (groebner) for polynomial systems, rsolve for recurrences, dsolve with checkodesol
Calculus: limit with a direction, series with O-terms, integrate checked by differentiating back, Sum/Product with doit, handling Piecewise results and convergence conditions
Exact linear algebra: Matrix with Rational entries, rref, nullspace, charpoly, DomainMatrix for speed; avoid symbolic matrices for floating-point data

Identity-checking protocol: simplify(a - b) == 0 proves the identity under the declared assumptions; a False result proves nothing; .equals may return None; substitute exact random rationals; for rational functions, evaluating on a degree-bounded grid is a proof (Schwartz-Zippel otherwise, labelled probabilistic)
Code generation: lambdify with numpy or jax modules, cse for common subexpressions, ccode/fcode, numerical comparison of the generated code against the symbolic expression
Performance: expression swell; use Poly and polys domains (QQ, ZZ); avoid simplify inside loops; set timeouts for integrate
High precision and constant recognition (moved): mpmath mp.dps at two precisions, nsum/quad, identify and pslq, reported as numerical evidence

Rigorous numerics and solvers (moved): mpmath.iv and python-flint arb enclosures, interval bisection proofs of inequalities on boxes; Z3 for bounded integer and nonlinear real arithmetic, treating unknown as unknown; the one-liner for OEIS JSON lookup
Worked example: derive sum_{k=1}^n k^3 = (n(n+1)/2)^2 with summation; prove it by checking the degree-4 polynomial difference at 5 exact points; emit a lambdified version tested against brute force

skills.name: lean4-mathlib-formalization
skills.description: Formal proofs in Lean 4 with Mathlib: project setup with lake and the Mathlib cache, faithful formalisation of statements (coercions, truncated subtraction, division conventions), choosing a tactic by goal shape, finding lemmas (exact?, Loogle, LeanSearch), structuring proofs, reading errors, and checking axioms. Load when a proof should be machine-checked or a Lean file must compile.
outline: Setup: elan toolchain, 'lake new proj math', 'lake exe cache get' before the first build, 'lake build' or 'lake env lean File.lean', a pinned lean-toolchain, and deliberate Mathlib updates with 'lake update'

Faithful statements: truncated subtraction and floor division on N, x / 0 = 0 in fields, junk values of Real.sqrt and Real.log, coercions between N/Z/Q/R (push_cast, norm_cast), Finset.range n = {0, ..., n-1}, the 'sum i in s' notation (written with the element-of symbol); re-read the formal statement against the informal one

Tactic decision table by goal shape: norm_num, decide, omega, linarith, nlinarith [hint terms], positivity, ring, field_simp then ring, gcongr, bound, simp/simp?, aesop, grind, fun_prop, continuity/measurability
Finding lemmas: exact?, apply?, rw?; Mathlib naming conventions (mul_comm, _of_, _iff_, _le_, le_ vs lt_); Loogle pattern queries; LeanSearch natural-language search; #check and go-to-definition
Proof structure: have, obtain <x, hx>, rcases, rintro, calc chains, induction ... with, Finset.induction_on, cases, by_contra, push_neg, contrapose!, refine with ?_ holes, conv for targeted rewriting
Sorry-driven development: a skeleton with one sorry per lemma, close the leaves first, keep each lemma small; never leave a sorry in a reported result
Reading errors: type mismatches from coercions, 'failed to synthesize instance', 'motive is not type correct', deterministic timeouts and maxHeartbeats, simp loops; the fix for each
Trust check: #print axioms should show only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; native_decide adds Lean.ofReduceBool (say so); grep for sorry/admit; CI via the exit status of lake build
Scope: formalise the crux lemma, not the whole paper; when a statement needs Mathlib infrastructure that doesn't exist, report it as an Open doubt rather than adding an axiom
AI-assisted proving: accept LLM or tactic-search output only after it compiles; watch for statement drift, where the proved theorem differs from the intended one
Worked example: sum over i < n of (2i + 1) = n^2 by induction with Finset.sum_range_succ; two-variable AM-GM via nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a - b)]; the #print axioms output

skills.name: proof-techniques-and-writing
skills.description: Choosing a proof technique from the statement's shape and writing or auditing the proof rigorously: induction variants, contradiction, descent and extremal arguments, pigeonhole, invariants, double counting, compactness, diagonalization, the proof template, hygiene and fallacy checks, refereeing. Load before proving anything or reviewing a proof.
outline: Restate first: quantifiers in order, domains (N with or without 0, R vs C), exactly what must be shown; ambiguities become Open doubts; status labels stay defined in mathematics-toolkit section 0 and are never upgraded.
Statement shape to first technique table (moved from hub section 2) with a 'watch for' column, plus rows for well-founded induction, infinite descent and bijective proofs.

Induction catalogue: weak, strong, structural, well-founded/lexicographic, two-variable, forward-backward (Cauchy); base cases a step of size k needs; loading the induction by strengthening (sum 1/k^2 <= 2 - 1/n).

Contradiction vs contrapositive with mechanical negation of nested quantifiers; minimal counterexample and infinite descent (sqrt 2, x^4 + y^4 = z^2); extremal principle after checking the extremum exists.
Pigeonhole patterns (residues, odd parts, prefix sums mod n, Erdos-Szekeres, averaging, infinite version); invariants and monovariants (parity, mod-k weights, colourings, potentials bounded below).

Double counting and bijections (handshake, sum k C(n,k) = n 2^(n-1), well-defined inverse); compactness (Konig, de Bruijn-Erdos) and diagonalization (Cantor, halting), each with the hypothesis that makes it apply.
When stuck (moved from hub section 4): specialise or generalise, add an auxiliary object, symmetry with a justified WLOG, change representation, work backwards, find the unused hypothesis.

Proof template (Theorem, Assumptions, Notation, Lemmas, Steps written 'by X, applicable because Y', Checks, Remarks, Open); one claim per sentence; explicit constants and their dependencies; rigor level stated: sketch, full, computer-assisted, formal.

Hygiene and fallacy checklist with one-line detectors: circularity, affirming the consequent, induction step that uses P(n+1), sign errors when multiplying inequalities, reused existential witness, examples as proof (n^2 + n + 41), WLOG breaking asymmetric hypotheses.

Auditing a proof: mark each step correct, gap, error or unjustified citation; try to break each lemma on small cases; report the first fatal error with a counterexample; add sharpness remarks (equality cases, hypotheses that cannot be dropped).
Worked examples: pigeonhole on odd parts (hub example C); auditing 'all horses are the same colour', where the step fails from n = 1 to n = 2 because the overlapping subsets share no horse.

skills.name: graph-theory-probabilistic-method
skills.description: Graph theory and the probabilistic method for proofs and counterexamples: core theorems with exact hypotheses, extremal and Ramsey results, spectral graph theory, first and second moment, alteration, the Lovasz Local Lemma, random-graph thresholds, derandomization, and exhaustive checks with nauty and networkx. Load for existence, extremal or structural claims about graphs and combinatorial objects.
outline: Theorem table with hypotheses: handshake, Euler tours, Hall, Konig-Egervary, Menger and max-flow min-cut, Tutte, Dirac/Ore, Euler's formula and E <= 3V - 6, Kuratowski/Wagner, Brooks, Vizing, four colour theorem.

Extremal results: Mantel, Turan ex(n, K_(r+1)) = (1 - 1/r) n^2/2, Erdos-Stone, Kovari-Sos-Turan, Zarankiewicz, with extremal graphs proving sharpness; Ramsey R(3,3) = 6 and R(s,t) <= R(s-1,t) + R(s,t-1).

Spectral: adjacency vs Laplacian vs normalised-Laplacian conventions, matrix-tree theorem, Fiedler lambda_2, Cheeger lambda_2/2 <= h <= sqrt(2 lambda_2), expander mixing lemma, interlacing; computed with numpy/scipy.
First moment and union bound: E[X] < 1 gives P(X = 0) > 0, C(n,k) <= (en/k)^k, worked R(k,k) > 2^(k/2) (hub example D); alteration (sample then repair) for alpha(G) >= n/(2d).

Second moment and thresholds: P(X > 0) >= (EX)^2/E[X^2], variance as a covariance sum; K4 in G(n,p) at n^(-2/3); connectivity at ln n/n, giant component at 1/n; Janson and Poisson approximation for overlapping substructures.
Lovasz Local Lemma: symmetric e p (d+1) <= 1, asymmetric and lopsided forms, building the dependency graph correctly; k-SAT application; Moser-Tardos resampling turns existence into an algorithm.
Derandomization by conditional expectations (MAX-CUT >= m/2, 7/8 for MAX-E3SAT, pessimistic estimators); concentration steps cite probability-distributions-limits.

Proof pitfalls: building G_(n+1) from G_n misses graphs (remove a vertex from an arbitrary graph instead), simple vs multigraph hypotheses, forgotten connectedness, directed vs undirected, dependent events treated as independent.

Computation: networkx/igraph invariants, nauty geng for all non-isomorphic graphs, graph6 I/O, House of Graphs and SageMath, SAT encodings for colouring and Ramsey existence, seeded simulation of random constructions with confidence intervals.
Certificates over trust: return a witness (colouring, matching, Hamiltonian cycle, Kuratowski subgraph) checkable in linear time instead of a solver's yes/no.
Worked example: Dirac's theorem via the longest-path argument, exhaustive check of all graphs with n <= 9 via geng + networkx, sharpness from K_((n-1)/2,(n+1)/2) for odd n.

skills.name: lagrangian-hamiltonian-mechanics
skills.description: Deriving equations of motion and conserved quantities: generalised coordinates and constraints, Euler-Lagrange with dissipation, Noether charges, Legendre transform to Hamiltonians, Poisson brackets, canonical transforms, normal modes, rigid bodies, nonlinear-oscillator perturbation and SymPy mechanics. Load when deriving or checking classical dynamics.
outline: Procedure: generalised coordinates are the DOF left after holonomic constraints. Write T and V in them, L = T − V, then d/dt ∂L/∂q̇ − ∂L/∂q = Q_nc. Linear damping enters through the Rayleigh function F = ½Σc q̇². Non-holonomic (velocity) constraints need Lagrange multipliers, never substitution.

Noether and conservation table (moved from physics-toolkit §3): cyclic coordinate → conserved p_q. The energy function h = Σq̇∂L/∂q̇ − L is conserved when ∂L/∂t = 0, but h = T + V only for scleronomic natural systems. Virial: 2⟨T⟩ = n⟨V⟩. Dissipative systems need an energy budget instead.

Hamiltonian formulation: p = ∂L/∂q̇, H = pq̇ − L and Hamilton's equations. A charged particle has p = mv + qA. Poisson brackets: {q,p} = 1 and dF/dt = {F,H} + ∂F/∂t. Canonical transforms come from generating functions F1–F4. Action-angle variables and adiabatic invariants ∮p dq hold only when time scales are separated.

Small oscillations: expand about equilibrium to M q̈ + K q = 0 and solve K v = ω² M v with scipy.linalg.eigh(K, M). Zero modes are symmetries. Worked coupled pendula: ω₁ = sqrt(g/l) and ω₂ = sqrt(g/l + 2k/m).

Central forces: reduce to the reduced mass and use the effective potential L²/(2μr²) + V(r). Binet equation for orbit shapes; Bertrand's theorem decides which potentials give closed orbits; Kepler elements from E and L.

Rigid bodies: inertia tensor and parallel-axis theorem, Euler's equations, and the intermediate-axis instability (rotation is stable only about the largest and smallest principal moments). Integrate orientation with quaternions to avoid gimbal lock and renormalise each step.
Nonlinear oscillators (moved from §4 classical rows): Poincaré-Lindstedt and two-timing remove secular t·sin t terms. Duffing gives ω = ω₀(1 + 3βA²/(8ω₀²)); the expansion is uniform for t ~ 1/ε.

SymPy code: sympy.physics.mechanics (dynamicsymbols, LagrangesMethod or KanesMethod) or calculus.euler.euler_equations, then lambdify the right-hand side for solve_ivp. Always check h or E conservation numerically on the generated code.

Chaos diagnostics: Poincaré sections, and the largest Lyapunov exponent by Benettin tangent-vector renormalisation. Double pendulum demo: compare trajectories with δθ₀ = 1e-9 to measure the divergence time.
Rotating frames: write L in rotating coordinates and the centrifugal and Coriolis terms appear automatically. Pitfall: adding them by hand as well double-counts them.

Worked example: bead on a hoop spinning at Ω, with L = ½mR²(θ̇² + Ω²sin²θ) + mgR cosθ. θ = 0 is stable for Ω² < g/R. It bifurcates at Ω_c = sqrt(g/R) to cosθ* = g/(RΩ²). h is conserved but is not T + V.

Pitfalls: sign errors in V, forgetting time-dependent constraints (which make H ≠ E), using generalised forces in the wrong coordinates, and integrating a stiff constrained system with an explicit method (hand off to physics-ode-integrators).

skills.name: physics-ode-integrators
skills.description: Choosing, running and diagnosing ODE and SDE time steppers for physical systems: symplectic Verlet/Yoshida for long Hamiltonian runs, adaptive RK (DOP853, Tsit5) with tolerance-reduction checks, stiff BDF/Radau/Rodas with Jacobians, events, constraints and Langevin integrators. Load when writing or debugging a time integrator.
outline: Decision table (moved from physics-toolkit §6): non-stiff → RK45/Tsit5; high accuracy → DOP853/Vern9; stiff → BDF, Radau, LSODA, Rodas5P, KenCarp4 or FBDF; Hamiltonian → velocity Verlet, Yoshida4 or KahanLi8; constrained → SHAKE/RATTLE or IDA DAEs; SDE → Euler-Maruyama, Milstein or BAOAB.

Symplectic schemes (moved from numerical-methods ref §1): velocity Verlet kick-drift-kick, and Yoshida/Forest-Ruth with w1 = 1/(2 − 2^{1/3}) ≈ 1.3512 and w0 ≈ −1.7024. Energy error stays bounded while phase error grows linearly. Verlet is stable for ωh < 2. Adaptive steps break symplecticity unless a Sundman time transform is used.

Explicit stability limits on the negative real axis: Euler 2, RK2 2, RK4 2.785, DP5 ≈ 3.3. Diagnose stiffness from steps ≫ visible time scale or a wide spread of Jacobian eigenvalues, then supply jac or jac_sparsity.

Tolerance discipline code: solve_ivp(..., 'DOP853', rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12) compared with rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14; the difference must shrink about 100×. Set atol per component when scales differ. Global error is not bounded by rtol.

2026 tool snippets: SciPy solve_ivp; Julia OrdinaryDiffEq (Tsit5, Vern9, Rodas5P, DynamicalODEProblem + KahanLi8 or McAte5); JAX diffrax (Tsit5, Kvaerno5, adjoint gradients); SUNDIALS CVODE/IDA via Sundials.jl or scikit-sundae; REBOUND (WHFast, IAS15) for N-body.

Kepler benchmark (moved, computed): e = 0.5, dt = 0.01. Verlet energy error stays bounded at 2.7e-4 over 1000 orbits. RK4 drifts 3e-8 → 3e-7 → 3e-6 at 10, 100 and 1000 orbits. At equal force evaluations RK4 wins up to ~5,600 orbits, so choose by horizon; the full script is kept in the skill.

Diagnostics: relative energy error vs t on log axes (a flat band is healthy, linear growth means non-symplectic or a bug, jumps mean close encounters). Angular momentum should be exact for central forces. Integrate forward then backward to test time reversal. Measure the observed order from dt, dt/2 and dt/4.

Events and discontinuities: event functions with terminal and direction for impacts and zero crossings. Restart the integrator at a kink instead of stepping across it with a high-order method. Use dense output only at a tight tolerance.

Stochastic and Langevin: Euler-Maruyama has strong order 0.5 and Milstein 1.0. BAOAB splitting gives accurate configurational sampling. Noise amplitude is sqrt(2γk_BT dt/m). Use independent seeded streams from SeedSequence.spawn.

Stiff worked example: Robertson kinetics (k = 0.04, 3e7, 1e4) on t ∈ [0, 1e5]. Compare sol.nfev for RK45 against Radau/BDF and show that the explicit solver's step count is limited by stability, not accuracy.

Pitfalls: reporting RK4 energy drift as physics, accumulating state in float32, atol in the wrong units, using the interpolant to locate events at loose tolerance, and stepping over a stability limit after a parameter change.

skills.name: pde-discretization-stability
skills.description: Choosing and stabilising grid discretisations (FD, FV, spectral, FEM) for diffusion, advection, wave, Poisson and Schrödinger equations: CFL and von Neumann analysis, Crank-Nicolson pitfalls, limiters, boundary conditions, and sparse solvers with preconditioners. Load when building or debugging a grid-based PDE solver.
outline: Scheme table (moved from numerical-methods ref §2): diffusion → Crank-Nicolson or BDF2; advection → upwind, Lax-Wendroff or TVD/WENO; shocks → FV with Roe/HLLC and limiters; waves → leapfrog; Poisson → multigrid, FFT or CG+AMG; Schrödinger → CN or split-step; smooth periodic → pseudo-spectral with 2/3 dealiasing; complex geometry → FEM.

Stability limits: CFL |c|Δt/Δx ≤ 1. FTCS diffusion needs r = DΔt/Δx² ≤ 1/2 in 1D and ≤ 1/(2d) in d dimensions. 3D leapfrog/Yee needs cΔt ≤ 1/sqrt(Σ1/Δx_i²). Central advection-diffusion needs cell Péclet ≤ 2 to avoid wiggles.

Von Neumann procedure: substitute u_j^n = G^n e^{ikjΔx} and require |G| ≤ 1 for all k. Worked FTCS: G = 1 − 4r sin²(kΔx/2). Lax equivalence theorem. Modified-equation analysis reveals numerical diffusion and dispersion.

Fixes: Crank-Nicolson rings at large r on discontinuous data, so use Rannacher start-up (2–4 implicit Euler half-steps). For upwind smearing use limiters (minmod, MC, superbee). Write conservation form for shocks, otherwise they move at the wrong speed (Lax-Wendroff theorem).

Boundary conditions: ghost cells, one-sided second-order Neumann stencils, periodic wrap, absorbing layers and PML. BC order must match the interior order, and BCs are the usual cause of lost convergence order.

Linear solvers (moved from ref §3): dense → LU; SPD → CG with AMG or IC; nonsymmetric → GMRES(m) or BiCGSTAB with ILU; saddle point → MINRES with block preconditioners; eigenproblems → eigsh shift-invert or LOBPCG. Stop at a residual tied to the discretisation error.

Tool snippets: scipy.sparse diags plus splu factorisation reused across steps, PyAMG, FEniCSx/dolfinx weak forms, Dedalus v3 spectral, petsc4py options (-ksp_type cg -pc_type gamg -ksp_monitor), and Julia Gridap.jl or Trixi.jl.

Failure signatures: odd-even checkerboard blow-up means a stability violation; Gibbs ringing appears at jumps; slow mass or energy drift means a non-conservative scheme; plot the spectrum of the discrete operator to diagnose.

Worked example: u_t = D u_xx with D = 1 and Δx = 0.01. FTCS needs Δt ≤ 5e-5. CN at Δt = 1e-3 (r = 10) is stable but rings on a step, and Rannacher start-up removes the ringing. Confirm O(Δt², Δx²) on three grids.

Pitfalls: treating unconditional stability as accuracy, refining Δx without scaling Δt ∝ Δx² for explicit diffusion, aliasing of nonlinear terms in spectral codes, and solving each step to 1e-14 while the discretisation error is 1e-4.

skills.name: em-field-solvers-fdtd-fem
skills.description: Electromagnetics problem solving and field solvers: Maxwell in media, interface conditions, skin depth, waveguide and cavity formulas, SI/Gaussian translation, then FDTD (Yee grid, Courant, PML, Meep/openEMS/Tidy3D) and FEM (Nédélec elements, FEniCSx/Palace/Elmer) set-up and validation. Load for any field, antenna, waveguide or EM simulation task.
outline: Triage by size and frequency: electro- and magnetostatics (Laplace/Poisson), quasi-static eddy currents (skin depth δ = sqrt(2/(ωμσ))), or full-wave when the size is about λ. Then choose time vs frequency domain and FDTD, FEM, MoM or BEM.

Core formulas: Maxwell with D = εE and B = μH. Interface conditions: tangential E and H are continuous without surface current, and normal D jumps by σ_s. Poynting S = E×H, η₀ ≈ 376.73 Ω, Larmor P = q²a²/(6πε₀c³). Waveguide cutoff f_c = (c/2)·sqrt((m/a)² + (n/b)²). Cavity mode frequencies.
Unit systems: state SI or Gaussian per formula and translate whole formulas with the substitution table in dimensional-analysis-units; never mix fields from two systems.

FDTD procedure: Yee staggered grid with at least 10–20 cells per shortest in-material wavelength. Courant S = cΔt/Δx ≤ 1/√3 in 3D (Meep defaults to 0.5). PML 8–16 cells thick and away from scatterers. Dispersive Drude/Lorentz media via ADE. Use subpixel averaging against staircasing.
Meep (pymeep) snippet: c = 1 units with frequency f = a/λ, geometry, PML, a Gaussian source, flux regions, and a mandatory normalisation run without the structure. Harminv extracts resonances and Q.

FEM procedure: the weak form of ∇×∇×E − k²ε_r E = 0 needs curl-conforming Nédélec elements, because Lagrange elements produce spurious modes. Use about 5–10 second-order elements per λ, absorbing BCs or PML, and eigenmodes with Q factors.

Tool map for 2026: FEniCSx/dolfinx, scikit-fem, MFEM, Elmer, Palace (AWS; superconducting-circuit eigenmodes and EPR), openEMS (FDTD, antennas), Tidy3D (cloud FDTD), COMSOL interop. Use gmsh for meshes.
Statics quick methods: method of images, capacitance from field energy (C = 2U/V²), inductance from flux, and Poisson solves by SOR or multigrid with a fringe-field check.

Validation benchmarks: Mie scattering for spheres (miepython), rectangular cavity resonances, a parallel-plate capacitor with fringing, the dipole far-field pattern and Fresnel reflection. Check R + T + A = 1 and reciprocity.
Worked example: copper at 1 GHz (σ = 5.96e7 S/m) gives δ ≈ 2.06 μm and R_s = 1/(σδ) ≈ 8.1 mΩ. Verify with an eddy-current FEM solve using at least 3 elements per δ.

Pitfalls: e^{−iωt} vs e^{jωt} flips the sign of Im ε (loss vs gain). A peak phasor vs RMS factor of 2 in power. A missing normalisation run. PML touching evanescent fields. Mesh too coarse inside conductors.

skills.name: quantum-mechanics-methods
skills.description: Analytic quantum mechanics toolkit: operator algebra and ladder operators, angular momentum addition and Clebsch-Gordan, selection rules, nondegenerate/degenerate and time-dependent perturbation theory, Fermi golden rule, variational and WKB methods, Born scattering, with validity and sign checks. Load when solving or checking a QM problem by hand or with SymPy.
outline: Procedure: find the symmetries and good quantum numbers, then choose the basis that diagonalises H₀ and the commuting set. Pick perturbative, variational, WKB or exact diagonalisation from the decision table, solve, then run the checks.
Operator toolkit: [x,p] = iħ; a and a† with x = sqrt(ħ/2mω)(a + a†); the Hadamard lemma e^A B e^−A; Heisenberg equations of motion; Ehrenfest; the virial theorem; Hellmann-Feynman dE/dλ = ⟨∂H/∂λ⟩.

Angular momentum: j₁ ⊗ j₂ = |j₁ − j₂| … j₁ + j₂. Clebsch-Gordan coefficients from sympy.physics.quantum.cg.CG or sympy.physics.wigner. Wigner-Eckart selection rules (E1: Δl = ±1, Δm = 0, ±1). ⟨L·S⟩ = ħ²[j(j+1) − l(l+1) − s(s+1)]/2.

Perturbation table (moved from physics-toolkit §4 quantum rows): E⁽¹⁾ = ⟨n|V|n⟩ and E⁽²⁾ = Σ|V_mn|²/(E_n − E_m), valid when |V_mn| ≪ |E_n − E_m|. The ground-state E⁽²⁾ is always < 0. For a degenerate level, diagonalise V in the subspace first: the n = 2 hydrogen Stark shifts are ±3e a₀ E.

Time-dependent: first-order amplitude c_f = (1/iħ)∫V_fi e^{iω_fi t} dt. Fermi golden rule Γ = (2π/ħ)|V_fi|²ρ(E_f), valid for continuum final states with t ≫ ħ/ΔE and Γt ≪ 1. Rabi formula beyond perturbation theory. Sudden and adiabatic criteria.

Variational (moved from §5): the Rayleigh-Ritz upper bound and Hylleraas-Undheim for excited states. Hydrogen with a Gaussian trial gives a = 8/(9π) and E = −4/(3π) Ha = −11.55 eV against −13.606 eV. Helium with Z_eff = 27/16 gives −2.848 Ha against −2.9037 Ha.

WKB: ∮p dx = 2πħ(n + ½) with two soft turning points, (n + ¾) with one hard wall and (n + 1) with two. Tunnelling T ≈ exp(−2∫κ dx). Validity |ħp′/p²| ≪ 1; use connection formulas at the turning points.
Scattering: Born f(θ) = −(m/2πħ²)∫e^{−iq·r}V d³r, with the Yukawa potential reducing to Rutherford. Partial waves and phase shifts; optical theorem σ_tot = (4π/k) Im f(0).
Identical particles: symmetrise or antisymmetrise; singlet/triplet exchange energy signs; Pauli exclusion; second-quantised operators for many-body bookkeeping.

Checks: hermiticity, normalisation, units (atomic units restored), the limits V → 0 and ħ → 0, the Thomas-Reiche-Kuhn sum rule and commutator consistency. Verify the algebra in SymPy (sympy.physics.quantum).

Worked example: V = λx⁴ uses ⟨n|x⁴|n⟩ = (ħ/2mω)²·3(2n² + 2n + 1), so the ground state shifts by 3λ(ħ/2mω)². Cross-check by truncated number-basis diagonalisation (see schrodinger-numerics) and watch where the series breaks down.
Pitfalls: nondegenerate formulas applied inside a degenerate subspace; box vs δ-normalisation in ρ(E); hf vs ħω; Fourier sign conventions; spin factor-of-2 degeneracies.

skills.name: schrodinger-numerics
skills.description: Numerical quantum mechanics: discretising H (finite differences, Colbert-Miller/Fourier DVR, number bases), sparse shift-invert eigensolvers, split-operator and Crank-Nicolson propagation with norm checks, spin chains by symmetry-blocked exact diagonalisation, MPS pointers, and Lindblad dynamics with QuTiP 5. Load when a QM problem needs a computer.
outline: Method selection: 1–3D single particle → FD or DVR grid. Smooth problems → Fourier/sinc DVR, which converges exponentially. Spin chains up to about 24–26 sites → sparse Lanczos. Larger 1D systems → DMRG/MPS (ITensors.jl, TeNPy, quimb). Open systems → QuTiP mesolve or mcsolve.
Grid rules (atomic units): Δx < π/k_max with k_max = sqrt(2mE_max)/ħ, and a box much larger than the wavefunction decay length. Converge eigenvalues in Δx and in L separately and report both.

Code: a 1D FD Hamiltonian from scipy.sparse.diags, then eigsh(H, k, sigma=E_guess, which='LM') with shift-invert. Test against the harmonic oscillator E_n = n + ½, which has O(Δx²) error. Colbert-Miller DVR kinetic matrix for spectral accuracy.

Time evolution: split-operator FFT (Strang, e^{−iVdt/2}e^{−iTdt}e^{−iVdt/2}), which is unitary with O(dt²) global error. Crank-Nicolson (1 + iHdt/2)ψ' = (1 − iHdt/2)ψ with the splu factorisation reused. expm_multiply or a Chebyshev propagator. Monitor norm and ⟨H⟩ every N steps.
Boundaries and aliasing: use complex absorbing potentials or masks against reflections. The momentum grid is capped at k_max = π/Δx, and a wavepacket that reaches it aliases. Keep |V|Δt/ħ ≪ π.

Spin systems: build Hamiltonians from Kronecker products, quspin or QuTiP tensor. Block-diagonalise with total S_z, translation and parity. N = 24 is 16.7M amplitudes, about 268 MB per complex128 vector.

QuTiP 5 snippet: mesolve(H, rho0, tlist, c_ops=[sqrt(gamma)*a], e_ops=[...]), steadystate, and QobjEvo for time-dependent H. Check trace = 1 and positivity. Born-Markov validity needs γ ≪ system frequencies.

Validation benchmarks: harmonic oscillator, infinite well E_n = n²π²ħ²/(2mL²), Morse and Pöschl-Teller levels, the hydrogen radial equation per l, and Rabi oscillation against the formula. Check the virial theorem.
Variational caveat: FD eigenvalues are not variational and often converge from below, while basis-set (Galerkin) results are upper bounds. Say which kind every reported eigenvalue is.
Performance: CuPy or JAX for large FFT grids, sparse formats (CSR) for H, and reuse of factorisations. Do convergence runs in float64 and production in float32 only after a cross-check.
Worked example: double-well tunnelling. ΔE comes from the two lowest FD eigenvalues and is compared with the WKB estimate. The split-operator run must show population transfer with period 2πħ/ΔE.
Pitfalls: eigsh without shift-invert stalls on low or interior eigenvalues; a real dtype in time evolution; degeneracies misordered; boundary reflections read as physics; an unconverged box size.

skills.name: statmech-monte-carlo
skills.description: Statistical mechanics and Monte Carlo practice: ensembles, fluctuation formulas and exact partition-function checks, Metropolis-Hastings and heat-bath updates, Wolff/Swendsen-Wang clusters, parallel tempering and Wang-Landau, autocorrelation/blocking/jackknife errors, and finite-size scaling. Load when sampling a physical system or judging MC error bars.
outline: Ensembles: microcanonical, canonical, grand canonical and NPT. F = −k_BT ln Z. Fluctuation formulas C_V = Var(E)/(k_BT²) and χ = βN·Var(m). Equipartition fails when k_BT ≪ ħω. Bose and Fermi occupancies.
Exact checks: 1D Ising; 2D Ising Onsager T_c = 2J/(k_B ln(1 + √2)) ≈ 2.269 with M = (1 − sinh⁻⁴(2βJ))^{1/8}; Einstein and Debye solids; ideal gas. Exact enumeration of a 4×4 lattice as a unit test.

Metropolis-Hastings procedure: detailed balance with acceptance min(1, e^{−βΔE}·q(x|x′)/q(x′|x)). Tune the step to about 0.44 acceptance in 1D and about 0.234 in high dimension. Sequential sweeps are fine because global balance holds. Heat-bath updates as an alternative.
RNG discipline: numpy.random.default_rng(seed) (PCG64) or Philox, with independent parallel streams from SeedSequence.spawn. Never reseed with nearby integers per worker.

Cluster updates (moved from physics-toolkit §6): Wolff with p_add = 1 − e^{−2βJ}, and Swendsen-Wang. The critical dynamic exponent of the 2D Ising model is z ≈ 2.17 for local Metropolis and z ≲ 0.3 for Wolff.

Rough landscapes: parallel tempering on a geometric ladder with swap acceptance about 20–30%. Wang-Landau for g(E) with an 80% flatness criterion, f → sqrt(f) (or the 1/t variant) until ln f < 1e-8. Umbrella sampling with WHAM or MBAR (pymbar 4).

Error analysis (moved from numerical-methods ref §4): τ_int = 1 + 2Σρ(t) with the Sokal window M ≥ 5τ and N_eff = N/τ. Flyvbjerg-Petersen blocking (code kept) must reach a plateau. Judge burn-in from traces. Use jackknife for nonlinear estimators. Multiple chains need R̂ < 1.01 and ESS > 400 (ArviZ).
Finite-size scaling: Binder cumulant U₄ = 1 − ⟨m⁴⟩/(3⟨m²⟩²) crossings, χ_max ∝ L^{γ/ν}, data collapse, and corrections to scaling. Never quote single-L exponents.
Code: a vectorised checkerboard Metropolis for the 2D Ising model in NumPy+Numba (or Julia), plus a Wolff cluster flip with an explicit stack. Seeds and config are saved next to the results CSV.
Quantum MC pointers: path-integral MC, SSE, variational and diffusion MC (NetKet for neural VMC), and the fermion sign problem as a hard stop that must be reported.
Worked example: 2D Ising with L = 16, 32, 64. Binder crossings near 2.269. Metropolis τ at T_c grows like L^2.17, Wolff makes it small again, and T_c is reported with jackknife errors.
Pitfalls: naive σ/√N on correlated samples; correlated RNG streams; equilibrating only from an ordered start; non-ergodic low-T updates; finite-size rounding read as a transition.

skills.name: molecular-dynamics-setup
skills.description: Classical molecular dynamics set-up and analysis: force-field and ML-potential choice, units, time step from the fastest mode, constraints and HMR, thermostats/barostats that sample the right ensemble, PME, the equilibration protocol, NVE drift checks, and RDF/MSD/Green-Kubo observables with OpenMM, LAMMPS, GROMACS or ASE. Load when building, running or reviewing an MD simulation.
outline: Workflow: build the system (packmol, PDBFixer, Moltemplate), then minimise, then NVT, then NPT equilibration, then production. Run replicas from different velocity seeds and judge run length against the slowest correlation time.

Force fields: AMBER ff19SB/OPC, CHARMM36m, OPLS-AA, GAFF2/OpenFF Sage 2.x for small molecules, EAM/MEAM for metals, ReaxFF for chemistry. Machine-learned potentials (MACE, MACE-MP-0 foundation models, NequIP/Allegro) with an extrapolation check. Never mix combining rules across force fields.

Time step rules (moved from numerical-methods ref §5): dt ≈ 1/10–1/20 of the fastest period, i.e. 1 fs with flexible X-H bonds, 2 fs with SHAKE/RATTLE/LINCS on H bonds and 4 fs with hydrogen mass repartitioning. NVE drift target < ~0.01 kT per DOF per ns.

Thermostats and barostats: Langevin (γ ≈ 1 ps⁻¹), Nosé-Hoover chains and Bussi v-rescale are canonical. Berendsen is for equilibration only, because its fluctuations are wrong. Barostats: Monte Carlo, C-rescale or Parrinello-Rahman. Use weak coupling when dynamics observables matter.

Electrostatics and cutoffs: PME/PPPM with ewald tolerance about 1e-5 and a 0.9–1.2 nm cutoff with a neighbour-list buffer. Add the LJ long-range dispersion correction. Minimum image requires box > 2r_c. Charged cells get a neutralising background.
Units: LAMMPS units real/metal/lj; GROMACS nm, ps, kJ/mol. Reduced LJ units T* = k_BT/ε and t* = t·sqrt(ε/(mσ²)). Convert explicitly when moving between codes.

Snippets: OpenMM 8.x Python (ForceField, PME, LangevinMiddleIntegrator(300*kelvin, 1/picosecond, 0.002*picoseconds), constraints=HBonds, MonteCarloBarostat); a minimal LAMMPS input with fix nvt and thermo; an ASE MD loop with a MACE calculator.

Analysis: g(r) with MDAnalysis 2.x or MDTraj. D from the MSD slope over 6t on unwrapped trajectories, with the Yeh-Hummer correction D_∞ = D_PBC + k_BTξ/(6πηL), ξ ≈ 2.837297. Green-Kubo viscosity. Equilibration detection with pymbar.timeseries.detect_equilibration and block averaging.

Validation: NVE energy conservation, canonical kinetic-energy fluctuations (physical_validation package), density and RDF against experiment (water's first O-O peak at about 2.8 Å), and reproducibility across replicas.
Performance: GPU platforms (OpenMM CUDA, GROMACS GPU-resident steps, LAMMPS KOKKOS), measured in ns/day. Profile neighbour-list and PME balance before buying hardware (link performance-optimization).
Worked example: Rahman's LJ argon with 864 atoms, ε/k_B = 119.8 K, σ = 3.405 Å, 94.4 K and 1.374 g/cm³. Reproduce D ≈ 2.43e-5 cm²/s from the MSD and report the NVE drift and finite-size correction.

Pitfalls: the 'flying ice cube' from velocity rescaling, MSD on wrapped coordinates, runs shorter than the correlation time, a single trajectory, thermostats damping dynamics observables, and a mismatched cutoff and dispersion correction.

skills.name: fluid-dynamics-cfd
skills.description: Fluid dynamics, convective heat transfer and CFD basics: regime triage from Re/Ma/Kn, analytic anchor flows and correlations, boundary layers, incompressible projection/PISO solvers, turbulence-model and y+ choice, OpenFOAM/SU2/Basilisk/LBM set-up, mesh checks and validation benchmarks. Load when modelling a flow or heat-transfer problem or setting up or reviewing a CFD case.
outline: Regime triage: Re (Stokes ≪ 1; pipe transition 2300–4000), Ma (incompressible below 0.3), Kn (continuum < 0.01, slip 0.01–0.1, DSMC/kinetic above that), free surface (We, Fr, Bo), buoyancy (Ra, Ri) and rotation (Ro). Each choice is written as an assumption with its number.

Anchor solutions: Poiseuille Q = πR⁴Δp/(8μL), Couette, Stokes drag 6πμRv, Schiller-Naumann C_D = 24/Re·(1 + 0.15Re^0.687) for Re ≲ 800, Blasius δ ≈ 5x/√Re_x with C_f = 0.664/√Re_x, Moody/Colebrook/Haaland friction factors, and Kolmogorov η with DNS cost ~Re^{9/4} points.

Convective heat transfer: Dittus-Boelter Nu = 0.023Re^0.8Pr^n (Re > 1e4); Churchill-Chu for natural convection; Churchill-Bernstein for cylinders; thermal resistance networks; radiation h_rad ≈ 4εσT³; conjugate heat transfer (chtMultiRegionFoam).
Boundary layers (moved from physics-toolkit §4 singular rows): δ/L ~ Re^{-1/2}, matched inner and outer expansions, and adverse pressure gradients leading to separation.

Incompressible solvers: Chorin projection (advect, diffuse, pressure Poisson, project), staggered grids or collocated grids with Rhie-Chow, and SIMPLE/PISO/PIMPLE. Explicit CFL ≈ 0.5. Semi-Lagrangian advection is stable but diffusive, which suits graphics.

Turbulence model table: k-ω SST for adverse gradients and separation, realizable k-ε for free shear, Spalart-Allmaras for external aero. LES (WALE, dynamic Smagorinsky) must resolve about 80% of the TKE; DDES as a hybrid. y+ ≈ 1 for resolved walls and 30–300 for wall functions, with the first-cell height from u_τ.

Tools for 2026: OpenFOAM (ESI v2412/v2506 or Foundation 12/13), SU2 8.x (compressible, adjoint), Basilisk (adaptive multiphase), Dedalus (spectral), LBM (Palabos, waLBerla, lbmpy), differentiable JAX-Fluids/PhiFlow, and ParaView/pyvista for postprocessing.

OpenFOAM commands: blockMesh/snappyHexMesh, then checkMesh (non-orthogonality < 70, skewness < 4), fvSchemes/fvSolution, simpleFoam/pimpleFoam/icoFoam, foamMonitor, postProcess -func yPlus, and foamToVTK.

Mesh and BC rules: a three-grid GCI study, outlets about 10 D downstream, blockage < ~5%, inlet turbulence intensity and length scale stated, and integral quantities (forces, Δp, Nu) monitored rather than residuals alone.

Validation benchmarks: the lid-driven cavity at Re = 100 and 1000 against Ghia et al. 1982; backward-facing step reattachment length; a cylinder at Re = 100 with St ≈ 0.165 and C_D ≈ 1.33; Taylor-Green vortex decay for DNS/LES.
Worked example: water at 1 m/s in a 5 cm pipe gives Re = 5e4, Blasius f = 0.316Re^{-1/4} ≈ 0.021 and Δp/L ≈ 211 Pa/m. u_τ = v·sqrt(f/8) ≈ 0.051 m/s, so a first cell at y+ = 1 is about 20 μm high.

Pitfalls: steady RANS on an inherently unsteady flow, wall functions at y+ < 30, first-order upwind in production, an incompressible solver at Ma > 0.3, 2D runs compared with 3D turbulent data, and residual drops taken as convergence.

skills.name: optics-wave-propagation
skills.description: Optics and wave propagation: regime choice by Fresnel number, ABCD ray matrices, Gaussian beams and q-parameters, diffraction formulas, correctly sampled angular-spectrum and Fresnel propagation with FFTs, Fresnel equations and thin-film transfer matrices, coherence, Fabry-Pérot, dispersion and pulse broadening. Load when designing, estimating or simulating an optical system or wave field.
outline: Regime triage: geometric ray optics when λ ≪ features, scalar diffraction when features ≫ λ, full-wave when features ~λ (hand off to em-field-solvers-fdtd-fem or RCWA). Fresnel number N_F = a²/(λz): ≫ 1 geometric, ~1 Fresnel, ≪ 1 Fraunhofer.

Paraxial rays: ABCD matrices (free space [[1,d],[0,1]], thin lens [[1,0],[−1/f,1]], interfaces); det = n₁/n₂; imaging when B = 0; lensmaker's equation. Real design tools: rayoptics, optiland, KrakenOS or Zemax for aberrations.

Gaussian beams: w(z) = w₀·sqrt(1 + (z/z_R)²), z_R = πw₀²n/λ, the Gouy phase, q′ = (Aq + B)/(Cq + D), divergence θ = λ/(πw₀), focused spot w_f ≈ λf/(πw_in), and the M² factor. Intensity FWHM = 1.1774w.
Diffraction formulas: slit minima a sinθ = mλ; Airy/Rayleigh resolution 1.22λ/D; grating equation d(sinθ_m − sinθ_i) = mλ; resolving power R = mN.

Numerical propagation procedure: angular spectrum H = exp(iz·sqrt(k² − k_x² − k_y²)). Critical sampling is Δx = λz/L (NΔx² = λz): use the transfer-function form at shorter z and the impulse-response form at longer z. Zero-pad against wrap-around, handle evanescent components, and check energy with Parseval.

FFT hygiene code: fftshift/ifftshift conventions, frequency grids from np.fft.fftfreq(N, dx), and phase-convention consistency (exp(i(kz − ωt))). Verify the free Gaussian beam against the analytic w(z).

Interfaces and films: Fresnel r_s and r_p; Brewster tan θ_B = n₂/n₁; TIR and the critical angle; the multilayer characteristic (transfer) matrix with the tmm package; quarter-wave AR coating n_c = sqrt(n₀n_s).
Coherence and cavities: coherence length l_c ≈ λ²/Δλ; van Cittert-Zernike for spatial coherence; fringe visibility; Fabry-Pérot finesse ℱ = π√R/(1 − R) and FSR = c/(2nL).
Dispersion and pulses: n_g = n − λ dn/dλ, GVD β₂, Gaussian broadening τ(z) = τ₀·sqrt(1 + (z/L_D)²) with L_D = τ₀²/|β₂|, Gaussian time-bandwidth product 0.441, single-mode fibre for V < 2.405.
Tools: NumPy/SciPy FFT, LightPipes, poppy, prysm, HCIPy, diffractsim, tmm, S4/grcwa for RCWA, Meep/Tidy3D for full-wave.

Worked example: a 632.8 nm beam with w = 2 mm through an f = 100 mm lens gives w_f ≈ 10.1 μm and z_R ≈ 0.50 mm. Reproduce it with angular-spectrum propagation (N = 4096, sampling criterion checked) to within 1%.
Pitfalls: paraxial formulas at NA > ~0.5 (vector Richards-Wolf needed); 1/e² vs FWHM radius; field vs intensity; unshifted FFTs; aliased chirp phase; mixed sign conventions.

skills.name: uncertainty-propagation-fitting
skills.description: Measurement uncertainty and model fitting for physics data: GUM Type A/B budgets, linear and correlated propagation with the uncertainties package, Monte Carlo propagation (JCGM 101), weighted least squares with chi-square diagnostics, ODR for x-errors, Poisson likelihoods, bootstrap, and reporting conventions. Load when a result needs an error bar or a model must be fit to data.
outline: Budget procedure (GUM, JCGM 100): list the inputs. Type A is s/√n. Type B from specs uses a/√3 for a rectangular and a/√6 for a triangular distribution. Compute sensitivity coefficients, then the combined u_c and the expanded U = k·u_c, with k = 2 ≈ 95% when the Welch-Satterthwaite ν_eff is large.

Linear propagation: u_y² = Σ(∂f/∂x_i)²u_i² + 2ΣΣ(∂f/∂x_i)(∂f/∂x_j)u_ij. Relative-error rules for products and powers. Worked: the difference of strongly correlated quantities, where correlation changes the answer.
Code: the uncertainties package (ufloat, correlated_values, unumpy) tracks correlations automatically. JAX or autograd Jacobians give sensitivities. pint Measurement combines units and errors.

Monte Carlo propagation (JCGM 101): sample the input distributions, push them through f and report the mean and percentile interval. Prefer it for nonlinear f, relative errors above ~10–20% or asymmetric outputs. About 1e6 trials gives a 95% interval to 2 significant figures.

Fitting: curve_fit(f, x, y, sigma=σ, absolute_sigma=True), noting that the default False rescales the covariance by χ²_ν. lmfit for bounds and conf_interval; iminuit/MINOS for asymmetric errors; emcee or PyMC when a posterior is wanted.

Goodness of fit: χ²_ν ≈ 1 ± sqrt(2/ν) and the p-value; normalised residual plots and a runs test; the parameter correlation matrix (near-degenerate parameters should be reparametrised); AIC and BIC for model choice.
Errors in x: orthogonal distance regression (scipy.odr or its successor odrpack; check deprecation in your SciPy) or the effective-variance method. Required when σ_x·|f′| is comparable to σ_y.
Counting data: Poisson likelihood or Cash statistic instead of χ² when counts are below ~10–20 per bin. Do not fit log-transformed data without transforming the weights.
Resampling: residual or pairs bootstrap; jackknife for nonlinear estimators; block bootstrap for time-correlated data (link statmech-monte-carlo).

Reporting: 1–2 significant figures in the uncertainty and the value rounded to match; concise form 1.2345(67); separate stat and sys terms, e.g. 9.81 ± 0.02 (stat) ± 0.05 (sys) m/s²; always state the coverage factor.

Worked example: a pendulum with L = 1.000 ± 0.002 m and T = 2.007 ± 0.005 s gives g = 4π²L/T² = 9.80 ± 0.05 m/s² (0.54%). Cross-check with MC propagation and note that the θ₀ = 5° amplitude correction (+0.05% in T) is negligible.
Pitfalls: a max-min spread used as σ, double-counted correlated systematics, a hidden systematic floor, absolute_sigma left at its default, and ignored parameter correlations in derived quantities.

skills.name: simulation-verification-validation
skills.description: Verification and validation of physics simulations: code verification by manufactured solutions and observed order, solution verification by Richardson extrapolation and GCI, error budgets, floating-point floors, conserved-quantity monitors, a benchmark catalogue, reproducibility and golden tests, and the pre-return physics sanity gate. Load before trusting, reporting or reviewing any simulated number.
outline: Vocabulary (moved from numerical-methods ref intro): code verification, solution verification and validation as in ASME V&V 10/20, Roache and Oberkampf. Name which one a claim requires before running anything.

Convergence study (moved from physics-toolkit §6): run h, h/2 and h/4. Observed order p = ln(|f₃ − f₂|/|f₂ − f₁|)/ln r. Richardson extrapolation f₁ + (f₁ − f₂)/(r^p − 1). Sign changes in the differences mean oscillatory, non-asymptotic convergence.

GCI (moved from ref §2): GCI_fine = F_s|(f₂ − f₁)/f₁|/(r^p − 1), with F_s = 1.25 for 3 or more grids and 3.0 for 2. Asymptotic-range check GCI_medium ≈ r^p·GCI_fine. Report it as the relative discretisation uncertainty.

Method of manufactured solutions (moved): choose u* exercising every term, derive the source with SymPy and lambdify it, then run 3–4 grids, where the error norm must fall at the theoretical order. Boundary conditions are the usual culprit; a SymPy template is included.

Error budget: discretisation, iterative (solve the residual to 0.01–0.1 of the discretisation error), statistical, roundoff, input-parameter and model-form errors are reported separately and never summed silently.

Roundoff floor: compare discretisation error with the floating-point floor and keep float64 references for float32/GPU runs; cancellation fixes, summation and step-size rules live in numerical-error-analysis.

Runtime monitors: drift per unit time of energy, momentum, mass, charge and norm; mirror inputs giving mirrored outputs; the time-reversal test; positivity of densities, probabilities and temperatures; the second law; causality.

Benchmark catalogue routed to the domain skills: Kepler and the harmonic oscillator, heat-equation Gaussian spreading, the Sod shock tube, the Ghia lid-driven cavity, 2D Ising/Onsager, Rahman LJ argon, Mie scattering, hydrogen and HO spectra.

Reproducibility and regression: seeds from SeedSequence; committed configs; locked environments (uv.lock, Manifest.toml, conda-lock); golden-value tests whose tolerance is derived from the error budget (never 1e-12 on chaotic outputs); differential tests against an independent implementation. Generic test design goes to testing-strategy.

Sanity gate (moved from §8; the hub keeps a short copy): dimensions, two limits, signs and monotonicity, a Fermi estimate within ×10, conservation, evaluated smallness parameters, observed order ≈ expected order, sourced constants, second law, causality and positivity.

Worked example: drag coefficient on three grids with r = 2, f = 1.338, 1.352 and 1.408. This gives p = 2, a Richardson value of 1.3333 and GCI_fine = 0.44%. GCI_medium = 1.73% ≈ 4 × 0.44%, so the grids are in the asymptotic range.

Pitfalls: claiming convergence from two grids, a residual drop taken as solution convergence, an observed order above theory (usually error cancellation or a too-coarse grid), and validation against the same data used for calibration.

skills.name: dimensional-analysis-units
skills.description: Dimensions, units and magnitudes: Buckingham pi and nondimensionalisation, regime-deciding dimensionless numbers, scaling laws, Fermi estimates, limiting cases, SI 2019 and CODATA 2022 constants, unit-carrying code (pint, astropy.units, Unitful.jl), unit systems and conversion traps. Load before deriving or trusting any physical formula, magnitude or conversion.
outline: Buckingham pi: list variables including dimensional constants, build the dimension matrix, rank k gives n-k groups; automate with sympy Matrix.nullspace and check each group with pint (q.dimensionality == {}); pendulum T = sqrt(L/g) Phi(theta0).
Nondimensionalisation from the dominant balance with each small parameter eps written down; eps on the highest derivative means a singular limit and a boundary layer; distinguished limits.
Regime table with thresholds: Re (pipe 2300), Ma 0.3, Kn 0.01/10, Fr, Pe, Pr, Bi 0.1, St, We, Bo, Ra 1708, Ri 0.25, Ro, De, v/c, S/hbar, k_B T/(hbar omega).

Scaling laws with validity conditions (Stokes vs Newton drag, diffusion length sqrt(Dt), Kolmogorov eta, Taylor blast wave, capillary length 2.7 mm) and similarity: Re and Fr cannot both match in a ship tank.

Fermi estimates: product of factors each known within x3, geometric mean of bounds, log-errors added in quadrature, 1 significant figure; anchors 1000 kg/m^3, 1.2 kg/m^3, 1e5 Pa, 1361 W/m^2, k_B T(300 K) = 25.9 meV.
Limiting-case checklist: each parameter to 0 and infinity, hbar to 0, c to infinity, symmetric configurations, signs and monotonicity; evaluate every smallness parameter at the actual numbers.

Constants: SI 2019 exact set (c, h, e, k_B, N_A, Delta nu_Cs) and derived exact values; CODATA 2022 with a vintage check (1/scipy.constants.fine_structure = 137.035999177); mu_0 no longer exact; never hand-type a library constant; cite NIST/CRC for material data.

Units in code: pint (contexts, spectral, @ureg.wraps, Measurement), astropy.units equivalencies, Unitful.jl with PhysicalConstants.jl, sympy.physics.units; strip units only at the numerical kernel and re-attach after.
