Unit systems: Gaussian to SI substitution table (owned here), natural units (1 GeV^-1 = 0.1973 fm), atomic units (E_h = 27.211 eV, a0 = 0.529 A), geometric G = c = 1, reduced LJ; restore dimensions explicitly at the end.

Traps: omega vs f, cm^-1 vs k = 2 pi/lambda, per mole vs per particle, eV vs eV/c^2, absolute K vs Delta T, dB as 10 vs 20 log, 2 pi hidden in 'dimensionless' radians; scipy.constants.g is standard gravity; NumPy silently strips pint units.

Worked examples: Taylor's Trinity yield E ~ rho R^5/t^2 ~ 25 kt; Al sphere lumped model (Bi = 1.4e-4, tau = 807 s, about 21-24 min with radiation); 1550 nm photon = 0.7999 eV = 193.4 THz = 6451.6 cm^-1, by hand and with pint.

skills.name: quantum-circuit-decomposition
skills.description: Building and decomposing circuits at gate level: Euler/ZYZ and KAK two-qubit synthesis, controlled-U and multi-controlled gates, Toffoli/CCZ and relative-phase variants, Pauli-exponential ladders, rotation-synthesis T-counts, state preparation and native-gate equivalences. Load when building, decomposing or hand-costing a circuit.
outline: Universal sets and cost metrics: Clifford+T, where T or Toffoli count is the fault-tolerant cost. Native 2q gates per platform: IBM Heron CZ plus fractional RZZ, Eagle ECR, Google CZ or sqrt(iSWAP), trapped-ion MS/ZZ(theta) with all-to-all connectivity. Report 2q count and 2q depth after translation to native gates, never before.

Single-qubit synthesis: U = e^{i alpha} RZ(beta) RY(gamma) RZ(delta) (ZYZ), plus the ZXZ, U3 and ZSX forms. Tools: Qiskit OneQubitEulerDecomposer(basis='ZSX') and cirq.single_qubit_matrix_to_phxz. Merge adjacent 1q gates before counting.

Two-qubit KAK/Weyl: any U(4) = (A1 x A2) exp(i(a XX + b YY + c ZZ)) (B1 x B2). The Weyl coordinates set the CNOT count: 0 for local, 1 for (pi/4,0,0), 2 when c = 0, otherwise 3. Tools: qiskit.synthesis TwoQubitBasisDecomposer and cirq.two_qubit_matrix_to_cz_operations. Approximate synthesis can trade a little fidelity for one fewer CNOT.

Controlled-U by ABC decomposition (U = e^{i alpha} A X B X C with ABC = I): 2 CNOTs plus 1q gates, and a phase gate on the control for e^{i alpha}. Known-answer test: controlled-RY(theta) = RY(theta/2) CX RY(-theta/2) CX on the target.

Multi-controlled X: no-ancilla linear-depth constructions vs clean- or dirty-ancilla variants (Qiskit synth_mcx_* plugins; check names in the installed version). Toffoli = 6 CNOT + 7 T. Margolus relative-phase Toffoli = 3 CNOT when its phase is later uncomputed. Gidney temporary logical-AND = 4 T, with a measurement-based uncompute that costs 0 T.

Pauli-string exponential exp(-i theta P/2) of weight w: basis change on each support qubit (H for X; S-dagger then H, or RX(pi/2), for Y), a CNOT ladder (2(w-1) CNOTs) or a balanced tree for log depth, then RZ(theta). Consecutive exponentials that share support cancel parts of their ladders.

Rotation synthesis for fault tolerance: gridsynth (pygridsynth or newsynth) needs about 3 log2(1/eps) + O(log log 1/eps) T per rotation, so eps = 1e-10 costs about 100 T. Probabilistic mixing roughly halves this. Set eps per rotation = eps_synth / N_rot.

Identities for hand optimisation: HZH = X; CZ is symmetric; CNOT = (I x H) CZ (I x H); SWAP = 3 CNOT, or 2 when one input is known to be |0>. Also iSWAP / sqrt(iSWAP) / ECR / CZ conversions, commuting RZ through a CNOT control, and phase-polynomial merging of CNOT+RZ networks.

State preparation and generic unitaries: an arbitrary n-qubit state needs about 2^n CNOTs (Shende-Bullock-Markov, Mottonen). Qiskit StatePreparation is unitary; Initialize adds a reset. A generic n-qubit unitary needs at least ceil((4^n - 3n - 1)/4) CNOTs. Flag any algorithm that assumes arbitrary data loads cheaply.

Measurement and dynamic circuits: X basis = H then measure; Y basis = S-dagger, H, then measure. Mid-circuit measure plus reset, and feed-forward (qc.if_test) for constant-depth fan-out and teleported gates. Check backend support and feed-forward latency first.

Verification: Operator(qc).equiv(target), which ignores global phase; cirq.testing.assert_allclose_up_to_global_phase; unitarity ||U^dagger U - I|| < 1e-10 for hand-built matrices; random-input-state fidelity tests above ~12 qubits. Record count_ops before and after.

Pitfalls: gates equal up to global phase stop being equal once controlled (XPowGate vs rx); un-uncomputed ancillas leave garbage entanglement that kills interference; gates counted before translation; SWAPs left in where a relabelling before measurement would do.

skills.name: qiskit-transpilation
skills.description: Qiskit 2.x transpiler workflow: preset pass managers and stages, Target and fake backends, layout and SABRE routing with seed sweeps, Heron fractional gates, AI routing passes, custom passes, layout-aware observables and equivalence checks. Load when compiling circuits to ISA form or minimising 2q count and depth after routing.
outline: Version gate first: print the qiskit, qiskit-aer and qiskit-ibm-runtime versions. Qiskit 2.x removed BackendV1, pulse, execute(), the V1 primitives and the V1 fake backends. Use qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider (FakeFez, FakeTorino, FakeMarrakesh) or GenericBackendV2(num_qubits, basis_gates, coupling_map, seed) offline. Confirm APIs via context7.

generate_preset_pass_manager(optimization_level, backend= or target=, seed_transpiler, layout_method, routing_method, approximation_degree). Stage table init -> layout -> routing -> translation -> optimization -> scheduling: level 0 does no optimisation; level 1 does light cancellation plus VF2PostLayout; level 2 adds commutation analysis; level 3 adds 2q block resynthesis.

Build a Target from data with Target.from_configuration(basis_gates, num_qubits, coupling_map), or InstructionProperties(error, duration) per qubit pair from published calibrations. Heavy-hex (Eagle/Heron) and square-lattice topologies give very different routing overhead.

Layout and routing: SabreLayout and SabreSwap are stochastic. Sweep 10-50 seed_transpiler values (or raise layout_trials/swap_trials) and keep the circuit with the fewest 2q gates, then the lowest error-weighted cost. VF2Layout finds perfect embeddings; VF2PostLayout remaps to the lowest-error qubits after routing.

Metrics script: tqc.count_ops(), tqc.num_nonlocal_gates(), 2q depth via tqc.depth(lambda i: i.operation.num_qubits == 2), and estimated success = product of (1 - error) from the Target. Always state backend, optimisation level and seed.

Layout bookkeeping: tqc.layout.initial_index_layout(), final_index_layout() and routing_permutation(). Map observables with SparsePauliOp.apply_layout(tqc.layout). Measured clbits keep logical order, so counts need no remap, but Statevector/Operator comparisons do (use Operator.from_circuit(tqc)).

Parameterised circuits: transpile once with Parameters and bind values in the primitive PUB. Never re-transpile inside an optimiser loop. Check that optimisation kept every parameter (compare qc.parameters with tqc.parameters).

Heron fractional gates: a backend fetched with use_fractional_gates=True exposes RZZ(theta) for 0 < theta <= pi/2 and RX(theta), which roughly halves 2q count for Trotter and QAOA layers. Check current docs for incompatibilities with dynamic circuits and some mitigation options.

Optional plugin passes: qiskit-ibm-transpiler AI routing and synthesis passes (local or service mode) and unitary-synthesis plugins. Adopt one only after it beats the preset baseline on the same seed set.

Custom passes: subclass TransformationPass or AnalysisPass, implement run(dag) on a DAGCircuit, and insert it through StagedPassManager hooks (pre_layout, post_routing, post_optimization). Share analysis results via property_set, and unit-test each pass with Operator equivalence.
Equivalence checks: Operator(qc).equiv(Operator.from_circuit(tqc)) up to ~12 qubits; mqt.qcec verify for larger circuits; random-state fidelity as a fallback.

Worked example: a 12-qubit GHZ chain on FakeFez at levels 1 and 3 with 20 seeds. Expect 11 CZ when VF2 finds a line; report 2q depth and the product of (1 - e). Pitfalls: barriers block optimisation; measure_all placed after transpile; comparing levels with a single seed; counting gates from a non-ISA circuit.

skills.name: qiskit-primitives-runtime
skills.description: Qiskit SamplerV2/EstimatorV2 and IBM Qiskit Runtime: PUB formats and broadcasting, local exact, Aer and fake-backend testing, execution modes, resilience/twirling/DD options, job management, addons and cost guards. Load when running circuits through primitives locally or on IBM hardware.
outline: PUB shapes: Sampler takes (circuit, parameter_values, shots); Estimator takes (circuit, observables, parameter_values, precision). Observables and parameter arrays broadcast like NumPy (shape (..., n_params)), so one PUB with a 2D sweep replaces hundreds of jobs.

Result access: res[i].data.<creg> is a BitArray with get_counts(), get_bitstrings(), get_int_counts() and slice_bits(). Estimator results give data.evs and data.stds in the broadcast shape; metadata holds shots and precision; precision is about 1/sqrt(shots).

Local tiers: StatevectorSampler/StatevectorEstimator are exact (set a seed; default_precision adds Gaussian noise). qiskit_aer.primitives SamplerV2/EstimatorV2 add noise models. Local testing mode passes a fake backend as mode= to the runtime primitives; it is the mandatory dry run before any QPU job.

Accounts and safety: QiskitRuntimeService with a saved account (channel ibm_quantum_platform or ibm_cloud, instance CRN). Tokens never go in code or the repo. A QPU submission needs the caller's approval of backend, shots and estimated QPU seconds.

Execution modes: job (single), Batch (independent jobs, overlapping classical work) and Session (iterative, dedicated access; not on the Open plan). Use max_execution_time as a cost cap. Batch suits sweeps, Session suits VQE loops.

ISA requirements: transpile with a backend-specific pass manager, then observables.apply_layout(isa.layout). Sampler circuits need measurements; Estimator circuits must not have any. Classical register names become data attributes ('meas' after measure_all).

Options map: default_shots and default_precision. resilience_level 0 is none, 1 adds TREX readout mitigation, 2 adds ZNE with gate twirling. Also twirling.enable_gates/enable_measure/num_randomizations; dynamical_decoupling.enable plus sequence_type ('XY4', 'XpXm'); resilience.zne_mitigation with zne.noise_factors, zne.extrapolator and zne.amplifier='pea'; pec_mitigation. Save the exact options with every result.
Job lifecycle: job.job_id(), service.job(id) to re-fetch, job.status(), usage metrics, cancel. Save job IDs, options and transpile seeds to out_dir so results reproduce without re-running.
Parameter binding order: qc.parameters is sorted by name (ParameterVector sorts by index), so pass arrays in that order. Test one known-answer point before sweeping.

Higher-level tools: qiskit-addon-sqd, -obp, -mpf and -cutting, and the Qiskit Functions catalog (IBM and partner circuit/application functions). Check plan availability and cost before proposing them.

Worked example: a 2-qubit RY-CNOT ansatz with one Estimator PUB of observables [[ZZ],[XX],[YY]] times 50 theta values gives evs of shape (3,50) in one job. Compare StatevectorEstimator, fake-backend local mode and resilience_level 1, each reported with sigma.

Pitfalls: V1 and V2 result access mixed; apply_layout forgotten, which silently measures the wrong physical qubits; precision confused with shots; max PUB size exceeded; resilience options assumed free (ZNE multiplies runtime by ~3-5x).

skills.name: pennylane-differentiable
skills.description: PennyLane differentiable quantum programming: device choice (default.qubit, lightning.*, default.mixed, default.tensor), diff methods (backprop, adjoint, parameter-shift, SPSA), JAX/Torch interfaces and Catalyst qjit, shot configuration, templates, the qchem and qaoa modules, gradient verification and specs. Load when building trainable QNodes or VQE/QAOA in PennyLane.
outline: Versions and breaking points: print qml.__version__. Shot configuration has moved (device shots= in older releases; qml.set_shots or QNode-level shots in newer ones), the TensorFlow interface was dropped, and plugins are pinned to the core version. Check via context7 before writing code.

Device table: default.qubit (reference, backprop), lightning.qubit (C++ CPU, adjoint), lightning.gpu and lightning.kokkos (GPU, threads), lightning.tensor and default.tensor (MPS/TN for wide shallow circuits), default.mixed (channels), default.clifford (stabilizer), and qiskit/braket plugins for hardware.

diff_method choice: backprop for simulators with many parameters (memory grows with layers); adjoint on lightning (exact, O(state) memory); parameter-shift for hardware and shots (2 evaluations per Pauli-generator parameter, a four-term rule for controlled rotations); spsa for many parameters under shots; finite-diff only for checks.

Interfaces: autograd (pennylane.numpy with requires_grad); JAX (jax.jit, optax optimisers, vmap over parameter batches); Torch (TorchLayer for hybrid models). Catalyst @qml.qjit compiles loops (for_loop, while_loop) and mid-circuit-measurement control flow.

Templates: StronglyEntanglingLayers, BasicEntanglerLayers, AllSinglesDoubles, UCCSD, Givens-style SingleExcitation/DoubleExcitation, AngleEmbedding and AmplitudeEmbedding (normalize/pad). Size weights with the shape helpers, e.g. StronglyEntanglingLayers.shape(n_layers, n_wires).

Measurements: expval, var, probs, sample, counts, state, density_matrix, classical_shadow and shadow_expval. Build Hamiltonians with operator arithmetic (qml.dot, qml.s_prod, qml.Hamiltonian) and group terms with qml.pauli.group_observables. Finite-shot expectation values always carry sigma.

VQE recipe: qml.qchem.Molecule -> molecular_hamiltonian(active_electrons, active_orbitals, mapping) -> hf_state -> excitations -> AllSinglesDoubles. Optimise with Adam, GradientDescent, QNGOptimizer (metric_tensor) or optax. Stop at |dE| < 1e-6 Ha on exact devices and compare with PySCF FCI.

QAOA recipe: qml.qaoa.maxcut(graph) returns (cost_h, mixer_h); stack qml.qaoa.cost_layer and mixer_layer with qml.layer. Sample bitstrings at the optimum, compute cut values classically, and report the approximation ratio against brute force (n <= 20) or the GW bound.

Gradient verification: compare qml.grad at 5 random points with central finite differences (h ~ 1e-4, exact device) to atol 1e-6. With shots, require agreement within 4 sigma. Check custom-gate recipes with qml.gradients.param_shift.

Resource inspection: qml.specs(qnode)(params) for gate counts, depth and parameter count; qml.draw and draw_mpl; transforms such as merge_rotations and cancel_inverses. Decompose to a native set before any cost claim. qml.from_qiskit and OpenQASM handle interop.

Worked example: H2/STO-3G at 0.7414 Angstrom, 4 qubits, a DoubleExcitation(theta) ansatz on HF |1100>, lightning.qubit with adjoint. It converges to the FCI energy -1.13728 Ha within 1e-6; rerun with 10k shots and parameter-shift and report E +/- sigma.
Pitfalls: wire 0 is the MSB; non-trainable inputs marked requires_grad; backprop on shot-based devices; QNodes rebuilt or re-jitted inside loops; Python control flow on traced values under jit.

skills.name: quantum-algorithm-primitives
skills.description: Textbook quantum algorithm building blocks with formulas, circuits and known-answer tests: QFT and approximate QFT, phase estimation (standard, iterative, Bayesian, Hadamard test), Grover and amplitude amplification, quantum counting, amplitude-estimation variants, and Shor order finding. Load when designing, implementing or debugging these algorithms.
outline: QFT: QFT|j> = N^{-1/2} sum_k e^{2 pi i jk/N} |k>, built from H plus a controlled-R_m ladder plus bit reversal: n(n+1)/2 rotations and floor(n/2) SWAPs. Approximate QFT drops R_m for m > log2 n + 2 (error O(n 2^{-m_max}), O(n log n) gates). Relabel instead of SWAP before measurement, and check the inverse-QFT sign convention against the SDK's QFT gate.

Phase estimation: t = n + ceil(log2(2 + 1/(2 delta))) ancillas give n bits with probability >= 1 - delta; the best t-bit estimate has probability >= 4/pi^2. The cost is the controlled-U^{2^k} powers, about 2^t tau of total evolution (Heisenberg 1/eps). A superposition input yields outcome i with probability |a_i|^2.

Low-ancilla variants: iterative (Kitaev) QPE with one ancilla, mid-circuit measurement and a feed-forward phase correction, reading bits LSB first. Bayesian, robust or statistical phase estimation for noisy early fault-tolerant hardware. Hadamard test for Re<psi|U|psi>, and with an S-dagger on the ancilla for Im.

Grover: a phase oracle O|x> = (-1)^{f(x)}|x> (MCZ with X sandwiches on the marked pattern) or a bit-flip oracle with a |-> ancilla (phase kickback). Diffuser = H^n (2|0><0| - I) H^n. With sin theta = sqrt(M/N), P = sin^2((2k+1) theta) and k_opt = floor(pi/(4 theta)); overshooting lowers success.

Unknown M: BBHT exponential search with random k (expected O(sqrt(N/M)) queries), quantum counting (QPE on the Grover iterate), or fixed-point amplitude amplification (Yoder-Low-Chuang) to avoid the souffle problem. BBBV gives the lower bound Omega(sqrt(N/M)).

Amplitude estimation: canonical QPE-based AE (depth ~1/eps), maximum-likelihood AE (Suzuki 2020, a schedule of k values) and iterative AE (Grinko 2021, with confidence intervals). Error O(1/k) against classical O(1/sqrt(k)); always state the cost of the loading operator A.

Shor: order finding by QPE on U_a|y> = |a y mod N>, then continued fractions (fractions.Fraction(s/2^t).limit_denominator(N)). It succeeds if r is even and a^{r/2} is not -1 mod N. Modular exponentiation (windowed arithmetic) dominates cost. Quote RSA-2048 estimates only with their assumptions (Gidney-Ekera 2019; Gidney 2025).

Oracle and arithmetic hygiene: compute-copy-uncompute (Bennett) for garbage-free oracles; the ancilla vs Toffoli trade-off; reversible adders (Cuccaro ripple-carry, Gidney's temporary-AND adder at about n Toffolis) and QROM lookups usually dominate the cost.

Crossover arithmetic: before recommending Grover or AE, find the N where sqrt(N) * t_oracle,quantum < N * t_classical, with logical clocks around a microsecond against 1e9-1e10 classical ops/s (Babbush et al. 2021, focus beyond quadratic speedups).

Known-answer tests: QPE on the T gate (phi = 1/8) with t = 3 returns 001 deterministically; QFT of |0...0> is uniform and QFT of |j> has linear phases; Bernstein-Vazirani returns s with probability 1; 3-qubit Grover with k = 2 gives 0.945; AE on an RY(2 theta) state recovers sin^2 theta.

Worked example: 3-qubit Grover with theta = 0.3614 and k = 2 gives P = 0.945 (k = 3 drops to 0.330). 10k shots give 0.945 +/- 0.0023. At least 24 CNOTs before routing bound fidelity near 0.995^24 = 0.89 at 0.5% 2q error; report ideal, noisy-sim and hardware numbers together.

Pitfalls: bit reversal forgotten; controlled-U^{2^k} built by repeating U 2^k times instead of evolving for 2^k tau; phase vs bit-flip oracle mismatch; dependence on qiskit-algorithms, now community-maintained (check its status before using it).

skills.name: variational-quantum-algorithms
skills.description: Variational algorithm design and trainability: VQE ansatz, optimiser and gradient choices, parameter-shift rules, barren-plateau diagnosis (global cost, depth, noise, Lie-algebra dimension) and the simulability tension, QAOA with QUBO/Ising mapping, warm starts and classical baselines. Load when proposing, debugging or reviewing VQE, QAOA or QML training.
outline: Loop anatomy and budget: ansatz U(theta)|ref>, E(theta) = sum c_j <P_j>, and a classical optimiser. Total shots = iterations x circuits per gradient (2 n_params for parameter shift) x shots per circuit. Compute this before running anything.

Ansatz table: UCCSD (chemistry, deep); k-UpCCGSD; ADAPT-VQE (gradient-selected growth from an operator pool, stop when the max gradient < 1e-3) and qubit-ADAPT; hardware-efficient (shallow, untrainable at scale); symmetry-preserving Givens circuits. Initialise from HF or MP2 amplitudes.

Optimiser table: L-BFGS-B/BFGS on exact simulators; COBYLA or Nelder-Mead for few parameters; SPSA under shot noise (alpha = 0.602, gamma = 0.101, calibrate a from the initial gradient size); Adam; quantum natural gradient and its metric-tensor cost. Stop on a statistically significant improvement, not a raw dE.

Gradient rules: two-term shift [f(theta + pi/2) - f(theta - pi/2)]/2 for generators with eigenvalues +/-1/2; a four-term rule for controlled rotations (eigenvalues 0, +/-1/2); generalised shift rules (Wierichs et al. 2022) for multi-frequency gates; stochastic shift for non-commuting generators. Check every rule against finite differences.

Barren-plateau diagnostics: sample 200 random theta and estimate Var[dC/dtheta_k] for n = 4..16; an exponential slope of log Var against n means a plateau. Causes: global cost observables, 2-design expressivity, noise (exponential in depth), entanglement, and a large dynamical Lie algebra (Var ~ 1/dim DLA, Ragone et al. 2024).

Simulability tension: provable absence of barren plateaus usually confines the dynamics to a small subspace that admits classical simulation (g-sim, Pauli propagation, tensor networks) (Cerezo et al.). Say so when claiming trainability, and run a classical-surrogate check.

Mitigations: local cost functions, layerwise or identity-block initialisation, warm starts from classical solutions, parameter transfer from smaller instances, problem-inspired ansatze. Record which were used.

QUBO/Ising mapping: x_i = (1 - z_i)/2 turns the objective into sum h_i Z_i + sum J_ij Z_i Z_j + const. Encode constraints as penalties A g(x)^2 with A > the maximum objective gain (check the argmin is feasible), or use constraint-preserving XY mixers (Hadfield 2019). Tools: qiskit-optimization QuadraticProgram.to_ising, docplex, dimod BQM.

QAOA specifics: |gamma, beta> = prod_l e^{-i beta_l B} e^{-i gamma_l C} |+>^n, with MaxCut C = sum (1 - Z_i Z_j)/2. p = 1 on 3-regular graphs gives ratio >= 0.6924. Initialise with INTERP or a linear ramp, exploit parameter concentration, use a CVaR objective (Barkoutsos 2020) for sampling. Each layer costs |E| RZZ after routing.

Benchmark protocol: same instances for every method; report approximation ratio and time-to-solution TTS = t_run ln(0.01)/ln(1 - p_success). QAOA baselines: Goemans-Williamson (0.878), Burer-Monteiro, simulated annealing (dwave-samplers), tabu, Gurobi/HiGHS/CP-SAT. VQE baselines: HF, CCSD(T), DMRG, FCI.

Worked example: MaxCut on a 10-node 3-regular graph with p = 1..3 QAOA on a statevector simulator: grid search at p = 1, then INTERP. Report the ratio against the brute-force optimum, the GW SDP (cvxpy) and SA, plus the shots needed to sample the best cut with 99% probability.

Pitfalls: optimising exact expectations and then claiming hardware results; weak baselines; over-parameterised hardware-efficient ansatze sold as 'expressive'; convergence criteria below the 1/sqrt(shots) noise floor; penalty weight too small (infeasible optimum) or too large (flat landscape).

skills.name: quantum-measurement-estimation
skills.description: Measurement statistics and estimator design for quantum experiments: shot budgets and standard errors, optimal shot allocation, commuting-group measurement, classical shadows, confidence intervals and bootstrap, and distribution comparison (TVD, Hellinger, heavy output, XEB). Load when choosing shots, estimating observables or judging whether a histogram matches theory.
outline:
Standard errors: an outcome probability has sqrt(p(1-p)/N) (worst case 0.5/sqrt(N)); a Pauli expectation has sqrt((1 -

^2)/N); H = sum c_j P_j measured in groups has sqrt(sum c_j^2 Var_j / N_j). Use Wilson intervals instead of the normal approximation for probabilities near 0 or 1.

Shot allocation: N_j proportional to |c_j| sigma_j, so total N = (sum |c_j| sigma_j)^2 / eps^2 <= lambda^2 / eps^2. Worked number: lambda = 10 Ha at eps = 1.6 mHa needs up to 3.9e7 shots per energy evaluation before grouping; the per-iteration optimiser budget follows from it.

Grouping: qubit-wise commuting groups (SparsePauliOp.group_commuting(qubit_wise=True), qml.pauli.group_observables) need only local rotations. General commuting groups need a Clifford diagonalisation circuit, trading extra 2q gates for fewer groups. Use the sorted-insertion heuristic, and include covariances inside a group in the variance.

Classical shadows: random Pauli or Clifford measurements, snapshot estimators, median-of-means. For M observables of locality k, N ~ O(3^k log(M/delta)/eps^2). Derandomised and locally biased variants exist; PennyLane has classical_shadow and shadow_expval. Shadows win for many low-weight observables and lose for few or high-weight ones.

Runtime-side helpers: Qiskit EstimatorV2 groups terms automatically and maps precision to shots (about 1/precision^2); Sampler BitArray has expectation helpers. Check in the metadata which grouping and shot count were actually used.

Derived quantities: propagate errors by the delta method or bootstrap (resample shots, recompute, at least 1000 resamples) for ratios, fidelities and mitigated values. A mitigated value never appears without its inflated sigma.

Comparing distributions: TVD = 1/2 sum |p - q|, Hellinger fidelity (qiskit.quantum_info.hellinger_fidelity), KL with smoothing. Build the finite-N null by simulating N-shot sampling from the ideal distribution 1000 times and compare with its 95th percentile. For a uniform distribution over K outcomes, E[TVD] is about sqrt(K/(2 pi N)).

Benchmark statistics: heavy-output probability (quantum-volume threshold 2/3 with a 97.5% one-sided CI) and linear XEB F = 2^n <p_ideal(x)> - 1 with sigma about 1/sqrt(N). Say when the ideal probabilities themselves need classical simulation.
Hypothesis tests: chi-square or G-test on counts with at least 5 expected per bin (merge bins); a 4 sigma rule for single probabilities; Bonferroni or Holm correction when scanning many settings.
Sparse outputs at many qubits: estimate marginals and correlators directly from bitstrings instead of full histograms, and process bit arrays memory-efficiently.

Worked example: a 6-qubit GHZ with 8192 shots. Estimate fidelity from populations plus parity-oscillation coherence, bootstrap the error, and report F +/- sigma and whether F > 0.5 (genuine multipartite entanglement) at 3 sigma.
Pitfalls: shot-noise fluctuations read as signal; the same shots reused for optimisation and reporting (optimistic bias); covariance inside groups ignored; TVD quoted without its null distribution.

skills.name: stabilizer-codes-surface-code
skills.description: Stabilizer and surface-code theory for practitioners: Pauli/symplectic representation, CSS construction and distance checks, a code catalogue (repetition to bivariate-bicycle qLDPC, color, bosonic), rotated surface-code layout and hook errors, thresholds by noise model, logical-error scaling and Lambda, lattice surgery and magic-state supply. Load when choosing, analysing or explaining QEC codes.
outline: Stabilizer basics: an abelian S inside the Pauli group with -I not in S and n - k generators; the code space has dimension 2^k. Logical operators are N(S) minus S, and the distance is the minimum logical weight. A syndrome bit records anticommutation with a generator. Degeneracy matters; Knill-Laflamme: P E_a^dagger E_b P = c_ab P.

Binary symplectic form: a Pauli maps to an (x|z) vector and commutation is the symplectic inner product. With check matrices H_X and H_Z, CSS codes come from classical codes with H_X H_Z^T = 0 mod 2, and k = n - rank H_X - rank H_Z. Compute over GF(2) with numpy or galois.

Distance computation: brute force for small n, integer or SAT search for medium codes, and circuit-level distance via stim shortest_graphlike_error / search_for_undetectable_logical_errors. Keep code distance and circuit (fault) distance apart.

Code catalogue with [[n,k,d]], check weight, connectivity and use: repetition, Shor [[9,1,3]], [[5,1,3]], Steane [[7,1,3]], rotated surface [[d^2,1,d]], color codes, the bivariate-bicycle gross code [[144,12,12]] (needs long-range couplers), hypergraph and lifted product codes, and cat/GKP bosonic codes in concatenation.

Rotated surface code layout: d^2 data plus d^2 - 1 measure qubits (2d^2 - 1 in total); X/Z plaquettes, with boundaries defining the logicals. The CNOT schedule (N/Z order) keeps hook errors from reducing the distance. Memory experiments use rounds = d.

Thresholds by noise model: code capacity ~10.3% (MWPM) and ~10.9% optimal; phenomenological ~2.9-3%; circuit-level depolarizing ~0.5-1%. SI1000-style models put more noise on measurement. Erasure-biased hardware has higher thresholds. Never quote code-capacity numbers for hardware.

Scaling: p_L(d) = A (p/p_th)^{(d+1)/2} with A ~ 0.1 and p_th ~ 0.01; Lambda = p_L(d)/p_L(d+2). Willow's 2024 memory had Lambda ~ 2.1 through d = 7 (~0.14% per round). The distance steps needed = log10(p_L,now / p_L,target) / log10(Lambda).

Logical operations: Pauli-frame tracking; lattice-surgery merges and splits that measure ZZ or XX over d rounds; transversal gates where the code allows them (color and Steane Cliffords); code deformation. Each logical operation takes about d rounds.

Magic states: 15-to-1 distillation (output error ~35 p^3), CCZ factories for arithmetic, and magic-state cultivation (Gidney-Shutty-Jones 2024) with a much smaller footprint. When T-count is large, footprint and production rate set the runtime.

Hardware realism: leakage (leakage-reduction units, reset), correlated bursts (cosmic rays), crosstalk, and real-time decoding latency. Qubit counts from memory experiments exclude routing and factories, which add 2-10x.

Worked example: Steane [[7,1,3]] built from Hamming(7,4). Verify H_X H_Z^T = 0 and k = 1, enumerate the weight-3 logicals, and tabulate single-X-error syndromes. Then the rotated d = 5 surface code: 49 qubits, corrects 2 errors.
Pitfalls: [[n,k,d]] confused with classical [n,k,d]; thresholds compared across decoders or noise models; 'below threshold' claimed from a single distance; measurement errors ignored (rounds < d).

skills.name: stim-qec-decoding
skills.description: Hands-on QEC simulation with Stim, Sinter and decoders (PyMatching, Fusion Blossom, BP-OSD, Chromobius, Tesseract): circuit language, detectors and observables, noise instructions, detector error models, threshold and Lambda sweeps with resume files, fits with confidence intervals, and circuit debugging. Load when logical error rates or thresholds must be produced numerically.
outline: Stim circuit language: R/RX, H, CX/CZ, M/MR/MX, TICK, QUBIT_COORDS, DETECTOR(coords) rec[-k], OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE(k), SHIFT_COORDS, REPEAT. Noise: DEPOLARIZE1/2, X_ERROR/Z_ERROR, PAULI_CHANNEL_1/2, HERALDED_ERASE. Generated circuits: stim.Circuit.generated('surface_code:rotated_memory_x|z', 'repetition_code:memory', 'color_code:memory_xyz', distance=, rounds=, noise arguments).

Noise models: uniform depolarizing through the generator arguments, or a custom SI1000 rewrite (2q gate p, 1q and idle p/10, measurement 5p, reset 2p) as a function that adds noise per layer. Keep measurement and reset errors in, and use rounds >= d.

Detector error model: circuit.detector_error_model(decompose_errors=True) for matching decoders. A non-deterministic detector or observable error points to a wrong stabilizer order; inspect with DEM and matchgraph diagrams.

Decoder table: pymatching for surface and repetition codes (Matching.from_detector_error_model, decode_batch); fusion_blossom for parallel MWPM; BP-OSD via stimbposd or ldpc for qLDPC; chromobius for color codes; tesseract (search-based) for qLDPC and color codes; correlated matching. Wrap new decoders as a sinter.Decoder subclass.

Sinter at scale: sinter.collect(num_workers, tasks, decoders, max_shots, max_errors, save_resume_filepath), or the CLI: sinter collect --circuits ... --decoders pymatching --max_shots 1e7 --max_errors 1000 --processes 16 --save_resume_filepath stats.csv --metadata_func auto. Collect 100-1000 logical errors per point.

Analysis: per-round rate via sinter.shot_error_rate_to_piece_error_rate(rate, pieces=rounds); binomial likelihood intervals via sinter.fit_binomial; plots via sinter.plot_error_rate or 'sinter plot --group_func ... --x_func ...'. The threshold is the crossing of the d curves; Lambda comes from a fit of log p_L against d.

Debugging: circuit.diagram('timeslice-svg' | 'detslice-svg' | 'matchgraph-svg'); shortest_graphlike_error() to confirm the circuit distance equals d; search_for_undetectable_logical_errors for hyperedge DEMs; compile_detector_sampler(seed) with manual decoding for spot checks.

Custom circuits (new layouts, qLDPC schedules): run with noise off and assert every detector is all-zero over 1k shots, then unit-test the logical observable with injected single errors before any sweep.

Experimental data: read hardware detection events with stim.read_shot_data_file (b8/01 formats), decode with DEMs reweighted from calibration (correlated matching), and compare with simulation at the fitted p.
Performance: parallelise with processes, precompute DEMs, avoid Python per-shot loops, cap max_shots for low-p points, and use count_detection_events for a quick sanity check.

Worked example: rotated memory_z with d in {3,5,7}, p in {0.001..0.01}, rounds = d, pymatching. The threshold crossing lands near 0.7-1%; Lambda at p = 0.001 is several (about p_th/p), within the intervals. Table every point with shots, errors and per-round p_L with its interval.

Pitfalls: decompose_errors missing (pymatching fails on hyperedges); per-shot and per-round rates mixed; too few errors at low p (only upper bounds are valid); observable in the wrong basis (memory_x vs Z errors); different round counts across distances.

skills.name: quantum-noise-mitigation
skills.description: Noise characterisation, noise-model building and error mitigation: Kraus channels and T1/T2 conversions, RB/interleaved RB/XEB/layer fidelity, Aer and Cirq noise models from calibrations, readout mitigation (M3, TREX), dynamical decoupling, Pauli twirling, ZNE, PEC/PEA, CDR and symmetry verification, with sampling-overhead accounting. Load when results come from noisy hardware or a noisy simulation.
outline: Channels and parameters: amplitude damping gamma = 1 - e^{-t/T1}; pure dephasing 1/T_phi = 1/T2 - 1/(2 T1), with T2 <= 2 T1; depolarizing; asymmetric readout confusion (1 -> 0 is usually worse); coherent over-rotation (infidelity grows quadratically); crosstalk; leakage. Check Kraus completeness sum K^dagger K = I.

Characterisation recipes: T1 decay, Ramsey T2*, Hahn-echo T2, readout assignment matrix, standard and interleaved RB (r = (d-1)(1-p)/d), XEB, and layer fidelity / EPLG for device-scale benchmarks. Use qiskit-experiments or the Cirq equivalents. F_avg = (d F_pro + 1)/(d + 1).

Noise-model construction: NoiseModel.from_backend(fake or snapshot backend), thermal_relaxation_error(t1, t2, gate_time), per-gate depolarizing_error from reported errors, ReadoutError; Cirq noise models likewise. Validate the model by reproducing measured RB or GHZ fidelities before trusting its predictions.
Success budget: product of (1 - e_gate) x readout fidelity x idle decay. 200 2q gates at 0.5% leave ~0.37. Below ~0.1, redesign the circuit before running it.

Suppression first: dynamical decoupling (XY4 or XpXm in idle windows, timed to the device), and Pauli twirling to turn coherent noise into stochastic noise (also a prerequisite for ZNE/PEC models). Twirl measurements too.

Readout mitigation: tensored or full confusion-matrix inversion (up to ~10 qubits), M3 (mthree, subspace-reduced, for many qubits), TREX (twirled readout; Estimator resilience_level 1). Calibrate on the same qubits in the same time window.

Zero-noise extrapolation: scale noise by unitary or gate folding (Mitiq fold_gates_at_random, fold_global) or pulse stretching / PEA, with scale factors such as {1, 3, 5}. Fit Richardson, linear and exponential extrapolators and report all of them, because ZNE is biased; variance grows with scale and with extrapolation order.

Probabilistic error cancellation: learn a sparse Pauli-Lindblad model per layer, then sample quasi-probabilities with overhead gamma_tot^2 (gamma_tot = product of gamma_i, about e^{2 lambda_total}). It is unbiased if the model is accurate and feasible while gamma^2 stays below ~1e2-1e3. PEA uses the same learned model to amplify noise for ZNE.

Other methods: Clifford data regression (train on near-Clifford circuits), symmetry verification and post-selection on particle number or parity, virtual distillation, Mitiq REM/DDD modules, and vendor tensor-network mitigation functions where available.
Tooling: Mitiq (execute_with_zne, execute_with_pec, cdr), Qiskit Runtime resilience options, mthree. Executors return expectation values with shot counts recorded.

Worked example: an 8-qubit 1D Ising Trotter circuit under the FakeFez noise model. Compare raw, readout-mitigated and ZNE (linear vs exponential, scales 1/3/5) estimates of <Z_4> with the exact value, showing bias reduction and sigma inflation, repeated over 5 seeds.

Reporting rules: raw and mitigated values side by side with shots, sigma, overhead factor and model assumptions. Mitigation does not scale (its sampling cost is exponential); never present it as error correction.

skills.name: quantum-resource-estimation
skills.description: Fault-tolerant resource estimation: logical-level costing (logical qubits, T/Toffoli counts, rotation synthesis), error-budget split, code distance and factory sizing, physical qubits and runtime, reaction-time limits, tools (Azure QRE via qsharp, Qualtran, PennyLane, pyLIQTR, bartiq) and reporting with sensitivity tables. Load when asked how many qubits or how much time an algorithm needs.
outline: Logical costing: count logical qubits Q (including arithmetic ancillas, QROM and block-encoding registers), Toffoli/T count, rotation count and logical depth. A Toffoli costs about 4 T with temporary AND, 7 T exactly. Arithmetic and data loading usually dominate.

Rotation synthesis: eps per rotation = eps_synth / N_rot, at about 3 log2(1/eps) T each with gridsynth, less with mixing. With many rotations, consider phase-gradient-register additions (Toffoli-based) instead.
Error-budget split: eps_total = eps_logical + eps_distillation + eps_synthesis; default to thirds and state the split. Target total failure is usually 1e-2 to 1e-3.

Code distance: the smallest d with (Q_patches x D_steps x d) x A (p/p_th)^{(d+1)/2} <= eps_logical. Patch size 2d^2 - 1; routing adds 1.5-2x patches. qLDPC memory is a lower-overhead layout with harder logic.

Factories: 15-to-1 (output 35 p^3, with its size and time per output), multi-level for low targets, CCZ factories, cultivation. Number of factories = required T rate / factory rate; add their footprint to physical qubits.

Runtime = max(D_steps x d x t_cycle, N_T / T-rate, reaction limit), where the reaction limit = sequential non-Clifford depth x (decode + feed-forward latency). t_cycle is ~1 us superconducting vs ~ms for ions and neutral atoms, which moves answers by 1000x.

Tools: the Azure Quantum Resource Estimator via qsharp (qsharp.estimate on Q# or Qiskit circuits; qubitParams such as qubit_gate_ns_e3/e4 or qubit_maj_ns_e4, qecScheme surface_code or floquet_code, errorBudget, Pareto frontier); Qualtran bloqs (call graphs, QECGatesCost, QubitCount, surface-code cost models); PennyLane resource estimation; pyLIQTR; bartiq symbolic. Check APIs with context7.

Cross-checks: hand estimate and tool should agree within ~2x; otherwise find the differing assumption (factory design, routing, synthesis). Compare with published anchors via paper-researcher: RSA-2048 at ~20M qubits / 8 h (Gidney-Ekera 2019) and <1M qubits / <1 week (Gidney 2025); FeMoco THC (Lee et al. 2021).
Sensitivity table: vary p in {1e-3, 5e-4, 1e-4}, t_cycle in {1 us, 10 us, 1 ms} and eps_total. Show physical qubits and runtime per cell and highlight the dominant term.

Worked example: Q = 100 (200 patches), D_steps = 1e8, p = 1e-3, eps = 0.01. d = 23 fails (2.3e-11 against a 5e-12 bound) and d = 25 passes, giving 1249 qubits per patch and ~2.5e5 physical qubits plus factories. Runtime is 1e8 x 25 x 1 us, about 42 min, if factories sustain 4e4 T/s. Report '~3e5 physical qubits, ~1 h at p = 1e-3'.

Reporting template: an assumptions table (p, t_cycle, code, decoder latency, factory, eps split, tool and version); outputs as ranges, not point values; omissions listed (leakage, correlated errors, I/O); each claim labelled Proven, Evidence or Conjecture.

Pitfalls: T counted but Toffoli-ladder ancillas missed; QROM and data-loading cost ignored; all T gates assumed parallel beyond factory capacity; physical counts taken from memory experiments; per-round and per-operation logical error rates mixed.

skills.name: quantum-chemistry-mapping
skills.description: Electronic-structure Hamiltonians for quantum algorithms: PySCF integrals, active-space selection, second quantisation, Jordan-Wigner, Bravyi-Kitaev, parity and ternary-tree mappings, symmetry tapering, Hamiltonian norms and factorisations (DF/THC), classical reference energies, and NISQ (VQE, SQD) vs fault-tolerant (qubitised QPE) routes. Load when turning a molecule or lattice model into qubit operators.
outline: Pipeline: geometry (Angstrom vs Bohr) + basis + charge/spin -> PySCF RHF/ROHF -> optional CASSCF or natural orbitals -> active space -> integrals h_pq and h_pqrs (chemist vs physicist index order) plus the nuclear-repulsion and frozen-core constants -> fermionic H -> qubit H.

Active-space selection: frozen core, AVAS-style projections, natural-orbital occupation thresholds (e.g. 0.02 < n < 1.98), CASSCF. Record (n_electrons, n_orbitals); qubits = 2 x active spatial orbitals.

Mapping table: Jordan-Wigner (weight O(n), simple, local in 1D); Bravyi-Kitaev (O(log n)); parity (enables 2-qubit tapering); ternary tree (optimal O(log_3 n) weight); fermionic swap networks for linear-depth simulation. Spin-orbital order differs (OpenFermion interleaved alpha-beta vs blocked in Qiskit Nature), and a mismatch gives wrong energies.

Symmetries and tapering: particle number, S_z and Z2 point-group symmetries remove qubits (Bravyi et al. 2017). Choose the sector containing the HF state. H2/STO-3G goes from 4 qubits to 1 with parity mapping plus tapering.

Tooling: PySCF; OpenFermion with openfermionpyscf; qiskit-nature (community-maintained, check its status); PennyLane qml.qchem molecular_hamiltonian (active_electrons, active_orbitals, mapping); block2 for DMRG references; ffsim for fast fermionic simulation.

Norms and factorisations: Pauli LCU lambda = sum |c_j|. Single/double factorisation and THC reduce lambda and the Toffoli cost of block encodings. Compute lambda for each representation, since fault-tolerant runtime scales as lambda/eps.

Reference energies: HF, MP2, CCSD(T), FCI (up to ~18 orbitals), DMRG or SHCI for strong correlation. Chemical accuracy is 1.6 mHa (1 kcal/mol) against FCI in the same basis and active space, not against experiment.

NISQ routes: VQE with UCCSD/ADAPT (shot cost from quantum-measurement-estimation); sample-based quantum diagonalisation (qiskit-addon-sqd: sample configurations on hardware, recover configurations, diagonalise the subspace classically); quantum Krylov. Report subspace dimension and classical cost honestly.
Fault-tolerant route: qubitised QPE with DF/THC block encodings, needing about pi lambda/(2 eps) walk steps; PREPARE/QROM Toffolis dominate. Hand lambda, n and eps to quantum-resource-estimation.
Lattice models: Fermi-Hubbard (t, U) with JW on snake ordering; Givens-rotation preparation of Slater determinants; Heisenberg and Ising directly as spin models.

Worked example: H2/STO-3G at 0.7414 Angstrom has HF -1.1168 Ha and FCI -1.1373 Ha; JW gives 4 qubits and 15 Pauli terms including identity; compute lambda; taper to 1 qubit. Check that exact diagonalisation of the qubit H matches PySCF FCI to 1e-8, constant included.

Pitfalls: nuclear-repulsion or core-energy constant dropped; Bohr/Angstrom mix-up; wrong spin multiplicity; FCI compared in a different basis; chemical accuracy claimed against experiment; an active space too small to matter.

skills.name: quantum-circuit-simulators
skills.description: Choosing, running and validating quantum circuit simulators: memory math; statevector, density-matrix, trajectory, stabilizer, extended-stabilizer, MPS, tensor-network and Pauli-propagation backends across Aer, qsim, Lightning, CUDA-Q, quimb and Stim; GPU and precision settings, convergence checks and a validation checklist. Load when picking a simulator, scaling a simulation, or proving a simulator result is right.
outline: Memory math: statevector 16 x 2^n B in complex128 (8 x 2^n in complex64), so 30 qubits = 16 GiB and 34 = 256 GiB. Density matrix 16 x 4^n (15 qubits = 16 GiB). Allow 2x workspace. MPS is O(n chi^2); a stabilizer tableau is O(n^2) bits.

Decision table: exact up to ~30-34 qubits: statevector (Aer, qsim, lightning, CUDA-Q nvidia). Channels up to ~15: density matrix. Larger noisy: trajectories. Clifford/QEC: Stim. Few T gates: extended stabilizer or stabilizer rank. Low entanglement at 50-1000 qubits: MPS. Shallow and wide: TN contraction (cuTensorNet, quimb with cotengra). Local expectations of deeper circuits: Pauli propagation / operator backpropagation.

Aer specifics: AerSimulator(method=..., device='GPU', precision='single' or 'double', fusion_enable, max_parallel_threads, blocking_qubits for multi-GPU). Shot branching handles dynamic circuits. save_statevector and save_expectation_value avoid sampling when exact values are wanted.

Other engines: qsimcirq for Cirq (big-endian results, PhasedXZ native gates, stimcirq for Clifford), PennyLane lightning.* (adjoint gradients), CUDA-Q (@cudaq.kernel typed subset; set_target nvidia fp32/fp64, mgpu, mqpu with observe_async batching, tensornet/tensornet-mps; mpirun to scale), quimb with cotengra, Qrack, Stim; one primary engine plus one cross-check engine.

MPS/TN convergence: sweep chi (32, 64, 128, 256) and require the observable to change by less than the tolerance. Track discarded weight and truncation error; entanglement-entropy growth predicts blow-up. Estimate contraction cost with cotengra before running.
Precision: fp32 adds roughly 1e-7 relative error per gate, so check fp32 against fp64 at small n and assert ||psi|| = 1 at the end.

Validation checklist: endianness probe (X on qubit 0 of 3 gives index 1 in Qiskit, 4 in Cirq/PennyLane); known answers (Bell, GHZ, QFT of a basis state, Grover sin^2((2k+1) theta)); unitarity ||U^dagger U - I|| < 1e-10; Operator equivalence after compilation (MQT QCEC beyond ~12 qubits); cross-simulator TVD < 1e-9 for exact results; sampled TVD inside the null distribution; noise sanity (p -> 0 gives ideal, maximal p gives uniform).
Regression testing: fix simulator and transpiler seeds, store golden amplitudes or probabilities for small circuits, write pytest tolerances (atol 1e-8 exact, 4 sigma sampled), and run small n in CI.

Performance hygiene: compile once and bind parameters; batch circuits in one call; no per-shot Python loops; use expectation-value instructions instead of sampling when exact values suffice; profile scaling with n to find the wall.
Benchmark reporting: wall time vs n, hardware (CPU model and threads, GPU, memory), library versions and precision, and at least one alternative engine for comparison.

Worked example: a 28-qubit random brickwork circuit at depth 10 on Aer statevector, CPU vs GPU and fp32 vs fp64 (time and inter-run fidelity). Then a 60-qubit 1D depth-20 Trotter circuit with an MPS chi sweep showing <Z_30> converging.

Pitfalls: density matrix chosen where trajectories suffice; MPS results reported without chi convergence; states compared without handling global phase; default seeds differing between engines; memory silently spilling into swap.

skills.name: hamiltonian-simulation-methods
skills.description: Hamiltonian simulation methods and their costs: Pauli-exponential circuits, Trotter-Suzuki orders with commutator bounds and empirical error measurement, qDRIFT, randomized and multi-product formulas, LCU block encodings, qubitization and QSP/QSVT, plus SDK implementations (PauliEvolutionGate, TrotterProduct, CUDA-Q exp_pauli). Load when implementing or costing time evolution, or when choosing a simulation method.
outline: Setup: H = sum_{j=1..L} c_j P_j, lambda = sum |c_j|, target ||U - e^{-iHt}|| <= eps. Write down the lattice geometry and the term grouping (even/odd bonds, X/Y/Z colours), because grouping into commuting layers sets both the Trotter constants and the depth.

Product formulas: S1; Strang S2; Suzuki recursion S_{2k} with p_k = 1/(4 - 4^{1/(2k-1)}). Error is O(alpha_comm t^{p+1}/r^p) with nested-commutator norms (Childs-Su-Tran-Wiebe-Zhu 2021). For 1D nearest-neighbour models the commutator terms scale with n, not n^2.

Empirical error: compute exact e^{-iHt} (scipy expm_multiply on sparse H up to ~20-24 qubits) and the Trotter-circuit statevector. Measure state or operator error against r, fit the slope p, and extrapolate the r that meets eps. Bounds are often 10-1000x loose.

Randomised and extrapolated methods: qDRIFT needs N = O(2 lambda^2 t^2 / eps) samples, independent of L. Also random term ordering, partially randomised hybrids, and multi-product formulas (classical combination of Trotter results; qiskit-addon-mpf) that cancel error orders.

Circuit costs: exp(-i theta P/2) via basis change plus a CNOT ladder of 2(w - 1) CNOTs. Jordan-Wigner strings have weight O(n), Bravyi-Kitaev O(log n); fermionic swap networks help. On Heron, fractional RZZ(theta) gates serve Ising-type layers. A 1D nearest-neighbour Trotter step has 2q depth 2 (even/odd layers).

LCU and block encoding: H = sum alpha_j U_j; PREPARE|0> = sum sqrt(alpha_j/lambda)|j>; SELECT = sum |j><j| x U_j; <0|PREP^dagger SELECT PREP|0> = H/lambda. Unary-iteration SELECT costs about L Toffolis; QROM loads the PREPARE coefficients.

Qubitization and QSP/QSVT: the walk operator has eigenphases arccos(E_k/lambda), and query complexity is O(lambda t + log(1/eps)). Get phase angles from pyqsp, QSPPACK or qml.poly_to_angles. QPE on the walk needs about pi lambda/(2 eps) steps for energy precision eps. Validate small cases with qml.Qubitization, PrepSelPrep and QSVT.

Method choice: small early-FT or NISQ circuits -> 2nd-order Trotter; many terms with moderate lambda -> qDRIFT or hybrids; long-time, high-precision fault-tolerant work -> qubitization; chemistry -> DF/THC block encodings; open systems -> Lindblad dilations or stochastic unravellings (route to physics-expert).

SDK implementations: Qiskit PauliEvolutionGate(op, time, synthesis=LieTrotter, SuzukiTrotter(order, reps) or QDrift); PennyLane qml.TrotterProduct(H, time, n, order) and qml.evolve; CUDA-Q kernels with exp_pauli. Check each synthesiser's term ordering.

Observables and baselines: correlators, magnetisation against time, Loschmidt echoes. Compare with exact results at small n and MPS/TEBD for large 1D systems; utility-scale claims must face tensor-network and Pauli-propagation simulation.

Worked example: transverse-field Ising, n = 12, J = h = 1, t = 5. Find r empirically for eps = 1e-3 with S1, S2 and S4. A first-order step costs (n - 1) RZZ = 2(n - 1) CNOTs plus n RX. Pick the order with the lowest total 2q count (usually S2) and validate <Z_6(t)> against exact evolution.

Pitfalls: worst-case bounds used to size circuits; term-ordering effects ignored; forgetting that controlled evolution for QPE roughly doubles cost; tau units mixed (hbar = 1, energy units); pre-routing gate counts used for hardware estimates.

skills.name: pbr-microfacet-brdf
skills.description: GGX/Trowbridge-Reitz microfacet BRDF/BSDF implementation: D, height-correlated Smith G2, Schlick vs exact Fresnel, glTF/OpenPBR parameter mapping, multiple-scattering energy compensation, rough dielectric transmission, layered lobes and their unit tests. Load when writing, porting or debugging a physically based material.
outline: Conventions block moved from hub sections 1-2 and brdf-and-sampling.md sections 1-2: shading frame n=(0,0,1), v/l/h, mu=cos theta, solid-angle pdfs, the alpha = roughness^2 remap pinned per asset format. The three BRDF invariants each become a unit test: non-negativity, reciprocity (|f(a,b)-f(b,a)| < 1e-5 relative), and directional albedo <= 1.

Formula sheet: Lambert rho/pi; isotropic and anisotropic D; Lambda, G1, height-correlated G2 vs separable G1*G1; f_spec = D G2 F / (4 n.l n.v); the Filament-style visibility term V; Schlick F using v.h, not n.v; exact dielectric Fresnel with total internal reflection; conductor Fresnel from complex IOR or the Gulbrandsen 2014 reflectivity/edge-tint mapping.

Parameter-mapping table: glTF metallic-roughness (F0 = mix(0.04, baseColor, metallic), diffuse = baseColor*(1-metallic)) plus the KHR_materials_{ior, specular, transmission, volume, clearcoat, sheen, iridescence, anisotropy, dispersion} extensions; Disney principled; OpenPBR Surface 1.x layers (coat, fuzz, thin-film) in a MaterialX 1.39 node graph; Unreal and Unity conventions.

Sampling code: VNDF via spherical caps (Dupuy-Benyoub 2023, equivalent to Heitz 2018), pdf G1(v)D(h)/(4 n.v), weight F*G2/G1(v); the classic D(h)(n.h)/(4|v.h|) Jacobian; lobe selection by estimated albedo, then the full mixture pdf sum_k P(k) pdf_k for MIS.

Energy compensation: a script (NumPy or compute shader) that builds the 32x32 E_ss(mu, alpha) LUT; Turquin 2019 scale 1 + F0(1-E_ss)/E_ss; Kulla-Conty 2017 f_ms with F_avg/E_avg; the E_ss regression table (alpha 0.1/0.5/0.81/1.0 x mu 0.1/0.5/1.0) as golden values.

Rough dielectric transmission (Walter 2007): generalized half-vector, the f_t formula, Jacobian dw_h/dw_o, (eta_t/eta_i)^2 radiance scaling at interfaces vs importance transport, thin-walled vs volumetric modes.

Real-time specifics: specular antialiasing (Kaplanyan 2016 / Tokuyoshi normal-variance roughness widening, Toksvig for mipped normal maps), horizon/micro-shadowing for normal maps, half-precision limits (65504, denormals in D at low alpha); split-sum IBL is in realtime-global-illumination.

Pitfalls: roughness used directly as alpha; NaN from 1/(n.v) at grazing angles (clamp 1e-4); back-facing shading normals (Chiang 2019 terminator fix); metallic applied twice to diffuse; F0 or baseColor left in sRGB; specular lobe evaluated without the cosine in the weight.

Test harness: a NumPy furnace integration via VNDF (1e5 samples), a reciprocity fuzz over random direction pairs, and a chi-square test of sample() vs pdf() at mu in {0.05, 0.5, 1} and alpha in {0.05, 0.3, 1} with a Bonferroni threshold. Reuse Mitsuba 3 ChiSquareTest or the PBRT-v4 tests.

Worked example (moved from hub section 12, step 1): a roughness-0.9 metal renders too dark. The furnace gives 0.42 at mu=1 and 0.54 at mu=0.5. The E_ss LUT compensation restores 0.99-1.0, with before/after numbers reported in the output contract.

skills.name: importance-sampling-mis-restir
skills.description: Monte Carlo sampling for rendering: estimator variance, measure conversions, light sampling (area, spherical triangle/rectangle, env-map CDFs), MIS heuristics, low-discrepancy and blue-noise sequences, many-light selection (alias tables, light BVH) and RIS/ReSTIR DI/GI/PT with unbiased reuse. Load when noise, fireflies or bias trace back to how samples and weights are chosen.
outline: Estimator core: F_N = (1/N) sum f/p, unbiased iff p > 0 wherever f != 0, stderr sigma/sqrt(N). Efficiency = 1/(variance x time) is the comparison metric. Measure conversions: p_w = p_A d^2/|cos theta_l|; env-map pdf p_uv/(2 pi^2 sin theta). Delta lights and specular lobes get MIS weight 1.

Light-sampling table moved from brdf-and-sampling.md section 5: point/spot, sun and sphere cones (cos theta_max = sqrt(1-(r/d)^2)), area-uniform vs spherical-triangle triangles (Arvo 1995), spherical rectangles (Urena 2013). Includes code to build an env-map marginal/conditional CDF with sin theta weighting and its pdf.

MIS: balance vs power heuristic (beta=2), one-sample MIS, defensive/mixture sampling, and the two-strategy contribution formula. Both weights must include the light-selection probability in the same measure. Regression test: BSDF-only, light-only and MIS renders must share one mean.

Sample sequences and dimension budgeting: Owen-scrambled Sobol (Burley 2020 hash), scrambled Halton, spatiotemporal blue noise (STBN 2022) for 1-4 spp. A fixed per-bounce dimension map (light select 1, light 2, lobe 1, BSDF 2, roulette 1), power-of-two sample counts, per-pixel seeds.

Many-light selection: a power-proportional alias table (Vose, O(1)), a light BVH/tree with orientation cones (Conty-Kulla 2018), and lightcuts. The selection probability is folded into the pdf used for MIS.

RIS in GRIS notation (Talbot 2005, Lin et al. 2022): w_i = m_i p_hat(x_i)/p(x_i), select y proportional to w_i, contribution weight W = (1/p_hat(y)) sum w_i. Choosing the target p_hat: unshadowed f*Le*G, with visibility tested only for the survivor.

ReSTIR DI (Bitterli 2020): reservoir struct {y, w_sum, M, W} and streaming update code; temporal reuse with motion-vector validation and an M-cap of ~20x; spatial reuse over 3-5 neighbours gated by depth/normal similarity; visibility reuse. Bias sources (1/Z normalisation vs pairwise or generalized-balance MIS) and the RTXDI SDK as the production path.

ReSTIR GI (Ouyang 2021) and ReSTIR PT (Lin 2022): the sample is a reconnection vertex or path suffix. Shift mappings (random replay, reconnection, hybrid) and the reconnection Jacobian (|cos theta_2|/|cos theta_1|) * (d_1^2/d_2^2). Recognising correlation artifacts (boiling) and how they interact with denoisers.

Diagnostics: a chi-square harness and a pointwise sample-vs-pdf check (relative error < 1e-4), per-pixel variance images, equal-time relMSE/FLIP comparisons across strategies, and a log-log convergence plot to expose bias.

Pitfalls: mixing area and solid-angle pdfs; omitting the light-selection probability from the MIS weight; one random dimension serving two decisions; zero-pdf divisions; temporal reservoirs reused across disocclusions or lighting changes (lag, energy loss); uncapped M.

Worked example: 10k emissive triangles at 1 spp. Compare uniform selection, a power alias table, and ReSTIR DI (32 candidates + temporal + spatial) at equal milliseconds with a relMSE table and variance images.

skills.name: path-tracer-implementation
skills.description: Building a correct, then fast, unidirectional path tracer on CPU or GPU: camera and film, an integrator loop with NEE and MIS, Russian roulette, robust ray spawning, megakernel vs wavefront on hardware RT, progressive accumulation, and the furnace/convergence/reference validation suite. Load when writing or fixing an offline or interactive path tracer.
outline: Architecture decision table: CPU (Embree 4 + TBB/ISPC); GPU compute with your own BVH; hardware RT (Vulkan ray query or RT pipeline, DXR 1.1/1.2, OptiX 9, Metal RT); megakernel vs wavefront (Laine 2013) vs inline ray queries; when shader execution reordering pays (DXR 1.2 MaybeReorderThread, VK_NV_ray_tracing_invocation_reorder).

Camera and film: pinhole and thin-lens ray generation; pixel filters (box vs Gaussian/Blackman-Harris splatting); float32 linear HDR film; AOVs (albedo, normal, depth, motion) for denoisers; deterministic per-pixel and per-frame RNG seeding.

Integrator skeleton moved from brdf-and-sampling.md section 6: NEE + power-heuristic MIS, emissive-hit weights with prevSpecular flags, env-map miss MIS, throughput beta update, max depth, and Russian roulette after bounce 3-5 with q = min(1, max beta) and a floor near 0.05.

Robust intersection and spawning: Wachter-Binder offset along the geometric normal (no global epsilon), watertight ray-triangle test (Woop 2013), shading vs geometric normal sidedness, alpha-tested any-hit and opacity micromaps.

Materials and media hooks: the BSDF eval/sample/pdf contract (sample and pdf must agree), two-sided handling, nested dielectric priorities, homogeneous and heterogeneous media with delta/ratio tracking (Novak 2014) and Henyey-Greenstein phase sampling.

Spectral vs RGB: hero-wavelength sampling (Wilkie 2014) and RGB-to-spectrum uplifting (Jakob-Hanika 2019) when dispersion, fluorescence-free accuracy or metamerism matters; otherwise linear Rec.709 or ACEScg RGB.

Validation suite moved from hub section 3: white furnace converges to exactly 1; two independent seeds give a zero-mean difference image; log-log error slope is -0.5; relMSE/FLIP vs PBRT-v4 or Mitsuba 3 at 4k-64k spp; Cornell-box reference; NaN/Inf counters per pass.

Firefly and bias triage order: sample/pdf mismatch, then missing MIS, then caustic paths, then a roulette q that is too low, then shading-normal artifacts. Radiance clamping is a documented last resort and never used in references.

Performance: rays/s and samples/s per named GPU; wavefront path regeneration with stream compaction; material/hit sorting; BVH node-visit heatmaps; progressive accumulation that resets on camera or scene change; tile sizes for CPU.

Worked example (hub section 12, steps 2-3): fireflies around a small area light trace to pdf_bsdf missing the 1/(4|v.h|) Jacobian. The chi-square test fails at p < 1e-6; after the fix, relMSE vs Mitsuba 3 at 256 spp drops from 0.11 to 0.004 and the slope is -0.49.

skills.name: bvh-build-traversal
skills.description: Bounding volume hierarchies for ray tracing and spatial queries: binned SAH and SBVH builds, LBVH/PLOC GPU builds, wide and compressed BVHs, stack traversal with robust slab tests, refit vs rebuild, and hardware TLAS/BLAS management with compaction. Load when building, tuning or debugging a BVH or acceleration structure.
outline: SAH cost model C = C_trav + (A_L/A) N_L C_isect + (A_R/A) N_R C_isect with a leaf-termination rule. Quality metrics to report: SAH cost, end-point overlap, average nodes and triangles tested per ray, and a node-visit heatmap.

Builder decision table moved from hub section 4: binned SAH (16-32 bins) for static CPU scenes, SBVH spatial splits for long thin triangles, LBVH with 30-bit Morton codes (Karras 2012) and PLOC/H-PLOC (HPG 2024) for per-frame GPU builds. Use Embree 4 or tinybvh instead of hand-rolled production code.

Binned SAH build code: centroid bounds, bin index k = floor(B (c - min)/(max - min)) clamped, prefix/suffix area sweeps, in-place partition, 32-byte node layout (aabb + leftFirst/count), iterative build stack, triangle index indirection.

Traversal code: precomputed inverse direction with +/-inf handling (avoid 0*inf NaN), robust slab test t_max*(1 + 2*gamma(3)) (Ize 2013), nearer-child-first ordering, shrinking t_max, any-hit early-out for shadow rays, short-stack/stackless GPU variants.
Wide BVHs: collapsing a binary tree to BVH4/BVH8, SIMD box tests, compressed wide BVH (Ylitie 2017 CWBVH, 8-bit quantized child boxes) for incoherent GPU traversal.
Dynamic scenes: O(n) bottom-up refit; rebuild when SAH cost grows more than ~30%; two-level TLAS over BLAS instances with object-space ray transforms; per-frame budgets for rebuilds.

Hardware RT: VK_KHR_acceleration_structure / DXR build flags (PREFER_FAST_TRACE vs PREFER_FAST_BUILD, ALLOW_UPDATE, ALLOW_COMPACTION), compacted-size query + copy, scratch sizing and reuse, instance masks and SBT offsets, OPAQUE geometry flags vs any-hit, opacity micromaps for foliage, inspection in the Nsight/RGP RT viewers.
Non-rendering uses: broad-phase collision, closest-point and nearest-neighbour queries, picking. A BVH vs k-d tree vs uniform grid vs octree selection table.

Pitfalls: degenerate or zero-area triangles; a wrong primitive-index indirection in leaves; float precision in huge worlds (camera-relative coordinates); forgetting to rebuild or update the TLAS after instance edits; refit quality decay under large deformation.
Worked example: a 2M-triangle scene built with median split vs binned SAH vs SBVH. Report build ms, SAH cost, and Mrays/s for primary and diffuse rays, plus node-visit heatmaps, on a stated CPU/GPU.

skills.name: raster-pipeline-architecture
skills.description: Real-time raster renderer architecture: forward, forward+/tiled and clustered light culling, deferred G-buffer layouts, visibility buffer, depth prepass, reversed-Z infinite projection, render graphs with transient aliasing, GPU-driven meshlet culling, and transparency. Load when designing, extending or debugging a raster frame.
outline: Architecture decision table expanded from hub section 5: forward / forward+ / clustered / deferred / visibility buffer, judged on light count, material count, MSAA, transparency, bandwidth, and desktop vs mobile tile-based (TBDR) GPUs.

Reversed-Z with an infinite far plane for [0,1] depth: the projection matrix, D32_SFLOAT, GREATER test, clear to 0. A precision comparison vs standard Z with D24, and the clip-space conventions per API (Vulkan y-down, GL [-1,1]).

Tiled and clustered light culling: 16x16 tiles with min/max depth; 16x9x24 clusters with exponential slices slice = floor(log z * S/log(f/n) - S log n/log(f/n)); sphere and cone vs AABB tests; compute-built light index lists; a light-count heatmap debug view.

G-buffer layout worked in bytes per pixel: albedo RGBA8_SRGB, octahedral normal RG16 or RGB10A2 (encode/decode code), roughness/metal/AO RGBA8, motion RG16F, depth D32F; bandwidth estimates at 1080p and 4K.

Visibility buffer: 32-bit triangle+instance IDs, material classification and tile binning, analytic barycentrics and derivatives for texture LOD, and when it beats deferred (dense meshlets, many materials).
Render graph: per-pass read/write declarations, automatic barriers and layout transitions, transient resource aliasing, pass culling, and async-compute placement.

GPU-driven rendering: meshlets (meshoptimizer, 64 vertices/124 triangles), frustum + normal-cone + two-phase HiZ occlusion culling, indirect draws or mesh/task shaders, bindless materials, LOD by screen-space error.

Transparency: a sorted forward pass after opaque, weighted blended OIT (McGuire-Bavoil 2013) weight functions, per-pixel linked-list costs, premultiplied alpha, and low-res particles with bilateral upsampling.
Depth-prepass rules (only when overdraw is high); mobile TBDR specifics: load/store ops, subpasses or dynamic-rendering local read, keeping the G-buffer on-tile.

Pitfalls: z-fighting from standard Z; light culling with the wrong depth convention; un-renormalized G-buffer normals; derivatives in the visibility-buffer resolve; MSAA in deferred; missing motion vectors for skinned or animated objects.

Worked example: 1,000 point lights at 1440p. Measure forward vs clustered forward+ vs deferred and tabulate per-pass GPU timestamps, bytes per pixel and light-heatmap captures on a stated GPU before recommending one.

skills.name: realtime-shadows
skills.description: Real-time shadows: cascaded shadow maps (split schemes, stabilization, bias), PCF/PCSS soft shadows, VSM/EVSM/MSM filtering, point/spot shadow atlases, virtual shadow maps, contact shadows, and ray-traced shadows with denoising. Load when fixing shadow acne, peter-panning, shimmering or light leaks, or when shadows cost too much.
outline: Technique decision table: single map (spot); CSM (directional); cube/tetrahedral maps or atlas (point); virtual shadow maps (huge worlds, dense geometry); ray-traced shadows (area lights, hardware RT); screen-space contact shadows as an add-on.

CSM setup: the practical split scheme C_i = lambda*n(f/n)^(i/N) + (1-lambda)(n + (f-n) i/N) with lambda 0.5-0.9 and 3-4 cascades; bounding-sphere fit plus texel snapping for stability; cascade blend bands; pancaking casters behind the near plane.

Bias toolkit: constant + slope-scaled depth bias (vkCmdSetDepthBias, D3D12 rasterizer state), normal-offset bias scaled to world-space texel size, receiver-plane depth bias. Diagnosing acne vs peter-panning from captures.
Filtering: a hardware comparison-sampler PCF (bilinear 2x2); Poisson or rotated-disk PCF with blue noise; PCSS blocker search and penumbra w = (d_r - d_b) w_light / d_b, with tap-count control.

Pre-filterable maps: VSM Chebyshev bound p_max = sigma^2/(sigma^2 + (t - mu)^2) with light-bleeding reduction; EVSM warp exponents (~40 fp32, ~5.5 fp16); moment shadow maps; blurring and mipping; where each leaks.
Point and spot lights: cube maps with per-face caster culling; atlas allocation by screen-space size; caching static casters; per-frame update budgets.
Virtual shadow maps: a 16k^2 virtual map with 128^2 pages, page marking from the depth buffer, invalidation and caching, and the cost model.
Ray-traced shadows: one ray per pixel to a blue-noise point on the area light; alpha via any-hit or opacity micromaps; denoise with NRD SIGMA or SVGF; hybrid fallback to CSM beyond the RT distance.
Contact shadows: a short screen-space depth-buffer ray march (8-16 steps) for small-scale occlusion, with thickness heuristics.
Debug views and pitfalls: cascade color overlay; texel-density view; shimmering from unsnapped cascades; reversed-Z in shadow passes; D16 precision limits; a frustum that misses off-screen casters.

Worked example: an outdoor scene with shimmering and acne. Add texel snapping, a 1-2 texel normal-offset bias and a cascade blend band, then verify with a camera-strafe frame sequence and a flicker metric.

skills.name: realtime-global-illumination
skills.description: Real-time indirect lighting: GTAO/RTAO, screen-space reflections, irradiance and reflection probes with SH and split-sum prefiltering, DDGI probe volumes, surface-cache and radiance-cascade approaches, and ReSTIR GI with radiance caching, plus leak and lag control. Load when choosing, implementing or debugging GI, AO or reflections in a real-time renderer.
outline: Decision table by platform and budget: baked lightmaps + probes; GTAO + SSR; DDGI; surface cache + screen probes (Lumen-style); radiance cascades; RT GI with ReSTIR GI + denoiser + radiance cache; voxel cone tracing as legacy.

Ambient occlusion: GTAO (Jimenez 2016) horizon search with cosine weighting and bent normals, half resolution with bilateral upsampling, a multi-bounce AO approximation, RTAO with short rays, specular occlusion.
Screen-space reflections: hierarchical-Z tracing, roughness-driven ray jitter via GGX VNDF with a spatiotemporal resolve, a fallback chain SSR -> reflection probe -> sky, and edge/back-face fading.

Image-based lighting: split-sum (Karis 2013) prefiltered environment mips by roughness plus a 2D BRDF LUT (F0*A + B); importance-sampled prefiltering with pdf-based mip selection; parallax-corrected box probes and probe blending.
SH irradiance: L2 projection (9 coefficients per channel), irradiance with Ramamoorthi-Hanrahan A0=pi, A1=2pi/3, A2=pi/4, ringing windowing, volume storage and trilinear interpolation.

DDGI (Majercik 2019): probe grid, 128-256 rays/probe/frame, octahedral irradiance 6x6 (+1 border) and distance 14x14 (+1 border) texels, Chebyshev visibility weight, hysteresis ~0.97, probe relocation/classification, normal and view bias against leaks.
Surface cache and radiance cascades: card/surface caching with screen-space probe placement; radiance cascades (Sannikov 2023) with interval doubling for 2D and 3D; memory and latency trade-offs.
RT GI: a 1-spp first bounce with ReSTIR GI reservoirs, ReLAX/ReBLUR denoising, and multi-bounce via radiance caches (SHaRC, neural radiance cache in RTXGI 2.x).

Pitfalls: light leaking through thin walls; lag and ghosting under moving lights from hysteresis; double-counting energy between AO and GI or between probes and SSR; missing specular occlusion; sky-visibility errors indoors.

Worked example: an indoor DDGI scene leaks at wall corners. Enable distance-based visibility, add normal/view bias of ~0.3x probe spacing, relocate stuck probes, then measure with a closed-room furnace-style test and per-pass timings.

skills.name: vulkan-setup-synchronization
skills.description: Vulkan 1.3/1.4 bring-up and correctness: instance/device/queue selection with vk-bootstrap and volk, VMA memory, swapchain and frames in flight, dynamic rendering, synchronization2 barrier recipes, timeline semaphores, bindless descriptors and push descriptors, and the validation and sync-validation workflow. Load when writing Vulkan host code or fixing validation errors, flicker or device-lost.
outline: Bring-up checklist: Vulkan SDK 1.4.x, volk loader, vk-bootstrap instance/device builders, the features chain (Vulkan13Features dynamicRendering/synchronization2; Vulkan12Features timelineSemaphore/bufferDeviceAddress/descriptorIndexing), debug-utils messenger, object names for every handle; verify signatures with context7 (Vulkan-Hpp, ash, vulkano).
Memory: VMA with VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO plus HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE/RANDOM flags, staging uploads vs ReBAR/host-visible device memory, persistent mapping, aliasing, budget queries.

Swapchain: surface-format choice (B8G8R8A8_SRGB, or UNORM with manual encode; HDR10 A2B10G10R10 + ST2084), present-mode table (FIFO always available, MAILBOX, IMMEDIATE), recreation on OUT_OF_DATE/SUBOPTIMAL, a render-finished semaphore per swapchain image (fixes semaphore-reuse VUIDs), swapchain_maintenance1 present fences.

Frames in flight (from gpu-api-map.md section 3): N = 2-3 per-frame command pools, uniform ring segments and descriptor pools, a fence or timeline value per frame, a deferred-deletion queue keyed by timeline value.

Barrier recipe table moved from gpu-api-map.md section 2: RT->sampled, depth->sampled, upload->sample, compute->compute, compute->indirect, compute->vertex, before-present, write-after-read. VkImageMemoryBarrier2 + vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 code; layout transitions count as writes; UNDEFINED discards contents; queue-family release/acquire; VK_KHR_unified_image_layouts where supported.
Timeline semaphores for CPU-GPU and cross-queue (async compute) sync with vkQueueSubmit2, wait/signal values and vkWaitSemaphores; when binary semaphores are still required (swapchain).

Descriptors in 2026: bindless via descriptor indexing (UPDATE_AFTER_BIND, PARTIALLY_BOUND, runtime arrays); VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer; push descriptors (core in 1.4); buffer device address + push constants; pipeline-layout compatibility rules; std140 vs std430 vs scalar layouts.

Pipelines: dynamic rendering and dynamic state, a pipeline cache persisted to disk, shader objects vs graphics pipeline libraries, the shader toolchain (glslc, DXC -spirv, slangc) with spirv-val on every output.

Validation workflow: VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation via vkconfig or VK_EXT_layer_settings; synchronization validation; GPU-assisted validation and Debug Printf; best-practices checks; device-lost triage with VK_EXT_device_fault and Nsight Aftermath.

Pitfalls: the acquire semaphore not waited at COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT; one fence for all frames; writing mapped buffers the GPU still reads; Vulkan NDC y-down and [0,1] depth; using features that were never enabled; a full-pipeline barrier used as a 'fix'.

Worked example: flicker only on AMD. Sync validation reports WRITE_AFTER_READ on a storage image between two compute passes; fix it with one precise sync2 barrier, then confirm clean validation and a stable 500-frame capture diff.

skills.name: webgpu-wgsl
skills.description: WebGPU and WGSL in browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) and natively (wgpu, Dawn): adapter limits and features, WGSL alignment rules, bind-group design, render and compute pipelines, uniformity analysis, canvas and HDR configuration, error scopes, timestamp queries, and GLSL/HLSL ports. Load for any WebGPU, WGSL, wgpu or three.js WebGPURenderer task.
outline: Platform matrix: Chrome/Edge (since 113), Firefox (Windows since 141, other platforms rolling out), Safari 26; native wgpu (Rust, breaking releases, so pin the version and query context7) and Dawn (C++); three.js WebGPURenderer + TSL, Babylon.js; feature detection via navigator.gpu and adapter.features.

Device setup: requestAdapter(powerPreference); requestDevice with requiredFeatures (shader-f16, timestamp-query, subgroups, float32-filterable, bgra8unorm-storage) and requiredLimits. Default-limits table: 4 bind groups, 64 KiB uniform binding, 128 MiB storage binding, 256 invocations/workgroup, 16 KiB workgroup storage, 256-byte dynamic-offset alignment.

WGSL memory layout: vec3<f32> has align 16 and size 12; uniform-address-space arrays need a 16-byte stride; struct alignment rules. A worked offset table for a camera/light struct and host packing helpers (webgpu-utils, wgsl_reflect, encase/bytemuck in Rust).

Bind-group strategy: group 0 per frame, 1 per pass, 2 per material, 3 per draw with dynamic offsets. Explicit bind-group layouts vs layout:'auto' pitfalls; no bindless in core, so use texture arrays or atlases.
Uniformity analysis: textureSample, dpdx/fwidth and workgroupBarrier require uniform control flow. Fixes: textureSampleLevel/Grad, hoisting samples out of branches, workgroupUniformLoad.

Compute: workgroup sizes 64/256, storage buffers vs storage textures (format limits, no -srgb storage), atomics, the subgroups feature, indirect dispatch, readback via mapAsync staging buffers with frame latency.
Canvas and color: getPreferredCanvasFormat (usually bgra8unorm), viewFormats for -srgb views, alphaMode 'premultiplied', HDR via rgba16float + toneMapping {mode:'extended'}, colorSpace 'display-p3'.

Errors and profiling: a label on every object, pushErrorScope/popErrorScope, the uncapturederror listener, device.lost recovery, getCompilationInfo surfaced in tests, timestampWrites (quantized), chrome://gpu, Safari Web Inspector.

Tooling and porting: the naga CLI for validation and WGSL<->SPIR-V/MSL/HLSL/GLSL translation, Tint, the wgsl-analyzer LSP. GLSL differences: no implicit conversions, separate textures and samplers, framebuffer y-down, [0,1] depth.

Pitfalls: writeBuffer sizes not a multiple of 4; a texture used as attachment and binding in one pass; depth32float not filterable (use textureLoad or a comparison sampler); bytesPerRow 256-byte alignment in copies; synchronous pipeline creation stalls (use createRenderPipelineAsync).

Worked example: port a GLSL separable Gaussian-blur compute shader to WGSL. Fix struct padding, add a workgroup-shared tile with workgroupBarrier, validate with naga, and compare to a CPU reference within 1e-3 in a headless test.

skills.name: metal-apple-gpu
skills.description: Metal 3 and Metal 4 on Apple silicon: device, queue and command setup (MTL4 command allocators, argument tables, residency sets), TBDR-aware render passes (load/store actions, memoryless targets, tile shaders, programmable blending), argument buffers and bindless, MSL specifics, MetalFX, shader validation and Xcode capture. Load when writing, porting or profiling Metal or metal-cpp code.
outline: Version and feature gate. Metal 3 (macOS 13+/iOS 16+): mesh shaders, MetalFX upscaling, fast resource loading. Metal 4 (OS 26 releases, Apple M1/A14 and later): MTL4CommandQueue, MTL4CommandBuffer + MTL4CommandAllocator, MTL4ArgumentTable, MTL4Compiler, explicit barriers, tensors in shaders, MetalFX frame interpolation and denoised upscaling. Check supportsFamily before choosing MTL4 types.
